docs.title: Household #8: Hodges, R L
docs.text:
Household #8: Hodges, R L¶

Back to the 1900 Census & Household Index

In the 1900 Barney census, R. L. Hodges headed a 10-person household. The table below preserves the exact names, relationships, ages, birthplaces, and occupations recorded for the household.

Household Snapshot¶

R. L. Hodges was listed in 1900 as a 64-year-old Georgia-born farmer. His household belongs to the farm economy around Barney, where land, crops, livestock, kin labor, and seasonal work still shaped daily life alongside the newer railroad town.

The 1900 household combined the older Hodges couple, three unmarried adult Hodges children, and the Culbreth son-in-law, daughter, and grandchildren. The page is a two-generation household record, with the Culbreth family already tied into the Hodges line through Effie V. Hodges Culbreth.

Every listed person in the household was reported as born in Georgia. Later records are still needed before claiming movement into or out of Barney for any individual member.

Newspaper and Public-Record Trail¶

  • The Valdosta Times reported on 1 December 1900 that R. L. Hodges died suddenly during cane-stripping work on Tuesday, 27 November 1900. The item says he complained of being tired, rested on a fence, fell a few minutes later, and was found dead. That article supplies the contemporary newspaper context for the death date preserved in the family narrative below.
  • A 2 January 1909 Valdosta Daily Times social note says Miss Hattie Hodges had returned to her home at Barney after visiting Miss Vesta Chambers in Valdosta. This is probably the Harriett Hodges listed in this 1900 household, but the notice itself gives only the shortened name and Barney residence, so it should remain a likely identification rather than a closed proof.

1900 Census Household¶

Name Relation Age Birthplace Occupation
R. L. Hodges Head 64 Georgia Farmer
Mary J. Hodges Wife 62 Georgia —
John H. Hodges Son 29 Georgia Farm Laborer
Harriett Hodges Daughter 26 Georgia —
Joseph E. Hodges Son 22 Georgia Farm Laborer
J. B. Culbreth Son-in-law 33 Georgia Saw Mill Laborer
E. V. Culbreth Daughter 30 Georgia —
James Culbreth Grandson 7 Georgia —
Carrodine Culbreth Grandson 5 Georgia —
Bessie Culbreth Granddaughter 1 Georgia —

Children and Later Trails¶

This section is reserved for later-life child evidence. No later spouse, death, burial, obituary, probate, separate household, or descendant-line identification has been added here yet from direct records.

Family Narrative¶

  • Head: R.L. Hodges (age 64, Georgia, USA, Farmer) — b. Jan 1836, GA
  • Spouse: Mary J. (Stephens) Hodges (Wife, age 62, Georgia, USA) — b. ~1838, GA; m. Jan 22, 1861
  • Children:
  • John H. Hodges (Son, age 29) — b. ~1871, GA, Farm Laborer
  • Harriett Hodges (Daughter, age 26) — b. ~1874, GA
  • Joseph Hodges (Son, age 22) — b. ~1878, GA, Farm Laborer
  • J.B. Culbreth (Son in law, age 33) — b. ~1867, GA, Saw Mill Laborer
  • E.V. Culbreth (Daughter, age 30) — b. ~1870, GA; Effie V. Hodges; married Joseph B. Culbreth
  • James Culbreth (Grandson, age 7) — b. ~1893, GA, born Barney
  • Carrodine Culbreth (Grandson, age 5) — b. ~1895, GA, born Barney; name from Ancestry tree (Art Stewart)
  • Bessie Culbreth (Granddaughter, age 1) — b. ~1899, GA, born Barney

Verified Identity: Robinson L. (Robert) Hodges

Full genealogy confirmed via Huxford's History of Brooks County (pp. 484–485) and Find A Grave (Memorial 111611356):

  • Father: James Carr Hodges (b. Mar 18, 1800, Bulloch Co., GA — d. Jan 17, 1865, Brooks Co., GA); buried Hodges Cemetery, Brooks Co. (Find A Grave 106716862); Indian War veteran (Capt. Levi J. Knight's independent company, 1838); Captain of Militia, 659th district, commissioned Apr 22, 1844; lived on lot 552, 13th district, Brooks Co.
  • Mother: Sarah Ann Newton (b. Jun 3, 1802 — d. Sep 18, 1893); daughter of George Newton; buried Hodges Cemetery (Find A Grave 106716833)
  • Wife: Mary J. Stephens (m. Jan 22, 1861)

Parents' Birthplace: 1880 census records both father's and mother's birthplace as North Carolina.

Siblings: 1. James Lafayette "Fate" Hodges (b. 1829 — d. 1890) — moved to Florida 2. Sarah Adeline Hodges (b. 1832) — m. William Alfred Robeson; d. 1883 3. Joseph Jackson Hodges (b. Jan 15, 1836 — d. Jul 26, 1910) — prominent farmer, 3,000 acres, owned store/sawmill/gristmill/cotton gins; buried Hodges Cemetery (Find A Grave 106717207); m. Rachel Caroline Delk (Nov 11, 1866); 11 children 4. Mary C. Hodges (b. 1838 — d. 1926) — m. Tobias G. Robinson, May 28, 1857; buried Hodges Cemetery 5. Margaret Hodges (b. 1840) — m. J. Cobb 6. Martha A. "Mattie" Hodges (b. 1842 — d. 1924) — m. Berrien Beaty; buried Hodges Cemetery

Grandfather: Joseph Hodges (b. 1758) — married (1) Elenor Denmark; (2) Sarah Carr

Great-grandfather: Joshua Hodges (b. Oct 13, 1736, NC — d. Mar 13, 1809, Bulloch Co., GA) — Revolutionary War soldier; enlisted from Martin Co., NC under Capt. Kenneth McKenzie, 1780; granted land in Burke Co., GA for service; married Ann Raiford, 1756

Death: November 27, 1900, Brooks County, Georgia. A 1 December 1900 Valdosta Times item reports that he died suddenly during cane-stripping work after the 1900 census enumeration.

Burial: Camp Ground Cemetery, Mount Zion Church, Morven, Brooks County, Georgia (Find A Grave 111611356). Note: Huxford references Hodges Cemetery, but FindAGrave confirms burial at Camp Ground.

Civic Roles: - Founding trustee, Barney Methodist Church (1899) — listed among early Barney settler families in Huxford

Notable Relatives: Brother Joseph J. Hodges was among the wealthiest farmers in northern Brooks County (Okapilco–Tallokas section); started with \$300 capital, accumulated 3,000 acres plus store, sawmill, gristmill, and cotton gins; stockholder in banks at Pavo and Quitman.

Culbreth Family: J.B. Culbreth (Joseph B. Culbreth, b. ~1867, Savannah, Chatham Co., GA) married Effie V. Hodges, daughter of R.L. and Mary J. Hodges. J.B. worked as a saw mill laborer in Barney. The Culbreth family was not established in Brooks County — no references in Huxford; left Barney District by 1910 (no Culbreth surname in 1910 census for Barney). Joseph B. Culbreth's parents are unknown (Ancestry tree says "Unknown"). The family likely came to Barney for saw mill work.

Effie V Hodges note: An unsourced Ancestry tree (Art Stewart's Ancestors 2025) links Effie to "Redding Othaniel Augustus Hodges Jr." (1837-1904, Sandersville, Washington Co., GA). This is incorrect — Redding Jr.'s family is entirely Washington County and unrelated to Brooks County. R.L. Hodges is Effie's actual father per the 1900 census (which lists her as "Daughter" in his household). The Ancestry tree likely conflated two different Effie Hodges from different branches.

1850 Census (Lowndes County, GA): Robertson Hodges, age 14, in household of James C Hodges (50) and Sarah A Hodges (47). Siblings: Lafayette (21), Adeline (18), Joseph J (15), Mary (12), Margaret (10), Martha (7). Robertson was attending school.

1860 Census (Brooks County, GA): Robinson L Hodges, age 24, farmer, still in father J.C. Hodges' household at Tallokas PO. Not yet married.

1860 Census — Wife's Family (Brooks County, GA): Mary J Stevens, age 18, in household of Cadar Stevens (53) and Levina Stevens (46). Siblings: Florida G, Richard C (16), Harriet A (14), Francis (6), Andrew (4), George F.

Marriage Certificate: Robinson Hodges married Mary J. Stephens on 22 January 1861 in Brooks County, Georgia. Confirmed by two independent sources (Ancestry 7839/92013 and Ancestry 4766/182273). Note: some sources incorrectly state 1864.

1870 Census (Brooks County, GA): Robinson Hodges, age 34, farm laborer, Quitman PO. Household: Mary (30, wife), Thomas (8, son), Sarah (4, daughter), Mary (3, daughter).

1880 Census (Morven, Brooks County, GA): R.L. Hodges, age 44, farmer. Mary J. Hodges (41, wife). Children in household: Thomas J. (16), Sarah L. (14), Mary A. (12), James H. (10), Margarette E. (8), Harriet A. (6), Emma F. (4), Joseph E. (2), plus unnamed infant (~1880). Father's birthplace: North Carolina. Mother's birthplace: North Carolina.

1900 Census: R.L. Hodges (64, head, b. Jan 1836 GA), Mary J. (62, wife), John H (29, son), Harriett (26, daughter), Joseph E (22, son). R.L. was alive at enumeration (June 1, 1900) and died five months later.

1910 Census (Barney, Brooks County, GA): Mary J. Hodges, age 71, widowed, remained at Barney with daughters Maggie Cribb and Hattie Hodges, son-in-law John Cribb, and two Cribb granddaughters. A same-name LaGrange entry should not replace this household continuity.

Early-family evidence: Huxford's compiled genealogy places James Carr Hodges under Joseph Hodges and identifies Joseph and Nathaniel Hodges as sons of Joshua Hodges and Ann Raiford. That makes Nathan Hodges a collateral relative of this Barney branch, not Robinson's direct ancestor. The upper genealogy is secondary-supported because no inspected parent-naming original verifies the Joshua-to-Joseph-and-Nathaniel generation. James Carr to Robinson remains strong probable from the 1850 and 1860 household chain plus Huxford's explicit son statement.

Connections to Other Barney Families¶

  • The page documents a direct Hodges-Culbreth connection inside HH#8: Effie V. Hodges, daughter of R. L. and Mary J. Hodges, was married to J. B. Culbreth, and their children James, Carrodine, and Bessie Culbreth were listed as Hodges grandchildren in the same household.
  • No separate Culbreth household has been identified elsewhere in the 1900 Barney census list on the current page evidence.
  • J. B. Culbreth may be related to Prof. B. H. Culbreth, the Barney school figure identified in 1901-1902 newspaper items, but proof of that relationship has not been found at this time.

docs.title: Household Snapshot
docs.text:
R. L. Hodges was listed in 1900 as a 64-year-old Georgia-born farmer. His household belongs to the farm economy around Barney, where land, crops, livestock, kin labor, and seasonal work still shaped daily life alongside the newer railroad town.

The 1900 household combined the older Hodges couple, three unmarried adult Hodges children, and the Culbreth son-in-law, daughter, and grandchildren. The page is a two-generation household record, with the Culbreth family already tied into the Hodges line through Effie V. Hodges Culbreth.

Every listed person in the household was reported as born in Georgia. Later records are still needed before claiming movement into or out of Barney for any individual member.

docs.title: Newspaper and Public-Record Trail
docs.text:
• The Valdosta Times reported on 1 December 1900 that R. L. Hodges died suddenly during cane-stripping work on Tuesday, 27 November 1900. The item says he complained of being tired, rested on a fence, fell a few minutes later, and was found dead. That article supplies the contemporary newspaper context for the death date preserved in the family narrative below.
  • A 2 January 1909 Valdosta Daily Times social note says Miss Hattie Hodges had returned to her home at Barney after visiting Miss Vesta Chambers in Valdosta. This is probably the Harriett Hodges listed in this 1900 household, but the notice itself gives only the shortened name and Barney residence, so it should remain a likely identification rather than a closed proof.

Verified Identity: Robinson L. (Robert) Hodges

Jul 26, 1910) — prominent farmer, 3,000 acres, owned store/sawmill/gristmill/cotton gins; buried Hodges Cemetery (Find A Grave 106717207); m. Rachel Caroline Delk (Nov 11, 1866); 11 children 4. Berrien Beaty; buried Hodges Cemetery

Grandfather: Joseph Hodges (b. 1758) — married (1) Elenor Denmark; (2) Sarah Carr

Great-grandfather: Joshua Hodges (b. Oct 13, 1736, NC — d. Mar 13, 1809, Bulloch Co., GA) — Revolutionary War soldier; enlisted from Martin Co., NC under Capt. Kenneth McKenzie, 1780; granted land in Burke Co., GA for service; married Ann Raiford, 1756

Death: November 27, 1900, Brooks County, Georgia. A 1 December 1900 Valdosta Times item reports that he died suddenly during cane-stripping work after the 1900 census enumeration.

Burial: Camp Ground Cemetery, Mount Zion Church, Morven, Brooks County, Georgia (Find A Grave 111611356). Note: Huxford references Hodges Cemetery, but FindAGrave confirms burial at Camp Ground.

Civic Roles: - Founding trustee, Barney Methodist Church (1899) — listed among early Barney settler families in Huxford

Notable Relatives: Brother Joseph J. Hodges was among the wealthiest farmers in northern Brooks County (Okapilco–Tallokas section); started with $300 capital, accumulated 3,000 acres plus store, sawmill, gristmill, and cotton gins; stockholder in banks at Pavo and Quitman.

Culbreth Family: J.B. Culbreth (Joseph B. Culbreth, b. ~1867, Savannah, Chatham Co., GA) married Effie V. Hodges, daughter of R.L. and Mary J. Hodges. J.B. worked as a saw mill laborer in Barney. The Culbreth family was not established in Brooks County — no references in Huxford; left Barney District by 1910 (no Culbreth surname in 1910 census for Barney). Joseph B. Culbreth's parents are unknown (Ancestry tree says "Unknown"). The family likely came to Barney for saw mill work.

Effie V Hodges note: An unsourced Ancestry tree (Art Stewart's Ancestors 2025) links Effie to "Redding Othaniel Augustus Hodges Jr." (1837-1904, Sandersville, Washington Co., GA). This is incorrect — Redding Jr.'s family is entirely Washington County and unrelated to Brooks County. R.L. Hodges is Effie's actual father per the 1900 census (which lists her as "Daughter" in his household). The Ancestry tree likely conflated two different Effie Hodges from different branches.

1850 Census (Lowndes County, GA): Robertson Hodges, age 14, in household of James C Hodges (50) and Sarah A Hodges (47). Siblings: Lafayette (21), Adeline (18), Joseph J (15), Mary (12), Margaret (10), Martha (7). Robertson was attending school.

1860 Census (Brooks County, GA): Robinson L Hodges, age 24, farmer, still in father J.C. Hodges' household at Tallokas PO. Not yet married.

1860 Census — Wife's Family (Brooks County, GA): Mary J Stevens, age 18, in household of Cadar Stevens (53) and Levina Stevens (46). Siblings: Florida G, Richard C (16), Harriet A (14), Francis (6), Andrew (4), George F.

Marriage Certificate: Robinson Hodges married Mary J. Stephens on 22 January 1861 in Brooks County, Georgia. Confirmed by two independent sources (Ancestry 7839/92013 and Ancestry 4766/182273). Note: some sources incorrectly state 1864.

1870 Census (Brooks County, GA): Robinson Hodges, age 34, farm laborer, Quitman PO. Household: Mary (30, wife), Thomas (8, son), Sarah (4, daughter), Mary (3, daughter).

1880 Census (Morven, Brooks County, GA): R.L. Hodges, age 44, farmer. Mary J. Hodges (41, wife). Children in household: Thomas J. (16), Sarah L. (14), Mary A. (12), James H. (10), Margarette E. (8), Harriet A. (6), Emma F. (4), Joseph E. (2), plus unnamed infant (~1880). Father's birthplace: North Carolina. Mother's birthplace: North Carolina.

1900 Census: R.L. Hodges (64, head, b. Jan 1836 GA), Mary J. (62, wife), John H (29, son), Harriett (26, daughter), Joseph E (22, son). R.L. was alive at enumeration (June 1, 1900) and died five months later.

1910 Census (LaGrange, Troup County, GA): Mary J. Hodges, age 71, widowed, living alone on Ware Street. Father's birthplace: North Carolina. Mother's birthplace: Georgia. After R.L.'s death in 1900, Mary moved from Brooks County to LaGrange.

• Head: Ceily, Cecly, Celia, or Ciley Davis, age 58 in 1900, born Apr 1842 in Georgia, widowed, farmer, and owner of her farm.

  • Earlier family household: The 1880 Quitman District household of Richard Davis and Celia Davis with children Warren, Charlotte J., Martha E., and John W. remains the core earlier census anchor.
  • 1900 household structure: Ceily Davis appears in Barney with daughter Jane Leonard and Leonard grandchildren. That is still the best supported reading of the intergenerational household.
  • Later child-forward lead: The 1910 Andrew J. Lennon / Lottie J. Lennon household remains the strongest candidate continuation for daughter Charlotte Jane Davis, but the Leonard/Lennon bridge should still be treated as likely rather than closed.
  • Property significance: Ceily was one of the documented Black property-owning heads in Barney in 1900, an important economic marker in the precinct.
  • Boundary on parentage: The Lightsey surname is directly supported by the marriage record, but claims that Ceily was a daughter of Primus Lightsey and Sylvia Capers-or-Davis remain unproven within this entry.

docs.title: Connections to Other Barney Families
docs.text: Ceily Davis is tied to the Barney Lightsey network through the 1872 Brooks County marriage record naming her as Ciley or Celey Lightsey when she married Richard Davis. Other Barney households currently discussed as part of the broader Lightsey cluster include William Betts (HH#10), through Ella Betts and Charley Lightsey; Thomas Lightsey (HH#12); Phillip Lightsey (HH#104); Jasper Lightsey (HH#126); and Henry S. Lightsey (HH#165). The connection should remain cautious: Ceily's Lightsey surname is directly supported, but her exact parentage and the precise relationship path to those other Lightsey households have not yet been proved within this entry.

Pace. That chain fits the 1900 birth-month report and later Thomas County records.
  • Correction to earlier draft: The earlier parentage claim tying this William to Ensil/Eusil Pace and Georgia Goolsby is not supported by the childhood census evidence and should not be repeated here.
  • Marriage to Emma Gornto: The draft cites a FamilySearch marriage record for William H. Pace and Emma Gornto on 29 Mar 1891 in Brooks County. The original image could not be reopened in this pass, but the 1900 and 1910 census records independently support a marriage beginning about 1891.
  • 1910 correction: William and Emma were still together in 1910 with children Reid, James F., Pearl, and Willie. The earlier claim that William had already remarried Loula in 1910 is incorrect for HH#11.
  • Later family trail: By 1920 Emma had remarried Frank M. Smith, while William had later married Ella Mae Duncan. William's later Thomas County trail is supported by the 1920-1950 censuses, probate material, and his 1953 obituary. Pearl Pace Owens's 1966 North Carolina death certificate independently confirms William Henry Pace and Emma Gornto/Gondo as her parents.
  • Obituary closure: The Valdosta Daily Times obituary of 7 Mar 1953 confirms William Henry Pace Jr.'s Columbus birthplace, Thomas County residence, surviving wife Ella Duncan Pace, surviving children W. R. Pace, J. F. Pace, Woodrow W. Pace, and Mrs. B. B. Owens, and burial in Boston City Cemetery.

docs.title: Family Narrative
docs.text:
• Head: Thomas Lightsy, also indexed as Thomas Lightey in one 1900 census entry. He was age 56, born Dec 1843 in Georgia, widowed, and working as a farmer. The census reports both parents born in South Carolina. He rented his farm in 1900.

Core record chain:

  • 1874 Brooks County marriage: Thomas Litsey married Elizabeth Florney on 20 Jul 1874. The record is from Georgia marriage records, Ancestry record 183273, image 40951_294515-00458.
  • 1880 census, Quitman, Brooks County: Thomas Lightsey, age 39, wife Elizabeth, age 27, and children Paul H., James R., Martha J., and Lucy.
  • 1880 agricultural schedule: Thomas Lightsey appears in District 4, Brooks County, enumerated 8 Jul 1880, page 36, line 1.
  • 1890 Georgia property tax digest: Thomas Lightsey, Black, Morven District 660, Brooks County, with land value reported at $200.

  • 1900 census, Barney, Brooks County: Thomas Lightsy, widowed, with children Martha, Clarice, John W., and Minnie.

  • Spouse:

Elizabeth Florney married Thomas in 1874 and appears as Elizabeth Lightsey in the 1880 census. She had died before the 1900 census, where Thomas is listed as widowed. The surname Florney may be a spelling variant of Flournoy, but the broader claim that Elizabeth belonged to a specific Flournoy sibling group has not been proven in this pass. No source found here identifies her parents.

Children with direct evidence:

  • Paul H. Lightsey, age 7 in the 1880 census. No confirmed post-1880 trace was found.
  • James R. Lightsey, age 6 in the 1880 census. No confirmed post-1880 trace was found.
  • Martha or Martha J. Lightsey, age 3 in 1880 and age 23 in 1900. This is almost certainly the same daughter, but no confirmed marriage, death, or later census trail was found.
  • Lucy Lightsey, age 5 months in 1880. She married George Wright in Brooks County on 30 Sep 1896 and appears as Lucy Wright in HH#13 in 1900.
  • Clarice Lightsey, age 17 in the 1900 household. No confirmed pre-1900 or post-1900 trace was found.
  • John W. Lightsey, age 15 in the 1900 household. No confirmed pre-1900 or post-1900 trace was found.
  • Minnie Lightsey, age 10 in the 1900 household. No confirmed post-1900 trace was found.

Probable but unproven child or kinship leads:

  • Ella Betts, wife of William Betts in HH#10, is a strong candidate for a Lightsey daughter or close relative. The main evidence is that Charley Lightsey is listed in the William Betts household as brother-in-law. No independent record found in this pass names Ella as Ella Lightsey or identifies Thomas and Elizabeth as her parents.
  • Charley Lightsey, age 12 in HH#10, is probably connected to the same Lightsey family and may be Ella's brother. The evidence does not yet prove that he was Thomas's son.

HH#13 Wright connection:

This connection is proven. Lucy Lightsey from the 1880 Thomas and Elizabeth Lightsey household married George Wright in 1896. In 1900, George and Lucy Wright live immediately after Thomas Lightsy's household, with children Allice and Thomas Wright. Lucy's age and birth month in 1900 fit the Lucy Lightsey listed as five months old in 1880.

HH#10 Betts connection:

The Betts connection is a strong lead, not a proved child line. Charley Lightsey's relationship as brother-in-law to William Betts points to a Lightsey connection through Ella Betts, but no separate marriage or vital record has been found to confirm Ella's maiden name or Charley's parents.

HH#185 Flournoy connection:

The 1874 marriage record gives Elizabeth's surname as Florney. This may be Flournoy, but the current source trail does not prove her relationship to Pollie Flournoy or any specific HH#185 family group.

docs.title: Family Narrative
docs.text:
• Head: George Wright, age 24, born about May 1876 in Georgia. In 1900 he was a day laborer at a sawmill in Barney, Brooks County, Georgia.

Wife: Lucy Wright, age 20, born January 1880 in Georgia. Lucy was Lucy Lightsey before marriage. She is securely identified as the daughter of Thomas Lightsey and Elizabeth Lightsey of HH#12.

Children identified from verified household records: - Allice Wright, daughter, age 3 in 1900, born about 1897 in Georgia. - Thomas Wright, son, age 1 in 1900, born about 1899 in Georgia. - Alice B. Wright, daughter, age 14 in 1910, born about 1896 in Georgia. - Tommie Wright, son, age 12 in 1910, born about 1898 in Georgia. - Eva May Wright, daughter, age 4 in 1910 and Eva Wright, daughter, age 14 in 1920, born about 1905-1906. - Jessie or Jesse J. Wright, son, age 10 in 1920 and age 20 in 1930, born about 1909-1910 in Florida.

Verified household path: - 1880: Lucy Lightsey appears in Quitman, Brooks County, Georgia, in the household of Thomas and Elizabeth Lightsey as their infant daughter. - 30 Sep 1896: George Wright married Lucy Lightsey in Brooks County, Georgia. - 1900: George and Lucy Wright appear in Barney, Brooks County, next to the Lightsey household, with children Allice and Thomas. - 1910: George and Lucy appear in Nixon, Washington County, Florida, with Alice B., Tommie, and Eva May. - 1920: George and Lucy appear in Newark, Essex County, New Jersey, at 21 Alling Street, with Eva and Jessie. - 1930: Lucy Wright appears in Newark as a widowed head of household with son Jesse J. Wright. - March 1937: Lucy Wright filed a Social Security application under the alias Lucy Lightsey, giving her birth as 19 Jan 1880 in Quitman, Georgia, and naming her father as Thomas Lightsey and her mother as Elizabeth Hurnur as indexed.

Assessment:

The link between HH#12 and HH#13 is proven. Lucy Lightsey of the Thomas Lightsey household is the same Lucy Wright who appears in 1900 Barney, 1910 Washington County, 1920 Newark, 1930 Newark, and the 1937 NUMIDENT record. The family moved from Brooks County into the Florida turpentine belt and then to Newark during the early twentieth-century labor migration.

George Wright is securely identified as Lucy's husband through the 1920 census. After that point, the record becomes less certain. The strongest current reading is that George either died or was otherwise absent before the 1930 census, because Lucy appears in Newark as a widow. A 1930 George Wright in Wilkes County, Georgia, and later 1940 and 1950 Georgia candidates remain unproven and should not be folded into this household without a direct bridge.

Connections to treat cautiously:

Lucy is tied to HH#12 through primary records. Wider claims linking this household to the Betts family or to a specific Flournoy sibling group remain unresolved and should not be stated as proven. George's parentage also remains unsettled. A FamilySearch tree and a plausible 1880 Brooks County household suggest Berry Wright and Catharine Mahaila Lampkins as candidate parents, but a World War I draft card from Newark names George's nearest relative as his mother, Mrs. Sallie Gibson, in Georgia. No direct record yet resolves that conflict.

  • The child-forward work is promising but still indirect. Alice B. Wright likely continued as Alice B. McKinnis in Newark, and Jesse J. Wright has plausible later candidates, but no parent-naming marriage, death, or Social Security record has yet locked either trail to this household.
  • Lucy's life after her March 1937 Social Security application remains open because her death or later continuation has not yet been proved.

docs.title: Household #14: Gornto, William
docs.text:
Household #14: Gornto, William¶

Back to the 1900 Census & Household Index

In the 1900 Barney census, William Gornto headed a 5-person household. The table transcribes the original household entries; uncertain readings are marked below.

Household Snapshot¶

William Gornto headed a 5-person household in the 1900 Barney census with 1 spouse or marital partner and 3 children.

William Gornto's listed occupation was Farmer.

All listed household members were reported as born in Georgia.

Newspaper and Public-Record Trail¶

This section flags public-record leads separate from the census table. The detailed discussion stays in the family narrative, research status, and source citations below.

1900 Census Household¶

Name Relation Age Birthplace Occupation
William Gornto Head 31 Georgia Farmer
Cordelia Gornto Wife Unclear* Georgia —
William C Gornto Son 5 Georgia —
Fannie Gornto Daughter 2 Georgia —
Joel C Gornto* Son 1 Georgia —

Children and Later Trails¶

Original census review. The 1900 sheet, ED 9, sheet 1B places Cordelia’s “10” in the years-married column. Her age is faint and is left unclear here; it must not be replaced by the marriage duration. Her birth entry reads November 1862, which differs from the June date in the later biographical identification below. The youngest son’s handwritten name is read as Joel C, birth February 1899, age 1; the earlier transcription was “Bill C.” This reading does not by itself establish his full name. William C remains William C on this sheet.

The 1910 original, ED 9, sheet 9A, household 176/177 in Morven district 660, lists Wille Gornto, 45, Kerdelia, 46, and children Calvin, 14; Fannie, 12; Joel, 10; Colin, 8; and Henry, 5. The family sequence supports household continuity. It does not alone prove that William C and Calvin are the same person, expand Joel or Colin’s names, or decide between competing Henry identifications. Cordelia is reported as mother of eight children, five living; that is not a complete named child list.

Fannie’s direct link. The Brooks County marriage return, page 108 records George Wilkins and Fannie Gornto married January 3, 1915, by J. H. Culpepper, J.P. The license was issued in December 1914; the recording date is blank. The marriage record does not name her parents.

Fannie Caroline Wilkins’s Georgia death certificate, no. 19052 explicitly names her father as W. B. Gornto Jr. and mother as Delia McRae. It reports birth August 16, 1897, death at Barney on April 16, 1925, and burial at Mt. Zion Cemetery on April 18. George Wilkins is the husband and informant. Together with the census daughter and marriage entries, these particulars identify Fannie as a child of this junior William and Cordelia—not the senior William next door. Birth and parent details are informant-reported; the burial entry is not a present-day grave inspection.

Cordelia’s dates and early census evidence¶

The photographed marker reads CORDELIA Mc GORNTO / JUNE 17, 1863 / NOV 30, 1949. Its installation date and informant are unknown. The memorial metadata instead supplies June 17, 1862, November 29, 1949, and Cook County as the death place. Those are different source statements, not interchangeable transcriptions.

The Georgia death index for Delia Gornto records age 86, death November 30, 1949, and Lowndes County as both residence and death place. This supports the marker’s death day but does not establish a precise birthday. The original 1949 certificate has not been inspected; the record page exposes no certificate image or certificate number. November 30 is supported by the index and marker, but the contemporary notice below instead places her death on Tuesday night, November 29. The exact day remains disputed.

In the 1870 original, Brooks County, page 115/74A, Cordelia McRae is listed at age 7 in Cornelius and Lucy McRae’s household. That schedule has no relationship column. The 1880 original, Quitman, ED 4, page 37 lists her at age 16, granddaughter, in C. W. and Lucy McRae’s household. These are original-image rechecks of previously cited records, not new discoveries. They support an early-1860s birth and the stated grandchild relationship, but neither names her parents or resolves the competing birth dates. The 1900 index reads May 1862, separately from the November reading of the handwritten entry above.

Contemporary death notice and surviving sons¶

The November 30, 1949 Valdosta Daily Times, page 12, headed “Services For Mrs. Willie Garnto In Hahira Thursday,” identifies her as “the former Delia McRea of Brooks county” and reports birth in 1863. It says she died at her son Calvin’s home “Tuesday night”. In this Wednesday issue, that means November 29, conflicting with November 30 in the death index and marker. The record image—not the search result’s erroneous December 6 death date—controls this reading. Her exact birth date and death day remain unresolved.

The notice explicitly names four surviving sons: Colon of Adel, Calvin and Joel of Hahira, and Henry of Ray City. With the given names, maiden name, husband and earlier census sequence, this strongly identifies the deceased as this household’s Cordelia and directly reports these men as her sons. It does not expand Colon, Joel or Henry’s names, establish their birth dates, or supply a complete lifetime child list. Fannie had already died in 1925.

The obituary describes a surviving husband and a marriage 61 years earlier; that duration differs from the cited December 27, 1889 marriage record and is not substituted for it. Services at Friendship Church in Hahira were announced for Thursday, December 1, at 3 p.m., with burial in the church cemetery. This is a prospective announcement, not confirmation that the service or burial took place.

The December 1 Hahira column, page 22 reports Calvin Garnto Jr. and Miss Margaret Garnto returning because of their grandmother’s illness and death, without naming her in that paragraph. A separate item calls Mrs. Will Garnto the grandmother of Mrs. G. C. Hodges. The December 7 column, page 10 repeats that relationship and reports the Hodgeses’ return to Atlanta after the death. Neither supplies Mrs. Hodges’s given name or the intervening parent; those links remain unassigned.

Henry’s name and the two memorial entries¶

The 1942 draft original reads Henry Casper Gornto, born July 1, 1903, at Barney, living at Ray City. It names Mrs. Delie Garnto as an address contact, without stating her relationship. The 1949 obituary’s son Henry of Ray City strengthens the household correlation; that identification remains a correlation across sources, not a parent statement on the draft itself.

The two memorial entries should not be counted as evidence of two separate sons. Memorial 44712201 labels him Henry Jasper, born 1905, but its own marker photograph reads HENRY C. GORNTO / JULY 1, 1903 / NOV. 3, 1974. The photograph attached to memorial 190185202 has the same inscription. Neither stone expands the middle initial to Jasper or Casper. These are probable duplicate memorial representations; the records are retained separately, and no external merge has been made.

The Georgia death index reports Henry C., 71, died November 3, 1974, in Lowndes County, with Berrien residence. It provides no original certificate image here. The marker and draft support 1903, while the earlier census ages and Jasper memorial metadata retain a 1905 conflict. The indexed 1974 obituary has not been inspected: the tested newspaper title’s current browse coverage ends in 1963.

William’s 1961 death and funeral notices¶

The September 30, 1961 Valdosta Daily Times, page 3, headed “W. B. GORNTO,” reports that William B. Gornto, age 94, died that day at Smith Hospital in Hahira. It names four surviving sons: Colon of Brooks County, Calvin of Hahira, Joel of Miami, and Henry of Ray City. The names, places and earlier family records strongly identify this as the junior William of HH14, not his father, whose original death certificate gives 1927. The notice says he was born and had lived most of his life in Brooks County, farmed there, and belonged to Salem Methodist Church. These are reported biographical details, not a land-title record.

The October 3 report, page 2, “W. B. GORNTO RITES,” says services for Willie B. Gornto of Route 2, Adel were held Sunday afternoon at Friendship Primitive Baptist Church, with burial in Friendship Cemetery. docs.text:
Household #15: Gornto, William¶

Back to the 1900 Census & Household Index

In the 1900 Barney census, William Gornto headed an 8-person household. The table below preserves the exact names, relationships, ages, birthplaces, and occupations recorded for the household.

Household Snapshot¶

William Gornto headed an 8-person household in the 1900 Barney census with 1 spouse or marital partner and 6 children.

William Gornto's listed occupation was Farmer.

All listed household members were reported as born in Georgia.

Children and Later Trails¶

This section is reserved for later-life child evidence. No later spouse, death, burial, obituary, probate, separate household, or descendant-line identification has been added here yet from direct records.

Family Narrative¶

  • Head: William Blair Gornto Sr., age 55 in 1900, farmer. His death certificate records birth on March 30, 1845, and death at Quitman on November 25, 1927; the birth particulars are informant-reported.
  • Spouse in 1900 household: Martha Gornto, age 50, born about 1850 in Georgia.
  • Children in the 1900 household: Leila, Thomas, Dollie, Gertrude, John J., and William.
  • Identity: William Blair Gornto Sr. is supported by the 1900 and 1910 censuses, his 20 May 1911 Confederate pension affidavit, land records, and the death certificate of son Thomas Norwood Gornto, which names mother Martha Taylor.
  • Parents: Joel Gornto and Mary Blair. No inspected record gives Mary the middle name Joyce; that name belonged to her reported mother.
  • First wife: Martha Jane Taylor. Her maiden name is supported by Thomas N. Gornto's Georgia death certificate.
  • Second wife: Fellie A., first securely identified in 1910. No record in this pass proves her prior surname or earlier identity.
  • Confederate service and land context: The cited records support Company A, 20th Georgia Battalion Cavalry service, a Brooks County pension filing, and long-term Gornto landholding on the older family tract.
  • Family context: HH#14 is William Blair Gornto Jr.; HH#7 connects through Hannah Elizabeth Gornto Hall.
  • 1899 newspaper context: A 14 Oct 1899 Valdosta Times article names "William Gornto" among the Barney-area farmers. Because the article does not distinguish senior from junior, the reference fits the Gornto farm network but cannot yet be assigned with certainty to HH#15 rather than HH#14.
  • Death and burial evidence: Georgia certificate image 004179451_01448, indexed as William Blair Garnte, records death at Quitman, Brooks County, November 25, 1927, age 82; parents Joel Garnte and Mary Blair; and burial at “Garnto Cemetery” on November 26. The informant was E. E. Eason of Quitman. Full name, generation, parents and named wife strongly identify this as the senior William, not his junior son, whose conflicting birth-year evidence is discussed in HH#14. The certificate is contemporary death evidence; its birth and parent information comes from the informant.
  • Marital-status caution: The original certificate says widowed, although its index says married, and names Martha Jane Taylor in the wife field. That entry does not explain the separately documented 1910 wife, Fellie A. Both records are retained; Fellie's prior identity and later history remain unresolved.
  • 1920 continuation: The original Barney census, ED 46, sheet 14A, image 4295805-00516, lists W. B. Garnto, 74 and widowed, as father in T. N. Garnto's household. This is an explicit relationship entry, not an inference from a shared surname.
  • Cemetery application: A March 28, 1940 headstone application for William Blair Garnto repeats November 25, 1927 and places Garnto Cemetery at Barney. Mrs. B. C. Eason is the applicant. Ordering and shipping annotations are present, but the application alone does not prove the stone was installed or identify a present grave location. Its unit line reads “29-Ga” with cavalry/Company A annotations; that differs from the pension-based 20th Battalion identification below and needs service-file comparison.
  • Estate distinction: The January 12, 1928 temporary appointment for W. B. Gornto names Mrs. B. C. Eason as administrator. The date, initials and headstone applicant make a strong estate-identification lead, but no relationship to Eason is stated. A separate 1906 J. J. Gornto estate had a W. B. Gornto as administrator; that person's senior/junior identity and the estate's 45-acre parcel remain unresolved.

Earlier Joel Gornto estate: a land lead, not a completed title chain¶

The Brooks will register preserves a petition and witness testimony on page 1 and the will and admission order on pages 2–3. Joel Gornto’s will is dated October 20, 1860. Nathan and Mary Gornto’s petition says he died that October, leaving the day blank. The will was proved December 3 and recorded December 5, 1860; those are not death dates.

Joel asks that his estate be kept together for his family, especially wife Mary Gornto during her natural life, then divided equally among his “legal heirs.” It does not name individual children, give Mary’s maiden name, or describe a numbered lot. The record is a strong research lead for the Joel and Mary named in William’s later death certificate, but this package does not by itself complete that identity and inheritance chain. The petition does not state smallpox or an exact death place.

The inventory warrant, page 47, explicitly identifies Mary Gornto and Nathan Gornto as administrators with the will annexed. The estate inventory, page 48, lists part of land lot 274, valued at \$1,200. The acreage reads 235 or 236; the final digit remains uncertain in the inspected image. No district or boundary is stated. Recorded September 10, 1861, this is an estate appraisal entry—not a deed to William, a later tax return, or proof of the tract’s subsequent ownership. It must not be used to silently resolve the separate 274/279 reading conflict.

Nathan Gornto's role as co-administrator does not establish that he was Joel's father. The current evidence does not prove Nathan's relationship to Joel.

Two administration bonds name Mary and Nathan as principals: January 3, 1861, with Enoch Hall as security, and March 4, 1861, with John Joyce and Tarlton B. Joyce named as securities. These roles do not establish kinship or personal ownership. The reason for the second bond is not stated in the inspected records. Neither is merged with the separate 1906 J. J. Gornto estate.

Military Service¶

The preserved record set supports William Blair Gornto Sr.'s Confederate service in Company A, 20th Georgia Battalion Cavalry. His 20 May 1911 Confederate pension affidavit and Brooks County filing provide the current service anchor; fuller service-file or pension transcription would strengthen the detailed chronology.

Connections to Other Barney Families¶

  • HH#15 to HH#14 William Blair Gornto Jr.: HH#14 represents William Blair Gornto Jr., son of this household head.
  • HH#15 to HH#7 Sion L. Hall: HH#15 connects to HH#7 through Hannah Elizabeth Gornto Hall, linking the Gornto and Hall lines.

  • Parentage audit: confirm both parents of the household head for HH#15 through direct or near-direct records where possible; mark derivative-only parent links as unresolved until supported.

Research Status¶

  • Status: Well-researched.
  • Strengths: Core identity, land history, military service, and family placement are well supported.
  • Remaining cautions: Fellie A.'s identity before 1910 remains unproven, and some later child attributions still need direct-record reconciliation. Joel’s 1860–1861 estate adds a lot274 lead but does not complete the later inheritance/title chain; its acreage reading remains uncertain.

docs.text:
• Census page: 2 | Lines: 35-38
  • Head: Isham Jones Pounds, age 27 in 1900, born 28 Dec 1872 in Georgia; identified in later records as a native of Valdosta, Lowndes County, Georgia
  • Death: 22 Sep 1964, St. Petersburg, Pinellas County, Florida; buried at Royal Palm South Cemetery
  • Parents: James Dix Pounds (1843-1875) and Mary Ann Bradford Pounds (1846-1875)
  • Earlier family research identifies Mary Ann Bradford as part of the Bradford family network also seen elsewhere in the Barney study, including HH#37.

  • Prior research also reports an 8 Feb 1876 guardianship by Shadrach Bradford for the Pounds orphans, but that record is not currently available for direct review and should be treated as an unavailable-source limitation rather than a fresh gap.

  • First wife: Cora Ella Roundtree Pounds, born 24 Apr 1873, died 14 Apr 1910

  • Seen as Cora E. Roundtree, age 6, in the 1880 household of James W. Roundtree and Anna J. Roundtree in Folsom, Lowndes County, Georgia.
  • Married Isham Pounds on 5 Mar 1895 in Lowndes County, Georgia. The county marriage certificate image is now on file.

  • Burial evidence now in hand places her at Salem United Methodist Church Cemetery, Hahira, Lowndes County, Georgia.

  • Second wife: Frances "Fannie" C. Horton Pounds, born 10 Mar 1888, died 19 Oct 1968

  • Married Isham Pounds on 5 Aug 1911 in Lowndes County, Georgia. The county marriage certificate image is now on file.

  • Later records place her in St. Petersburg, Pinellas County, Florida. Her obituary and memorial both support burial at Royal Palm South Cemetery.

  • Children documented in the records now assembled:

  • By the first marriage: Anna Estelle Pounds, Carl Minor Pounds, Nora M. Pounds, Charlie Isham Pounds, James T. Pounds, and William Wadeford Pounds.
  • By the second marriage: James Horton Pounds, Jones LaVern Pounds, Wilson Francis Pounds Sr., Wilbur Owen Pounds, and a younger son recorded as La Coy/Lacey Pounds in later census records.

Life course and work: - 1900: locomotive engineer in Barney, Brooks County, Georgia, with wife Cora and children Anna Estelle and Carl Minor in the household. - 1910: widowed brick mason in Valdosta, Lowndes County, Georgia, with Estelle, Carl Minor, Charlie, and Wadford in the home. - 1918: registered for the First World War draft in Polk County, Florida; residence Nichols, Polk County; nearest relative Mrs. F. Pounds. - 1920: bricklayer in a phosphate mine at Bartow, Polk County, Florida. - 1930: grocery store proprietor in St. Petersburg, Pinellas County, Florida. - 1935: still in Pinellas County, Florida, with Fannie and younger sons in the household. - 1940: gardener in St. Petersburg, with home ownership reported. - 1950: still at 3524 Tangerine Avenue in St. Petersburg; listed as a proprietor-worker and marked unable to work.

Notes on evidence and interpretation: - The entry is now supported by a much stronger record set than the earlier draft, including the 1900, 1910, 1920, 1930, 1935, 1940, and 1950 censuses, Isham's 1918 draft card, his 1964 obituary, Fannie's 1968 obituary, memorial evidence for both wives, and county marriage certificate images for both marriages. - The best burial documentation now in hand for Cora and Fannie comes from obituary and memorial evidence. No stronger cemetery-register copy is currently available in this file set. - Earlier wording that treated Find a Grave as negative for this family is obsolete.

docs.title: Family Narrative
docs.text:
• Census page: 2 | Lines: 39-43
  • Head: Benjamin F. Bridges appears in the 1900 Barney census as age 33, born May 1867 in Georgia, working as a lumber inspector. The 1910 census gives age 42 and birth year 1868, which is close but not perfectly aligned.
  • 1880 anchor: enumerated in Dooly County, Georgia, dwelling 519, as "Benjamine Bridges", age 12, son in the household of J. W. Bridges and Lidia Bridges.
  • Wife: Annie Bridges / Annie R. Bridges appears with Benjamin in both 1900 and 1910. A user-supplied Dooly County marriage certificate identifies her as Annie Aldridge.
  • Marriage record: Dooly County, Georgia, certificate for "B. F. Bridges" and "Annie Aldridge", dated 3 Oct 1891, with the marriage held 4 Oct 1891.
  • Marriage timing: the 1900 census reports marriage year 1891; the 1910 census reports 18 years married.

Children currently attributed to the household: - James Bridges, age 6 in 1900, is now well traced as James E. Bridges. User-supplied records place him in Columbia County, Florida, in 1920; Jacksonville, Duval County, in 1930 and 1940; Atlanta, Fulton County, in 1950; and Ormond Beach, Volusia County, by his 1975 Find a Grave memorial. Across those later records he appears with wife Nettie H. Bridges and children including James E. Bridges, Ann Bridges, and John H. Bridges. - William Bridges, age 4 in 1900, is well supported as William N. Bridges. His 1954 North Carolina death certificate gives birth on 10 Sep 1894 at Unadilla, Georgia, residence at Starke, Bradford County, Florida, father "B. F. Bridges", mother "Annie Aldridge", and burial at Lake City, Florida. A 1954 military headstone application adds WWI service details, confirms burial at Memorial Cemetery in Lake City, and names applicant Mrs. Edna Bridges of Gainesville, Florida. - Wilmer Bridges, age 5/12 in 1900, appears in the user-supplied screenshot as "Daughter". No stronger later record has been located in the present file set, so that reading remains the most cautious treatment. - Ben F. Bridges Jr., age 4, appears in the 1910 household. - Benjamin Aldridge Bridges, born 1 Aug 1905 in Dooly County, appears consistent with the 1910 "Ben F Bridges Jr" entry, but the present materials still do not prove that the two names belong to the same person.

Working reconstruction of family context: - The entry currently identifies Benjamin as a son of Joseph W. Bridges and Lydia A. Sutton Bridges of Dooly County, Georgia. - It also attributes siblings Sarah Bridges, William Bridges, Jefferson Davis Bridges, and Edwin C. Bridges to the same family cluster. - Those relationships may be correct, but the sources cited here do not yet provide the direct evidence needed to treat every kinship link as verified.

Life course reflected in the present evidence base: - 1880: Benjamin appears as a 12-year-old in Dooly County, Georgia, in the household of J. W. and Lidia Bridges. - 1900: Benjamin appears in Barney, Brooks County, Georgia, working as a lumber inspector. - 1910: Benjamin appears in Wadesboro, Leon County, Florida, working in saw milling; the household also includes Annie R. Bridges, their children, and Elizabeth Aldrige, listed as "Mother". - 1919: Find a Grave memorial 132464930 gives death on 25 Oct 1919 and burial at Florida State Hospital Cemetery, Chattahoochee, Gadsden County, Florida. A user-supplied Florida death index page also includes "Bridges, Ben F." in Gadsden County in 1919, giving derivative index support for the same death timeframe and place. - 1920-1950: James E. Bridges can be followed through successive census records from Columbia County to Jacksonville and then to Atlanta, showing a stable later-life trail well beyond the 1910 household. - 1954: William N. Bridges's death certificate, Find a Grave memorial, and military headstone application show that another son also remained traceable into mid-century records, strengthening the Florida continuation of this family line after 1910.

Interpretive notes: - The migration pattern from Dooly County to Brooks County and then into Florida is plausible and consistent with the current summary, but it should still be treated as a reconstruction drawn from the sources listed below rather than as a fully closed proof statement. - The earlier completion language overstated the current evidence state. This entry is better understood as a strong working profile pending fuller citation cleanup.

docs.title: Military Service
docs.text: William N. Bridges, the four-year-old son in the 1900 household, is tied to a 1954 military headstone application that gives service details and confirms burial at Memorial Cemetery in Lake City, Florida. The headstone application strengthens the adult identification of the child, though the page should continue to cite the application rather than expanding the service story beyond the preserved record.

• Census Page: 3 | Lines: 1-3
  • Head: Dave Bridges (age 20, Georgia, laborer at saw mill) — born October 1879, Georgia
  • Spouse: Cassie Bridges (wife, age 23, Georgia) — born about 1877
  • Marriage: 22 May 1898, Berrien County, Georgia, to Cassie/Cossie Wilker or Wilkes
  • Children:
  • John D. Bridges (son, age 1) — born about 1899

Identity and family reconstruction - The 1900 census records this household under the name Dave Bridges and ties the entry to index variants that include Downie Bridges. - A Berrien County marriage record dated 22 May 1898 names Downie Bridges as the groom and Cassie/Cossie Wilker as the bride. - A World War I draft registration card for Donnie Bridges, signed Downie Bridges, gives residence at Berlin, Georgia, birth date 23 October 1879, and nearest relative Cassie Bridges. - Later family records connect Willard D. or Willard Downey Bridges to wife Nancy Wilkes/Nancy C. Bridges and son John Durell Bridges. Those records include a FindAGrave memorial for Nancy C. Bridges and the death certificate of son Bruce Burton Bridges, which names his parents as Willard D. Bridges and Nancy Wilkes. - Taken together, these records support identifying the 1900 household head Dave Bridges as the same man later recorded as Downie/Donnie Bridges and Willard D./Willard Downey Bridges.

Parentage and sibling context - An 1880 census household in Powder Springs, Cobb County, Georgia, lists T. M. Bridges and S. L. Bridges with children including J. M. Bridges, age 3, and D. Bridges, age 7/12. - This household fits the later evidence well and strongly supports identifying Dave/Downie/Willard as a son of Thomas M. Bridges and Sarah L. Bridges, later expanded in other records as Thomas Marion Bridges and Sarah Louisa Dean Bridges. - The same 1880 household also provides the strongest preserved support that HH#21 Dave Bridges and HH#27 James Marvin Bridges were brothers.

Later residence and death - Later records place the family in south Georgia and eventually in Chatham County. - A Chatham County death index entry records Willard D. Bridges, age 70, dying on 30 March 1949 under certificate 4514.

docs.title: Family Narrative
docs.text:
Walter Kellbrew, age 21, and his wife Mary, age 22, appear in the 1900 Barney census as a two-person newly married household. The household was renting its home. In the preserved local census summary report, Walter's occupation is not listed.

A user-supplied marriage license/certificate image now directly supports the marriage. It shows Walter Kelbrew and Miss Mary Tillman in Lowndes County, with the license issued 2 Feb 1900 and the marriage certified 4 Feb 1900. This corrects the earlier "Mary Fillman" reading in the encyclopedia.

A user-supplied 1880 census screenshot strengthens Walter's side of the identification as well. It shows "Henry Killibrew", born Jul 1879, in the household of "Taylor Killibrew" and "Nancy Killibrew" in Macon, Georgia. James clarified that Henry was Walter Killebrew's middle name, so this works well as a childhood anchor for the later Walter Henry Killebrew.

A user-supplied 1929 Georgia death certificate strengthens the identification. It names "W. H. Killebrew", white male, age 51, residence Ellenton, Georgia, who died 19 Oct 1929 in Moultrie, Colquitt County. The certificate names his wife as "Mrs. Mary Killebrew" and gives his parents as "U. T. Killebrew" and "Miss Susiana Barfield". That age fits the HH#23 Walter far better than the earlier preserved note that gave a birth month and year of Apr 1862.

The 1910 widow household is now directly supported. A user-supplied census screenshot shows Mary Killebrew, age 36, widowed, in Hahira, Lowndes County, with daughters Perlie and Sallie C. in the household of Jim H. Tillman and Sara A. Tillman. Additional user-supplied census screenshots then carry Mary forward in 1920, 1930, and 1950 in Colquitt County.

Those later records now look less contradictory than they first seemed. The 1880 census screenshot shows Mary Tillman, age 5, as daughter of Harrison Tillman and Sarah A. Tillman. The 1920 census also places Mary in that same line. The 1910 census shows her as daughter in the household of Jim H. Tillman and Sara A. Tillman at Hahira. If "Jim H." is James Harrison Tillman, these may be different name forms for the same parental couple rather than two separate parent hypotheses.

A newly supplied Tillman family book page still needs careful handling. It lists Mary Tillman under Harrison Tillman and Sarah Ann Duckworth, then lists James H. Tillman separately on the same page. That remains a compiled secondary source, not primary proof. But once James clarified that "Jim H." stood for James Harrison, the page no longer reads like a clean contradiction of the 1910 household.

The FindAGrave memorials for both Mary and Walter add useful burial and family-link support, including cemetery photographs and matching child names, though one memorial detail — marriage year 1889 — conflicts with the direct 1900 marriage record and should be disregarded. A newly supplied Tampa obituary for "Mrs. Mary M. Killebrew" also fits the later-life trail: it says she died in 1964, was a native of Berrien County, and was survived by "one daughter, Mrs. Ben Tillman", which matches the 1930 and 1950 households.

One preserved research note from 29 Mar 2026 identified a "Walter H. Killebrew" who died in 1929. That note now looks partly right on the death year and spouse name, but wrong or at least unverified on the reported 1862 birth year and the military framing.

  • Record set now in hand:

docs.title: Family Narrative
docs.text:
This household is now much firmer than it looked on first review. The 1880 census places Calvin L. McKinney, age 7, in District 1311, Berrien County, Georgia, in the household of James W. McKinney and Julia A. McKinney, with siblings Ada O., William W., and Carlos T. By 1900, the Barney census shows the same man under a different form, Luther McKinie, age 25, renting a house in Brooks County and working as "Laborer Tables", with wife Priscilla and daughter Katie, age 3. The odd spelling "McKinie" fits the usual census-transcription drift rather than a separate surname.

The marriage record ties that Barney household together cleanly. A user-supplied Brooks County marriage certificate shows Luther McKinney and Priscilla Berryhill joined in matrimony on 6 Nov 1895. The 1910 census then shows Calvin L McKinney, age 36, still in Barney, Brooks County, with wife Priscilla McKinney, age 41, and daughter Katie Lou McKinney, age 13. In 1920 the family appears in Greggs, Cook County, where C L McKinney, age 46, is listed with wife Pricilla McKinney, age 50, daughter Katie Lou McKinney, age 23, and grandson Charlie Howell, age 2. Those four censuses give a coherent county-to-county progression and confirm that the daughter's fuller name was Katie Lou by 1910.

The later-life burial evidence also holds. FindAGrave memorial #74217594 identifies Luther McKinney, born 22 Sep 1872, died 21 Jun 1928, buried at Antioch Cemetery, Adel, Cook County, Georgia. The same memorial links spouse Priscilla A McKinney and lists parents James W McKinney (1853-1921) and Julia Ann Norman McKinney (1855-1926). Memorial #74217611 identifies Priscilla A McKinney, born 2 Nov 1869, died 29 Oct 1954, buried beside him at Antioch Cemetery.

What changed here is not that the old "RESEARCH COMPLETE" label suddenly became justified. It did not. What changed is that the household now has direct support across 1880, 1900, 1910, 1920, the 1895 marriage record, and both memorials. That is enough to restore a broader continuity narrative. What still remains unsettled is the exact fully spelled-out name Calvin Luther McKinney. The records checked in this pass show Calvin L., C L, and Luther, which makes the synthesis very plausible, but I still have not seen a directly checked primary record spelling out the whole combined form.

So the household is best described as substantially verified, but not fully source-exhausted. The false negative FindAGrave claim is gone. The family trail from Berrien County to Barney and then to Cook County now stands on real evidence. What still needs closing is the exact full-name proof, the Berryhill obituary citation chain, the daughter's later identity, and the relationship path behind grandson Charlie Howell.

• Census Page: 3 | Lines: 17-18
  • Head: James Marvin Bridges, also recorded as James M. Bridges, Marvin Bridges, and Mervin Bridges (age 23 in 1900, Georgia, laborer at saw mill) — born 23 February 1877, Georgia; died 18 February 1938
  • Spouse: Jennie Parrish Bridges (wife, age 17 in 1900, Georgia) — born 3 March 1883, Georgia; died 7 March 1962
  • Marriage: 25 May 1899, Berrien County, Georgia

Identity and family reconstruction - The 1880 census in Powder Springs, Cobb County, Georgia, lists J. M. Bridges, age 3, in the household of T. M. Bridges and S. L. Bridges. The same household includes D. Bridges, age 7/12. - A Berrien County marriage certificate dated 25 May 1899 names James M. Bridges and Jennie Parrish. - A marriage notice reprinted in The Valdosta Times on 6 June 1899 reports that Marvin Bridges married Miss Jennie Parrish at the Parrish home near Adel. - The 1900 census in Barney, Brooks County, Georgia, records the household as Mervin Bridges with wife Jennie Bridges, married within the year. Taken together, these records support treating J. M., James M., Marvin, and Mervin Bridges as the same man.

Connection to HH#21 - The 1880 Cobb County household places J. M. Bridges and D. Bridges in the same home under T. M. and S. L. Bridges. - That record, together with the separate HH#21 review, supports the conclusion that HH#27 James Marvin Bridges and HH#21 Dave Bridges were brothers. - The parent names preserved in this record set are T. M. Bridges and S. L. Bridges, later expanded in family materials as Thomas M./Thomas Marion Bridges and Sarah L./Sarah Louisa Dean Bridges.

Later life - By 1910 the family was in Birmingham, Jefferson County, Alabama, where James M. Bridges worked as a locomotive fireman. The household included wife Jennie and children Vernon H., Marvin, Stella, and Mildred. - In 1920 the family remained in Birmingham. James was recorded as J. M. Bridges, with wife Janie/Jennie and children Vernon, Marvin, Stella, and Dorie. - In 1930 James M. Bridges was still in Birmingham, working as a locomotive engineer on the steam railroad. The household included Jennie, Vernon H., James M. Jr., and Darris. The census marked him as a Spanish-American War veteran. - FindAGrave memorials place James M. Bridges and Jennie Parrish Bridges in Sparks City Cemetery, Sparks, Cook County, Georgia. James's memorial gives the same 25 May 1899 marriage date and identifies his service in Company D, 3rd Georgia Infantry. - Jennie appears as a widow in Birmingham in the 1940 and 1950 censuses, which fits James's 1938 death.

The memorial evidence and census placement support that reading, though not every later-life step has been independently documented.

Sapp and Pope connection - The 1900 household ties Eliza Cooper to Frances "Fannie" Pope Sapp and Ansel Turner Sapp. - The preserved source trail also links Frances Sapp to George Washington Sapp and to John A. Pope. - The collected records attribute John A. Pope's death to Civil War service and identify Frances as his daughter. That claim is supported here by the listed military indexes rather than by a local service file.

Later household trail - The preserved entry states that the Cooper family appears again in Colquitt County in 1910 and 1920. - The 1910 household is summarized as showing four children born, two living. - The 1920 household is summarized as showing the family in or near Moultrie, Colquitt County, with additional surviving children. - Those later census placements appear consistent with the memorial dates for William Franklin Cooper and Nancy Elizabeth Sapp Cooper, but the original census records should be checked before treating the connection as settled.

Related lines noted in the present record set - Frances "Fannie" Pope Sapp is linked to FindAGrave memorial 90447093. - George Washington Sapp is linked to FindAGrave memorial 90447094. - Ansel Turner "Ancil" Sapp is described in the current entry as later marrying Susan Rosenia Rosa Meredith in Worth County, Georgia, serving in World War I draft or service records tied to Dade County, Florida, and later living in Florida. Those details appear to come from the documented marriage, military, and tree materials named below, but not all of those extracts are preserved locally in this pass.

docs.text:
• Census Page: 3 | Lines: 28-32
  • Head: John Register, age 40 in 1900, recorded as born Oct 1859 in North Carolina, occupation "Wood Woodsman"

  • Children shown in the 1900 household:
  • Katherine "Katie" Register, age 9
  • John Register, age 2
  • Other household member:
  • Martha "Willear" Wilcox, mother-in-law, age 62

Direct household anchor - The surviving HH#30 record set securely anchors the family in Barney in 1900. - The preserved 1900 household shows John Register, Della Register, Katie Register, John Register, and Martha Willear in one home. - The same 1900 entry supports that the household was owned and free of mortgage. - It also preserves John's occupation as "Wood Woodsman."

Later record trail - User-supplied census screenshots now directly document the family in 1910 and 1920. - The 1910 Barney census shows John D. Register, age 47, born in North Carolina, with wife Della, daughter Catharine Moris, son Rufus Register, and daughter Gladis Register. It also shows laborer work in public work, home ownership, and free-of-mortgage status. - The 1920 Hickory Head, Brooks County, census shows J. D. Register, age 57, born in North Carolina, with wife Della, daughter Gladys Register, Martha Wilcox, and nephew Lonnie Wilcox. - The preserved HH#30 materials also cite a marriage record for John Register and Susan Idella Wilcox on 10 Jul 1890 in Berrien County, Georgia. - User-supplied FindAGrave screenshots add two direct cemetery references: John Drew "Jack" Register, memorial 87406499, and Susan Idella "Della" Wilcox Register, memorial 87406334, both at Oak Hill Cemetery in Quitman, Brooks County, Georgia. - The John memorial shows birth 16 Aug 1861 in North Carolina and death 31 Dec 1927 in Brooks County, Georgia. The Susan memorial shows birth in 1868, death in 1946 in Jefferson County, Florida, and burial at Oak Hill Cemetery. - User-supplied 1860, 1870, and 1880 census screenshots now provide a stronger North Carolina pre-Barney trail for John D. or Jack Register. In 1860 he appears as John D. Register, age 2, in Northwest District, Brunswick County, North Carolina, in the household of John N. Register and Elizabeth Register. In 1870 and 1880 he appears in Richmond County, North Carolina, in the household of John M. or J. N. Register and Elizabeth Register. - User-supplied Georgia death-certificate screenshots now directly document John Drew Register's death in Brooks County on 31 Dec 1927. The certificate gives birth 16 Aug 1861 in North Carolina, spouse Della Mae Wilcox, father John Register, mother Elizabeth Thornton, and burial at Oak Hill Cemetery on 1 Jan 1928. - User-supplied Georgia death-certificate screenshots also now directly document Martha J. Wilcox's death in Brooks County on 6 Dec 1920 at age 82. The certificate gives birthplace Georgia, father Hugh McCann, mother Sarah McCann, spouse J. B. Wilcox, and burial at Oak Hill Cemetery on 7 Dec 1920. - User-supplied 1850 Thomas County census screenshots add an earlier McCan household that includes Martha McCan, age 11, and Sarah McCan, age 46. James reviewed the census image and confirmed that the indexed name "Hazh" is a transcription error for Hugh, which brings the household into much closer agreement with Martha's later death-certificate parent pair. - User-supplied later-life screenshots now extend Susan Idella Register's trail through 1930 in Brooks County, 1940 in Wakulla County, Florida, 1945 in Jefferson County, Florida, and a 1946 Florida death-index entry in Jefferson County.

What the current record set supports - The family is now directly anchored in Brooks County in 1900, 1910, and 1920. - The user-supplied 1910 and 1920 screenshots materially strengthen the household continuity that earlier versions only summarized. - The user-supplied 1860, 1870, and 1880 screenshots strongly support a North Carolina origin line for John D. or Jack Register and fit the later Brooks County birthplace reports. - The 1860 Brunswick County household is especially important because it places John D. Register in the John N. Register and Elizabeth Register household at about age 2, which aligns well with the later death-certificate identification of his parents as John Register and Elizabeth Thornton. - The user-supplied death certificate and FindAGrave memorial together directly support John Drew Register's death on 31 Dec 1927 and burial at Oak Hill Cemetery in Quitman. - The death certificate also materially strengthens the identification of John's parents as John Register and Elizabeth Thornton, which fits the North Carolina Register household trail. - The user-supplied later-life screenshots show a coherent widowhood trail for Susan: 1930 in Brooks County with daughter Gladis, 1940 in Wakulla County in the Ray Thompson household, 1945 in Jefferson County, Florida, and a 1946 Florida death-index entry in Jefferson County. - The user-supplied FindAGrave memorials directly support that John and Susan were buried at Oak Hill Cemetery in Quitman and that the memorial creator associated them as spouses. - Martha Wilcox's presence in both the 1900 and 1920 households supports a multi-generational household structure over a long span. - Martha J. Wilcox's death is now directly documented on 6 Dec 1920, which reconciles the earlier conflict created by the unreliable 1919 family-panel date attached to Susan's memorial. - The 1850 Thomas County McCan household materially strengthens the identification of Martha's parents as Hugh McCann and Sarah McCann. That conclusion is now supported by the death certificate plus the census image James reviewed, not by derivative tree material alone.

Cautions - Much of the older HH#30 narrative was more specific than the currently preserved local proof packet justified, but the new screenshots materially improve that packet. - The FindAGrave memorials improve the burial and death trail for John and Susan, but FindAGrave remains a derivative source unless matched against death certificates, cemetery registers, or other direct records. - A real birth-year conflict remains visible. The 1900 census gives John a birth date of Oct 1859, the 1860 census points to about 1858, while the 1870 and 1880 censuses, the death certificate, and the John memorial point toward 16 Aug 1861, and the 1910 and 1920 enumerations point more broadly to about 1863. - The 1900 screenshot gives a marriage year of 1891, but the supplied marriage certificate shows John Register and Susan Idella Wilcox married on 10 Jul 1890 in Berrien County, Georgia. The 1890 date should be preferred over the census-year discrepancy. - The Susan memorial's family-members panel points to Martha Jane McCann Wilcox as 1838-1919, but the 1920 census screenshot shows Martha Wilcox alive in the household at age 81, and the supplied Georgia death certificate records Martha J. Wilcox's death on 6 Dec 1920. The family-panel date is therefore unreliable. - The recent Geneanet screenshots are still useful only as clue material. They are no longer necessary for the core McCann parent identification, which now rests on the death certificate and the 1850 census household.

docs.title: Historic Family Line
docs.text:
Bolin Green Hall belongs to the same early Hall family line. Huxford identifies Bolin as a son of Col. Enoch Hall and Enoch's first wife, Sallie Self Hall. Huxford also identifies Enoch as the son of Sion Hall and Bridget "Beady" Hall, making Bolin a grandson of the early Sion Hall whose Coffee Road home stood near present Morven.

This makes the Bolin Hall household more than a farm family entry in the 1900 census. It is a surviving branch of the family associated with the Coffee Road, the first Lowndes County court sessions, the Hall inn near Morven, early militia leadership, and the old Hall home place that Huxford traced back to the opening of the road in 1823.

Bolin also connects directly to the next Barney generation. His son Arthur P. Hall appears nearby as a separate 1900 household, and his half-brother Sion L. Hall appears as a Barney merchant in HH#7. The census therefore shows three layers of the Hall line close together: Bolin's older farm household, Sion L. Hall's merchant household, and Arthur P. Hall beginning his own household.

Source note: this section is based on Folks Huxford, The History of Brooks County, Georgia, 1858-1948, especially the Coffee Road, Morven, and Col. Enoch Hall passages.

docs.title: Family Narrative
docs.text:
• Head: Bolin Green Hall, age 62 in 1900, born May 1838 in Georgia, farmer.
  • Wife: Julia Phillips Hall, age 52 in 1900, born Jan 1848 in Georgia.
  • 1900 household facts: Married about 35 years; Julia reported 10 children born and 10 living; Bolin could read and write; the farm was owned free of mortgage.
  • Children in the 1900 household: Enoch Harrison, Chloe Ann, Arthur P., Thomas Gilette, Ophelia, Florence, John Phillips, Lorena, Louisa, and Sarah Hall.
  • Identity chain: The preserved census sequence from 1850, 1870, 1880, 1900, and 1910 strongly supports the same Bolin Hall household despite small name-form variation.
  • Marriage and Phillips bridge: The current research trail supports a Brooks County marriage for Bolin Hall and Julia Phillips dated 25 Mar 1866. User-supplied 1850 and 1860 census images for Julia Phillips, plus her 1924 death certificate, strongly support Levi Phillips as her father.
  • Mother-name boundary: Julia's death certificate does not independently confirm her mother's name. The mother remains best supported through the 1850 and 1860 census chain as Cloe or Clara Phillips.
  • Military and burial evidence: The War Department headstone application and positive Hall Cemetery memorials materially strengthen Bolin's military unit, burial place, and 1918 death trail.
  • Date conflict: The headstone application gives 22 Oct 1918 while the memorial shows 21 Oct 1918. That discrepancy should remain visible until a direct death record resolves it.

docs.title: Military Service
docs.text: The War Department headstone application identifies Bolin G. Hall as a private in Company F, 12th Georgia Infantry, providing direct support for Confederate service. The same military-burial trail strengthens his Hall Cemetery placement, though the 21 October versus 22 October 1918 death-date conflict should remain explicit.

docs.title: Historic Family Line
docs.text:
Arthur P. Hall was part of the Bolin Green Hall and Julia Phillips Hall family. Through Bolin, Arthur connects back to Col. Enoch Hall and then to Sion Hall, the early Coffee Road settler whose home and inn stood near present Morven. Huxford's account makes this Hall line one of the families tied to the first settlement period, the early court sessions, the Coffee Road, and the old Morven community.

Arthur's separate 1900 household shows the next generation of that line forming a new household in Barney while his parents remained nearby in HH#33.

Source note: this section is based on Folks Huxford, The History of Brooks County, Georgia, 1858-1948, especially the Coffee Road, Morven, and Col. Enoch Hall passages.

docs.title: Family Narrative
docs.text:
• Head: Arthur P. Hall (age 25, Georgia, farmer)

  • Wife: Emma Burney Hall (age 23, Georgia)

  • The preserved research trail places Arthur P. Hall in the household of Bolin Green Hall and Julia Phillips Hall in 1880 and then as a separate married head in Barney in 1900, supporting identification of Arthur as their son.

  • In the 1900 census Arthur appears as a 25-year-old farmer in Barney with wife Emma Burney Hall, age 23, and the census indicates a recent marriage.
  • The next documented marriage in the current trail is Arthur Hall to Flora Willis on 31 Jan 1907 in Georgia.
  • Arthur's World War I draft registration card, dated 12 Sep 1918, places him in Barney, Brooks County, Georgia, gives his birth date as 7 Jun 1873, describes him as a merchant working for himself, and names Mrs. Flora Hall as nearest relative.
  • The later census trail continues through 1910, 1920, and 1930.
  • The 1930 census places Arthur and Flora Hall in Haines City, Polk County, Florida, with children Marguerite, William F., Lois, George W., Flora, and Dorothy in the household, along with divorced daughter Bertha Rivero and granddaughter Bettie J. Rivero.
  • The current death-record trail identifies Arthur's death on 12 Sep 1930 in Haines City, Florida.
  • A positive FindAGrave memorial for Arthur P. Hall identifies Forest Hill Cemetery in Haines City, Polk County, Florida, as his burial place.
