docs.text:
Back to the 1900 Census & Household Index

In the 1900 Barney census, George Ingram headed an 8-person household. The table below follows the household transcription, with George’s age corrected from the original schedule; uncertain name readings remain noted below.

docs.title: Household Snapshot
docs.text:
George Ingram headed an 8-person household in the 1900 Barney census with 1 spouse or marital partner and 6 children.

George Ingram's listed occupation was Farmer.

All listed household members were reported as born in Georgia.

docs.title: Newspaper and Public-Record Trail
docs.text: This section flags public-record leads separate from the census table. The detailed discussion stays in the family narrative, research status, and source citations below.

docs.title: 1900 Census Household
docs.text:
Name Relation Age Birthplace Occupation George Ingram Head 49 Georgia Farmer Mary C Ingram Wife 37 Georgia — Lingusia Ingram Daughter 20 Georgia — Simion Ingram Son 17 Georgia — John H Ingram Son 15 Georgia — Mary M Ingram Daughter 13 Georgia — Annie B Ingram Daughter 8 Georgia — Shellie Ingram Son 2 Georgia —

The original schedule (ED 9, sheet 8B, dwelling/family 161, lines 70–77) gives George a March 1851 birth and age 49. The former “21” was the years-married entry, not his age; Ancestry’s household index separately reads the age as 42. Mary C. is entered as February 1863, age 37, married 21 years, with six children born and five living. The six children’s relationships are to George as head; the count does not establish that all six were Mary’s biological children. The eldest daughter’s indexed name “Lingusia” remains a reading to reconcile with Eugenia in 1880.

docs.title: George’s Death and Estate
docs.text:
A recorded widow-support petition by Mrs. M. C. Ingram states that Geo. W. Ingram died on December 1, 1903, leaving her and four minor children. The children are not named in that petition. Abel Ingram acknowledged service as administrator on July 1, 1904; separate administration letters name him for George W. Ingram’s estate. Neither document calls Abel George’s brother.

The appraisers’ return of July 16, 1904 sets apart property assessed at $1,843, including 300 acres of lot 364, livestock, farm equipment, produce, $100 cash and household/kitchen furniture. The approval paragraph is completed, but its term/date blanks are unfilled. This is a support award, not an underlying purchase deed or a complete title chain. It must not be confused with the I. B. Ingram estate’s lot 414 sale described in the probate guide.

The Valdosta Times, December 22, 1903, page 3, reprinted an Adel News notice headed “Mr. George Ingram Is Dead.” It reports that George W. Ingram died at home about four miles north of Barney after becoming ill in Quitman, and that the funeral occurred at the family’s old burial ground at Pine Grove Church in Colquitt County. Its wording “Tuesday night of last week” is relative to an undated reprinted report; it does not independently settle the calendar date or resolve the petition’s December 1 entry. No grave-marker identification is established here.

George W.’s Book L final return, dated November 13, 1905, sworn December 31, 1905 and allowed February 5, 1906, records Abel as administrator and transactions with M. C. Ingram. Its voucher dates must not be mistaken for George’s death date. The shared names, widowhood and Barney household sequence support this estate connection, rather than initials alone.

docs.title: Mary C. / Katie and the Household Sequence
docs.text:
The original Colquitt marriage register names George W. Ingram and Miss Katie Daley in the certificate: license February 11, ceremony February 13, 1879, received February 22. The inspected page is a later register transcription from Book A-1, page 98, recorded May 5, 1905—not a surviving loose 1879 license.

The 1880 original lists G. W. Ingram, 29; Mary C., 20, wife; Eugenia, five months, daughter; and Leah, 80, explicitly his mother. In 1910, Mary C. is a 49-year-old widow at Barney with Simmie O., Mary M., Annie B., Shellie D. and Katie G. listed as her children (ED 21, sheet 12B, dwelling 218/family 219). The 1850 George W. infant in Guilford and Leah’s household remains part of the earlier candidate chain, but its birth timing conflicts with March 1851; that census has no relationship column. Leah’s age and birthplace also differ between 1850 and 1880.

Mrs. M. C. Ingram’s original death certificate records death May 19, 1935, at Barney and burial at Sardis on May 20. It gives birth September 10, 1860, parents D. Dailey of Ireland and Mozelle Lovell of Georgia. That birth date conflicts with the 1900 census, and is reported here as the certificate’s statement, not a resolved correction. Mrs. J. W. Carter is the informant; no relationship is supplied. Later administration letters name Mrs. Belle Carter for Mrs. M. C. Ingram’s estate. Their indexed December 2, 1936 date and earlier January 1936 inventory deadline require reconciliation; the index’s inferred death year is not evidence of a 1936 death. The two Carter names have not been merged here.

docs.title: Children and Later Trails
docs.text: This section is reserved for later-life child evidence. No later spouse, death, burial, obituary, probate, separate household, or descendant-line identification has been added here yet from direct records.

docs.title: Connections to Other Barney Families
docs.text: Nearby 1900 Ingram households may be collateral relatives, including HH#168 and HH#169, but those connections have not been re-proved in this cleanup. Abel Ingram in the 1850, 1860, and 1870 Guilford Ingram household appears to be George's brother and may help explain part of the nearby Ingram cluster.

docs.title: Research Notes
docs.text:
• Reconcile the widow petition’s December 1, 1903 death date with the reprinted notice’s relative wording; locate the original Adel News issue and an independently identified Pine Grove grave. Trace the lot 364 deed history without treating the support award as a purchase deed.
  • Resolve whether Eugenia in 1880 and Lingusia in 1900 are the same daughter, and seek a direct marriage, death, burial, or parent-naming record.
  • Continue targeted searches for John H. Ingram after 1900. Current later John Ingram hits are too weak or point to other parents and places.
  • Prove Georgia/Katie G. Ingram's later life with a direct parent bridge, or keep her adult trail unresolved.
  • Do not use the Tennessee Civil War pension index for Mary Ingram, widow of Washington Ingram, as proof of this family without the pension file or another direct bridge.
  • Do not use the Georgia Ingram Peavy, Sallie Eugenia Ingram Curenton, or 1940 Washington, D.C. records as proved HH#161 evidence.

docs.text: • Resolve the open items flagged in Research Notes above with direct records before expanding this household narrative.

docs.title: Research Status
docs.text:
• Status: Source-Researched / not source-exhausted.
  • Strengths: Original adult censuses, marriage, widow-support petition and administration letters support the household and estate trail. Earlier census age/birthplace conflicts remain visible. Mary C./Katie Dailey's identity rests on the 1870 Dailey household, the 1879 marriage, the widow household sequence, and her 1935 death record. Mary M.'s 1923 death record directly names Geo. Ingram and Kate Daily as parents. Simmie/Simion, Annie B., and Shellie/Shelly have usable adult trails.
  • Remaining cautions: The widow petition directly reports George’s death and the newspaper reports his funeral location, but the date wording and exact grave remain unresolved. Lingusia/Eugenia, John H., and Georgia/Katie G. remain unresolved. Several candidate clusters have been rejected or left as leads because they do not bridge back to George W. Ingram and Mary C./Katie Dailey.

docs.title: Children and Later Trails
docs.text:
No children are listed in this household in the 1900 census table.

Census Page: 16 | Lines: 28-30 District: 1571 (Barney), ED 9, Brooks County Race: Black in 1900; other records and indexes vary by enumerator or indexer Research Status: Source-Researched / not source-exhausted

Henry appears in the 1900 Barney census under the difficult surname form indexed by Ancestry as Henry Lee Or See. The same household names his wife as Fannie Lee Or See and places Herman Mitchell with them as a boarder. The strongest record trail for Henry uses several surname forms: Lee, See, Sea, and Seay. Race and birthplace also vary across records. Those differences should be preserved as part of the evidence rather than smoothed into one uniform identity.

A likely earlier Henry appears in the 1880 Quitman, Brooks County household of Angeline See. That record lists Henry See, age 13, as Angeline’s son, with other sons Mathew, Jackson, Augustus, Robert, David, and Jasper. It supports a Henry-and-Angeline relationship, but it does not prove every later Seay family claim found in derivative trees.

A candidate childhood record was also reviewed in the 1870 Madison County, Florida census. It places Angeline W. Lee, age 26, and Henry Lee, age 4, in Madison County. This record fits the Madison, Florida birthplace and Angeline mother pattern seen in Henry’s 1934 death material, but it is not a direct bridge to the 1880 Brooks County Angeline See household. The 1870 entry should remain a candidate clue, not a settled identification.

Henry married Fannie Exom in Brooks County on 4 October 1894. The 1910 Barney census then lists Henry Sea, age 40, born Florida, with wife Fannie and children Olvie, Dollie, and Jessie. The 1910 household is the clearest direct bridge for those three children.

Henry’s 1934 Georgia death entry strengthens the Henry-and-Angeline connection. FamilySearch indexes him as Henry Sea, age 68, born Madison, Florida, a farmer, with mother Angeline Sea. The FamilySearch original-document viewer text gives the death place as Brooks County, Georgia, with cemetery wording as Wesleys Chappel and burial place as Berlin, Georgia. A certificate-viewer screenshot was reviewed, but the handwriting and OCR were not strong enough to support a fully normalized transcription of every field.

docs.title: Connections to Other Barney Families
docs.text:
The direct record trail supports Henry’s connection to Angeline See/Sea/Lee and to Fannie Exom/Seay. Broader Angeline Seay ancestry claims in online trees remain leads unless direct records are pulled and reconciled.

Adult-child trails are uneven:

  • Ike Seay is not in Henry and Fannie’s 1900 or 1910 household, but his 1936 Georgia death record names his parents as Henry Seay and Fannie Seay. This is the strongest parent-naming adult-child evidence found so far.
  • Olvie Sea/Seay appears as Henry and Fannie’s daughter in 1910. Fresh searches found the 1910 parent-naming census, but no accepted adult trail. Later Ola, Olas, Ola See, and Olive candidates lack a bridge to Henry and Fannie.
  • Dollie Sea/Seay appears as Henry and Fannie’s daughter in 1910. A 1930 Brooks County record places Dollie Seay, age 21, in the same Tallokas household cluster as Jessie W. Seay, where she is indexed as his sister. This supports a likely Dollie/Jessie sibling trail, but it still does not name Henry and Fannie as parents. Later Dollie or Dolly Seay obituary and cemetery material remains derivative or unbridged.
  • Jessie Sea/Seay appears as Henry and Fannie’s infant son in 1910. The adult trail is plausible: Jessie W. Seay appears in Tallokas in 1930 with Dollie Seay nearby; Jesse Seay married Lorene Cobb in Brooks County on 14 January 1932; Jessie/Jesse Seay appears in Brooks County in 1940 with wife Bessie and children, in 1950 in Tallokas with wife Pearl and children, and in the 1966 Georgia death index as Jessie W. Seay, died 2 May 1966 in Brooks County. A fresh FamilySearch parent-search found the 1910 parent-naming census and the same adult candidates, but no adult record extracted so far names Henry and Fannie as his parents.

docs.title: Research Notes
docs.text:
• The earlier entry’s source-exhausted framing is not supported by the current source trail. The status is therefore Source-Researched / not source-exhausted.
  • Henry’s reported birthplace varies: Georgia in 1880 and 1900, Florida in 1910, and Madison, Florida in the 1934 death material.

docs.title: Children and Later Trails
docs.text:
No children are listed in this household in the 1900 census table.

Stephen Swain and Susan Sellers Swain are documented as a couple from their 1873 Mitchell County marriage through the 1910 census in Barney, Brooks County. The confirmed sequence places them in Pearces District, Decatur County, in 1880, then in Barney in both 1900 and 1910. A 1920 Boston, Thomas County census household for Stephen and Susan Swain is probably the same couple, but the record does not name children, parents, or a collateral relative.

The 1900 Barney census is the anchor record for this household. It records Stephen as a farmer, born in Georgia in January 1855, and Susan as his wife, born in Georgia about 1854. The couple had been married 27 years, which fits their 1873 marriage. Susan was recorded with 7 children born and 5 living. James reviewed the 1900 census image and confirmed that no children were enumerated in Stephen and Susan's household.

The 1910 Barney census again places Stephen and Susan together. Stephen was recorded as Stephen W. Suain/Swain, age 55, and Susan as age 53. Their marriage length was recorded as 37 years, again fitting the 1873 marriage. Susan's child count, however, changed to 15 children born and 8 living. The current evidence does not explain that difference. Because no children appear with Stephen and Susan in the confirmed household records, their children cannot be named from the 1880, 1900, or 1910 census alone.

Stephen's parents are not proved by primary records. The Find a Grave memorial for S. W. Swain, memorial ID 24938259, includes a headstone photo at Gornto Cemetery and gives his death date as 10 October 1927. The memorial names Thomas E. B. Swain and Sarah Jane Gilbert as his parents and links apparent siblings John Randolph Swain and Thomas Jefferson Swain. Those names are useful leads and may be described as believed parents, but the parentage still needs proof from probate, guardianship, land, church, death, or another primary record. An 1860 Decatur County Stephen Smain/Swain remains only a possible origin lead. The earlier 1870 Wilcox County Stephen Swain lead is weaker because the Wilcox/Berrien Stephen A. or Stephen Americus Swain trail belongs to a man whose later marriages conflict with HH#163 Stephen's 1873 marriage to Susan Sellers.

Susan Sellers's origin is better developed but still not fully proved. The 1873 Mitchell County marriage record proves her maiden name. James supplied Ancestry census-index images for a likely childhood trail: Susan Cellars, age 6, in the 1850 District 8, Baker County household of Wright and Mary Ann Cellars/Sellers; and Susan Sellers, age 14, in the 1860 Mitchell County household of Wright Sellers and Marianna Sellers. The 1860 Mitchell County placement matters because Susan married Stephen Swain in Mitchell County in 1873. These records support Wright Sellers/Cellars and Mary Ann or Marianna Sellers/Cellars as Susan's believed parents. The relationship is still based on household placement and index inference, not a direct adult record naming her parents.

Susan's 1937 death certificate confirms her late-life trail. The certificate names her as Mrs. Susan Swain, age 82, widowed, and says she died 21 February 1937 at Pavo, Georgia. It names J. P. Jones of Pavo as informant, gives congestive heart failure as the cause of death, and records burial on 22 February 1937 at Campground Cemetery, Morven, Georgia. It does not list her spouse, father, or mother.

docs.title: Connections to Other Barney Families
docs.text:
No children or close relatives are confirmed from the Barney household itself. Possible children need to be developed through separate marriage, death, probate, land, cemetery, obituary, church, or collateral census records that name or otherwise connect them to Stephen and Susan Swain.

Two child or family leads should not be merged into this household without new evidence. A Marion County Stephen/Susan Swain household with children John, Alvertis, Susan, Joseph, and Francis is a separate older couple. A Joseph S. Swain death record names Darling Swain and Elizabeth Spence as his parents, so that Joseph is not evidence for a child of Stephen and Susan Sellers Swain.

docs.text:

  • The 1920 Boston, Thomas County Stephen/Steven Swain and wife Susan household is a probable later appearance, but it still needs a child, neighbor, cemetery, or collateral bridge.
  • Thomas E. B. Swain and Sarah Jane Gilbert are believed parents for Stephen/S. W. Swain from Find a Grave memorial evidence, not primary proof.
  • Wright Sellers/Cellars and Mary Ann or Marianna Sellers/Cellars are believed parents for Susan from the 1850 and 1860 household trail, not direct adult-record proof.
  • The 1860 Decatur County Stephen Smain/Swain remains an origin candidate only.
  • The Wilcox/Berrien Stephen A., Stephen America, or Stephen Americus Swain trail is separate and should not be merged with HH#163.

The 1920 Boston, Thomas County household is a probable continuation. Stephen's burial at Gornto Cemetery is supported by a Find a Grave memorial with a headstone photo. Susan's 1937 death certificate confirms her date and place of death, age, widowhood, informant, burial place, burial date, and cause of death. docs.title: Connections to Other Barney Families
docs.text:
The Henry, Williams, Roberts, and Rountree connections are important but unevenly proved. The Williams link is direct through Peter Henry's 1888 marriage to Hulda Williams. The Roberts link is downgraded to a lead: Roberts household members may still sit near or around the Henry family network, but the marriage record currently extracted does not support calling Hulda a Roberts without additional proof. The Rountree link is strongest through Rosa Rountrie/Rountree in Peter's 1900 household and Huldah Henry's 1920 placement in William Rountree's household. The Roberts link is newly complicated by Huldah/Hulda Hendry's 1930 placement as aunt in Willie Roberts's household; that suggests a possible Roberts-family relationship but still does not prove that Peter's 1888 bride was born or previously known as Hulda Roberts.

The 1900 household includes four adult Henry children: Benjamin, Lucian, Joseph, and Moriah. Lucian/Lucias now has a likely local post-1900 trail: in 1910 he appears as Lucias Hendry, age 40, single son in widowed Huldy Hendry's Barney household, and in 1920 he appears as Lusious Hendry, age 50, single head in Barney. This is strong by name, age, race, and place, but the 1910 mother/son relationship should be read cautiously because Lucian was born before Peter's 1888 marriage to Hulda Williams. Joseph also has a probable local adult trail as Joe/Joseph Hendry/Henry of Barney, husband of Ida Lee Roberts, with records from 1904 through a 1952 Brooks County death-index entry. That trail is promising but still needs original-image review and a parent-naming record if available. Benjamin still lacks a secure adult trail after 1900. A 2026-06-08 targeted search found no proof-level post-1900 Benjamin/Ben Henry/Hendry tied to Peter; the Brooks County tax-digest lead remains weak and the Benj Henry mortality-schedule lead remains conflicting. Moriah/Marin A. now has a candidate adult trail through a 25 December 1901 Brooks County marriage of Mariah Hendry to James Roberts, but the extracted marriage record does not name parents and later Roberts records have not supplied enough continuity to prove she is Peter's daughter. Rosa Rountrie/Rountree also has a stronger but still candidate trail through Rosa L. Rountree's 1903 Lowndes County marriage to Baxter S. Blakeney, 1910/1920/1930/1940 Lowndes County census continuity, James N. Blakeny's 1923 death record naming mother Rosa Rountree, and a 1959 NUMIDENT entry. The trail is coherent, but none of the extracted records name Peter or Hulda/He?lie Henry as Rosa's parents, and the later records give an 1879/1880 birth range rather than the 1900 household's June 1875. Fortinon Brown, listed as mother in 1900, and Fanny Smith, listed as mother-in-law in 1880, remain unresolved identity problems; the 2026-06-08 pass found no independent identity bridge for either woman.

docs.title: Research Notes
docs.text:
• Peter Henry's birthplace and age discrepancies need image-level confirmation across 1870, 1880, and 1900.
  • Peter's death date and burial place are not proved. The current evidence places his death after the 1900 census and before Huldah/Huldy's widowed 1910 enumeration; a 2026-06-08 targeted web/local-corpus pass found no proof-level cemetery, obituary, probate, land/tax, or death-record hit.
  • Argie/Argia's maiden name, parents, marriage, and death are unknown.
  • Fanny Smith's relationship needs clarification. The 1880 census says mother-in-law, but the line could connect through Argie unless another record proves otherwise.
  • Hulda Williams's identity needs follow-up. The older Roberts claim conflicts with current FamilySearch and Ancestry marriage-index extractions; the marriage image and any Williams/Roberts bridge should be checked before using either maiden-name claim as final.
  • Fortinon Brown's relationship to Peter or Hulda is unresolved despite the 1900 relationship field.
  • Benjamin Henry still needs an adult trail after 1900. Moriah/Marin A. Henry has a candidate 1901 Brooks County marriage to James Roberts, but later Roberts continuity and parent-linking evidence remain missing. Lucian/Lucias/Lusious has likely 1910 and 1920 Barney placements, and Joseph/Joe has a probable Barney trail with Ida Lee Roberts, but both trails still need original-image review and parent-linking records if available. The Benj Henry mortality-schedule hit dated December 1879 conflicts with Benjamin's 1880 population-census placement and is only a lead until county/image context is checked. A 2026-06-08 gap pass closed this as a negative search, not a proof resolution: no secure Benjamin, Moriah/Mariah, or Rosa parent-linking record was found beyond the candidate trails already cited.
  • Rosa Rountrie/Rountree has a coherent candidate Rosa L. Rountree / Baxter S. Blakeney trail in Lowndes County from 1903 through 1959, now including 1910, 1920, 1930, and 1940 census continuity, but no direct record yet ties that Rosa to Peter Henry's household or proves the exact Rountree connection.
  • The possible relationship between Joe Hendrey in HH#187 and the Peter Henry family remains only a surname lead.

It also has later placements for widowed Huldy/Huldah Hendry in 1910, 1920, and 1930, a Brooks County death-index lead in 1934, a likely 1910/1920 Lucian-to-Lucias/Lusious Hendry trail, and a probable 1904-1952 Joseph-to-Joe/Joseph Hendry/Henry trail in Barney.

Peter's exact death/burial/probate, Benjamin's adult trail, Moriah/Mariah's parent-linked adult trail, Rosa's parent proof, Argie/Argia's identity, Fanny Smith's exact connection, and Fortinon Brown's identity remain unresolved after targeted negative searches. docs.title: Children and Later Trails
docs.text:
No children are listed in this household in the 1900 census table.

The 1900 household is unusual because Lillie was recorded as a married sixteen-year-old head of household with no husband present. The surviving local source extracts now support the older identification of this woman as Lollie/Lottie Chambers McCoy: FamilySearch marriage-index extracts for Joseph McCoy and Lollie/Lottie Chambers give a Brooks County marriage on 11 March 1900, and the 1910 census places Joe W. McCoy and Lollie McCoy together in Barney with children Georgie, Oma L., Clara B., Gordon, Talmage, and Howard. The marriage date and the 1910 census marriage-duration statement should still be handled cautiously, because the 1910 index says the couple had been married eleven years, while the indexed marriage date is March 1900.

Lillie/Lollie’s parentage is supported by the FamilySearch death-index extract for Mrs. J. W. McCoy, wife of Joseph William McCoy. It records her death on 17 December 1928 in District 637, Thomas County, Georgia, age forty-four, born Georgia, certificate #34540, and lists James Chambers and Nettie Webb as other people on the record. That supports the connection to James G. Chambers of HH#198. A saved FamilySearch image-page screenshot exists for the death certificate, but the OCR is imperfect; the indexed extract is currently the clearer local source.

Joseph William McCoy’s identity is now stronger than in the older entry. FamilySearch and Ancestry extracts give a 1 February 1883 birth date, with the WWI draft registration placing the birth in Brooks County, Georgia and naming Lollie McCoy as spouse in the Ancestry extract. The 1900 Ancestry census extract places Joe McCoy, born February 1883, as a son in John and Hester McCoy’s household, and the FamilySearch NUMIDENT extract names Joseph William McCoy’s parents as John B. McCoy and Hester A. Strickland. This gives direct support for the HH#117 John Buck McCoy and HH#32 William M. C. McCoy cross-volume line, though the HH#117/HH#32 entries should remain the main place for the full parentage chain.

There were no children in Lillie’s 1900 household. The child trails belong to the continuing Joe and Lollie/Katie McCoy family documented in later records. The 1910 census records Joe and Lollie with six children. The 1920 census records Joe W. and wife Katie, likely the same woman under a variant or indexing problem, with Belle, Gordon, Talmage, Howard, Rosie, Agnis, and Herman. By 1930, after Lollie’s 1928 death, Joe appears with wife Mary, son Herman, daughter Rosa M., son Carden/Gordon, and Manning stepchildren or household children. In 1940, Joe W. McCoy is in George B. and Clara Hunt’s Brooks County household as father-in-law, with Stella McCoy also present. In 1950, widowed Joseph W. McCoy is in St. Petersburg, Pinellas County, Florida, as father of Arthur H. McCoy. A Florida death-index extract records Joseph W. McCoy’s death in Pinellas County in February 1965, certificate #10042.

docs.title: Continuing family / child trails
docs.text:
Child or lead Evidence currently in the trail Status Georgie / Belle McCoy Georgie appears in the 1910 Joe/Lollie household, age 10. The prior 1928 Patt/Patt Jenkins lead resolves to Agnes McCoy, not Georgie/Belle. A separate 1916 Georgie Mae McCoy/Watt Jenkins marriage and 1920/1930/1940 Georgia Jenkins census chain in Colquitt County is a strong candidate trail, but the visible extracts reviewed so far do not name her parents. The 1920 Joe W. McCoy household’s “Belle” should not automatically be treated as Georgie; she may be Clara Belle or another name-form issue pending original-image review. No direct record supports a Georgie C. Richardson identity. Strengthened candidate trail; not fully closed until parent-naming/original-image or death/obituary proof is reviewed. Oma L. / Oma Lee McCoy Jones Oma L. appears in 1910, age 8. FamilySearch marriage extraction records Oma Lee McCoy marrying Calvin Jones in Brooks County on 20 November 1919, and a NUMIDENT child-link extract names Oma L. McCoy as spouse of Calvin Jones and mother of William Claude/William C. Jones. Strengthened adult trail; Oma Lee's own death record still needed. Clara B. McCoy Hunt Clara B. appears in 1910, age 6. A FamilySearch marriage extract records Clara Belle McCoy marrying George B. Hunt in Colquitt County on 5 July 1924. The 1940 Brooks County census places Joe W. McCoy as father-in-law in George B. Hunt’s household with Clara Hunt, and later NUMIDENT/obituary-linked child extracts support the Clara Belle McCoy/George B. Hunt family cluster. Strong adult trail; Clara's own death/obit still needed. John Gordon / Carden McCoy Gordon appears in 1910 and Gorden appears in 1920. The 1930 extract lists Carden McCoy, age 24, in Joe’s household, likely the same son under a name/index variant. FamilySearch extracts now continue him as Gordon/John G. McCoy in 1940/1950 with Trudie/Trudy Cone McCoy and support death/burial through death-index, NUMIDENT-style, and Find A Grave index records. This man should not be merged with the unrelated military record for Gordon H. McCoy born in Murfreesboro, Tennessee. Strong adult trail; direct death certificate needed because the extracted death evidence conflicts between May 1951 and May 1952. Talmage McCoy Appears in 1910 and 1920. A 2026-06-09 FamilySearch search pass found possible W. T., Robert T., Lee T., and muster-roll leads, but none was parent-linked to Joe and Lollie. The 1919 muster-roll lead is suspicious because HH#166 Talmage was only about 10–12 then. Open; adult identity not currently closeable. Howard / William Howard McCoy Howard appears in 1910 and 1920. A FamilySearch marriage extract records Wm Howard Mc Coy, age 25, son of Lollie McCoy and Joe W. McCoy, marrying Oleta Rogers at Berlin, Colquitt County, Georgia, on 14 March 1934. Browser-backed FamilySearch follow-up found NUMIDENT child-link records naming William H. McCoy with wife Nina/Oleta Rogers and children Patricia Ann Bennett and Remer/Reamer Joe McCoy. A focused 2026-06-09 public/newspaper search found no proof-level death/obit/burial hit. Strengthened adult-family continuation; Howard's own death/obituary still open. Rosa / Rosie M. McCoy Glow Rosie appears in 1920 and Rosa M. appears in Joe’s 1930 household. A FamilySearch marriage extract records Rosa Mae McCoy, age 24, daughter of Lollie McCoy and J. W. McCoy, marrying Colbert Glow in District 1151, Colquitt County, on 22 December 1934. A focused 2026-06-09 public/newspaper search found no proof-level later census/death/obit/burial hit. Strengthened adult trail; later census/death still open. Agnes / Agnis McCoy Jenkins Agnis appears as a daughter in 1920, age 6. A FamilySearch marriage extract records Agnes McCoy, age 18, daughter of Lollie McCoy and Joe McCoy, marrying Patt Jenkins in District 1151, Colquitt County, on 2 September 1928. A focused 2026-06-09 public/newspaper search found no proof-level later census/death/obit/burial hit. Strengthened; later census/death still open; the older A. H. McCoy/Fay Lewis groom lead is not used for this daughter and should be treated cautiously. Arthur Herman McCoy Herman appears as a young son in 1920 and 1930. A FamilySearch WWII draft-registration extract identifies Arthur Herman McCoy, born 26 February 1914 in Brooks County, and the 1950 census places Joseph W. McCoy in Arthur H. McCoy’s St. Petersburg household as father. Browser-backed FamilySearch follow-up extracted NUMIDENT 6KSB-Q311VV73-2DH for Arthur Herman Mccoy, born 06 Feb 1914, died 9 Nov 1972 in Pinellas County, Florida, certificate #76029. Strong adult trail with index-level death evidence; parent/spouse-naming death certificate or obituary still needed.

Mary Studstill remains unresolved. The 1900 boarder was about 24 and born in Georgia. Candidate review rejects Mrs. Mary S. Studstill, born about 1845, as too old; Mary E. Studstill in Wilcox County and Mollie Studstill in Berrien County are age-compatible but not tied directly to Brooks/Barney or to McCoy/Chambers records. Lollie Chambers McCoy's sister Vesta Chambers later married/lived with Hugh Studstill in Valdosta, but that is contextual only and too late to identify the 1900 boarder. Mary should be treated as an associated boarder, not as a proven relative of Lillie or Joseph.

docs.title: Household identity and correction
docs.text:
Isom Barney Ingram was a White farmer in the Barney district of Brooks County in 1900. This household should not be merged with Walter Benjamin Ingram of Monroe County; that earlier association was a separate-family conflation.

Barney appears in earlier records as Isam B. Ingram in 1870 and Icoum B. Ingram in 1880. Those records place him in Berrien County, Georgia, in the household of John L. Ingram and Martha A. Ingram. By 1900 he was living in Brooks County with his wife, America, and nine children. A 1906 Valdosta obituary reports that Barney died near Barney after a 25-day illness with typhoid fever and left a wife and eleven children. The obituary also names his brother as G. W. Ingram of Adel, tying Barney back to the John L. and Martha A. Ingram family cluster.

Annie America Folsom is supported as Barney's wife by the 9 November 1884 Berrien County marriage record for America Folsom and Barney Ingram, the 1900 household, the 1910 and 1920 widow-household trail, and her 1923 Brooks County death certificate. Her death record names her father as William Folsom and her mother only as Martha; the mother’s maiden surname is not supplied on the original. It names I. B. Ingram as spouse and records Mt. Zion Cemetery, not the combined Camp Ground / Mt. Zion wording. The relationship between those cemetery names needs separate evidence. The Folsom and Ingram families were near one another in Berrien County's District 1311 in 1880.

docs.title: 1910 widow household
docs.text:
By 1910 Barney had died and America appears as a widow, indexed as America Ingham. The household includes eleven children: John, William L., Del B., Walter W., Mattie, Charlie B., Georgie A., Nina, Tennis M., Lonla/Lula M., and Annie B. The surname is a transcription error, but the children's names, ages, and location match the Ingram household.

The 1910 household contains eleven children, but that later household count is not a list of the children living when Barney died in 1906. The 1910 original separately reports twelve children born and twelve living; the 1907 support petition reports twelve unnamed minors. These statements are retained separately from the obituary’s eleven survivors. Annie B., age 3 in 1910, may be a posthumous or near-posthumous child, but a precise birth record is still needed before using her to revise the child count beyond the obituary and census framework. Her inspected marriage does not supply that date.

docs.title: Children and later trails
docs.text: Child Current evidence assessment Minnie / Ninnie Ingram Holloway Original death and direct niece bridge inspected. The earlier marriage/census trail is now supplemented by the 1974 original certificate and a 1965 obituary naming Audrey Bernice Holloway Jones as Ninnie’s daughter and Mattie Ingram’s niece. The certificate itself—not just the index—uses Holloway for both parents’ surnames. Preserve that source conflict; do not silently correct it. John Ingram Parent-naming application index added. The Social Security Applications and Claims Index names Isom B. Ingram and Annie A. Folsom, with September 10, 1887 birth in Berrien. The inspected 1917 draft original and photographed marker agree on that birth date; the 1950 Ty Ty original lists wife Nancy E. The underlying application and original civil death certificate remain uninspected; the earlier census sequence is retained as supporting continuity, not newly rechecked in full. William Lee Ingram Census-confirmed child. He appears as William in 1900 and William L. in 1910, with later local 1920 and 1930 Brooks County household evidence with wife Beulah. Find a Grave gives William Lee Ingram, 1889-1947. Oel Barnes / Dell / Del B. / Pal Ingram Closed at high confidence. The chain connects 1900 Pal, 1910 Del B., 1920 Dell Barnes with wife Viola and daughter Alice, 1930-1950 continuation with Viola and children, WWI draft and service records for Oel/Oel Barnes Ingram, VA Master Index, Georgia death index, military headstone application, Social Security, and Barwick Cemetery burial. Walter Washington / Walter W. Ingram Closed at high confidence. The trail connects 1900 Walter, 1910 Walter W., the 1917 Brooks County marriage of W. W. Ingram to Willer Page Humphery, 1920 W. W. with wife Willie Page and daughter Lenora, 1930-1950 Florida census continuity, a WWII draft-card middle-name bridge, California death index, and Rose Hills burial. Mattie Louise / Mattie L. Ingram Closed at high confidence. The chain connects 1900 Mattie, 1910 Mattie, probable 1920 Macon nurse Louise Ingram, 1930-1950 Beaufort nurse records, 1940 and 1950 sister placements with the Holloway/Ninnie line, Cadet Nursing Corps/public-health evidence, SSDI, Find a Grave, and a 1972 South Carolina death record naming father Isom B. Ingram and mother Annie America. Charles Benton / Charlie B. Ingram Direct adult parent bridge added. The original 1975 Virginia death certificate for Charles Benton Ingram names Barney Ingram and Annie America Ingram as parents; June 23, 1896 birth fits Charley’s June 1896 entry. Mattie’s 1972 obituary names brother Charlie of Falls Church, matching his later residence. The C. B. Ingram informant on Annie’s 1923 certificate still has no explicit kinship label there. Georgia / Georgie A. Ingram Competing surname evidence remains open. Mattie’s inspected 1972 obituary prints Georgia Proudfoot of “Odell.” A probable Georgia Ingram Bradford trail now has an original daughter’s marriage naming her maiden surname, a 1920 Cook household, and a marker whose July 1898 birth agrees with this child’s 1900 month/year. A direct parent-naming adult record is still needed before fully assigning that trail or explaining the newspaper discrepancy. Nina Ingram Adult trail strongly supported. Mattie’s 1972 obituary names sister Nina Barrs of Quitman. The original 1950 Brooks census places Nina, 50, with husband Edward Barrs; an inspected Oak Hill marker reads Nina I. Barrs, March 19, 1900–December 30, 1987, and the Georgia death index agrees on the death date. A direct marriage record and original death certificate remain open. Tennis / Tennie / Tennys Ingram Knight Married identity strongly supported. The inspected 1930 original places Tennie M.,28, as William L. Ingram’s sister. An October 17, 1930 Brooks marriage joins Tinnis Ingram and Douglas Knight; the 1950 original places Tenny,48, with Douglas and their children. The marker reads Tennys Ingram Knight, December 14, 1901–November 20, 1983, agreeing with the death index on death date. Her own original civil death certificate and a parent-naming adult original remain open. Lula / Lonla M. Ingram Original marriage and parent-naming notices added. Lula Mae Ingram married William Claude Webb on December 18, 1932, according to the original return and contemporary announcement. The announcement names the late Mr. and Mrs. Barney Ingram of Barney as parents. Her original 1998 obituary names Isom Barney and Annie America Folsom Ingram, reports November 19, 1904 birth and December 17, 1998 death. The original 1950 Columbus household and Mattie’s sibling notice support continuity; civil death and completed burial confirmation remain open. Annie B. Ingram Original marriage and adult household added. Annie B. Ingram married Homer Howard December 23, 1926, in the original Brooks register. Their 1950 Brooks household lists Annie, 43, with Homer, 44. Mattie’s obituary names Annie Howard of Quitman as sister. A precise birth date, parent-naming adult record, death and burial still remain open; posthumous birth is not established.

docs.title: Adult parent and sibling bridges
docs.text:
The original Virginia death certificate for Charles Benton Ingram, state file 75-034720, records death November 24, 1975 at Northern Virginia Doctors Hospital in Arlington, usual residence Falls Church, age 79, and June 23, 1896, Georgia, birth. It names Barney Ingram and Annie America Ingram as parents, Helen Duke Ingram as wife and informant, and Oaklawn Cemetery, Fort Valley, Georgia, as burial place. The parent names and birth month/year bridge the adult to Charley in this household. The certificate’s military notation is not a substitute for a service record.

The original South Carolina death certificate for Mattie L. Ingram, 72-001775, records January 29, 1972, Beaufort, death, April 6, 1895, Georgia, birth, age 76, never married, occupation nurse, and parents Isom B. Ingram and Annie America, with Folsom also entered in the mother’s maiden-name field. It records burial January 31 in Beaufort Memorial Gardens. The informant’s handwritten surname remains uncertain and is not expanded here.

Mattie’s February 3, 1972 Beaufort Gazette obituary, page 11, was read directly. It calls her a Barney native and retired nurse, gives age 77 rather than the certificate’s 76, and names these survivors:

Relationship to Mattie Name and place as printed What this establishes Sister Nina Barrs, Quitman Direct sibling statement and adult surname Sister Annie Howard, Quitman Direct sibling statement; husband’s given name not supplied Sister Mrs. M. A. Holloway, Beaufort Supports the earlier Holloway family trail; no expansion from initials alone Sister Lula Webb, Columbus Direct sibling statement and adult surname Sister Georgia Proudfoot, “Odell” Direct sibling statement; printed place not silently changed to Adel Brother Charlie Ingram, Falls Church, Virginia Connects the sibling group to Charles’s later residence

The notice reports the funeral already held Monday at Carteret Street Methodist Church, followed by burial in Beaufort Memorial Gardens. It does not say February 7; the death certificate supplies the January 31 burial date. A survivor list is not a complete list of every child born or proof of when unlisted siblings died.

For Nina, the 1950 original, Brooks ED 14-1, sheet 20, lines 22–28, lists Edward Barrs, 49, wife Nina, 50, and four children, with Mamie, 76, recorded as mother of the head, not Nina’s mother. Nina is a primary-grade teacher. Her age, locality and sibling notice support this identification. The photographed marker at memorial 140812774 reads Nina I. Barrs / March 19, 1900 / Dec. 30, 1987; Oak Hill Cemetery attribution comes from the memorial catalog, not words on the stone. Georgia’s death index independently indexes December 30, 1987, Brooks death and residence, age 87. The original civil death certificate has not been obtained.

A suggested 1923 marriage of Nina Barrs to Eston L. Milton is not assigned to Nina Ingram Barrs. Likewise, a Social Security parent-role entry for Flora N. Ingram is a derived lead, not a basis by itself to expand Nina’s name. Bounded marriage searches did not locate a secure Nina Ingram–Barrs or Georgia Ingram–Proudfoot entry; this is not proof that those records do not exist.

docs.title: Georgia: a probable Bradford trail, with the discrepancy retained
docs.text:
Mattie’s 1972 notice was re-inspected: it really prints Georgia Proudfoot of “Odell.” Neither word is silently corrected. The following Bradford evidence is stronger than the earlier AI-only lead, but is presented as a probable trail, not a completed parentage proof.

The 1920 original, River Bend, Cook County, ED 78, sheet14A, lines 2–3, lists O. J. Bradford, 20, head, and Georgia, 21, wife, both Georgia-born. The original 1946 Lucas County, Ohio, marriage record, page 78, no. 156633, for Evelyn E. Bradford Drought and Richard C. Bechtol, names Evelyn’s father Oscar J. Bradford and mother’s maiden name Georgia Ingram. License and ceremony are dated February 21, 1946. This is the daughter’s marriage, not Georgia’s own marriage and not a record naming Georgia’s parents.

The photographed marker at memorial 36868602 reads Georgia Bradford / July 5, 1898 / Jan. 9, 1988. The 1900 original gives this household’s daughter Georgia July 1898 birth. The match in name, maiden surname, birth month/year and nearby Cook locality makes the Bradford identification probable. It does not, by itself, explain Proudfoot or prove that “Odell” meant Adel. Antioch Cemetery, Adel, is the memorial’s catalog attribution, not wording on the stone.

The Georgia death index gives Georgia E. Bradford, 89, death and residence in Cook County, January 9, 1988, filed January 14. The original civil certificate remains uninspected. A suggested 1973 Harry Bradford obituary is another parent-role lead; its source image 889622668 returned “page … not found” and was not read.

Two Social Security candidates—Georgia Bradford born November 27, 1897 and Georgia B. Ingram born June 23, 1897—lack the necessary parent/locality bridge and remain unassigned. A search-result candidate Georgia Evelyn Bradford with July 5, 1898 birth but February 5, 1988 death also remains unassigned pending record-level reconciliation. Bounded Georgia/Oscar marriage searches did not locate their own original entry in the reviewed results; no absence is claimed.

docs.title: Tennie / Tennys Ingram Knight: the later trail
docs.text:
The 1930 original, Brooks ED 14-17, sheet 13B, lines 53–63, lists Tennie M. Ingram, 28, single, sister of head William L. Ingram, with his wife Beulah and children. The occupation/industry cells contain overwriting; the earlier clean description “private-school teacher” should not be treated as an exact settled transcription.

A May 25, 1930 Florida Times-Union notice, page 31, Jasper column, says Miss Tennys Ingram, who had been teaching at Barney, Georgia, was visiting “her brother and sister, Mr. and Mrs. W. W. Ingram.” This is direct contemporary support for her teaching and a family visit, but the initials alone are not expanded to a full identity here.

The original Brooks white marriage register, Book F, right second entry, names Douglas Knight and Miss Tinnis Ingram, with license and ceremony October 17, 1930. The groom’s handwritten middle initial is not resolved here; the index reads W. The recording date is blank. The entry supplies no parents.

The 1950 original, Brooks ED 14-1, sheet 10, line 30, begins the household with Douglas Knight, 52, farmer. Sheet 11, lines 1–4, continues with wife Tenny, 48, daughter Charlotte, 15, son Wade, 9, and daughter June, 7. Both pages were inspected; the head is not inferred from the index alone.

The photographed marker at memorial 43226328 reads Tennys Ingram Knight / Dec. 14, 1901 / Nov. 20, 1983. “Myrtle,” birthplace, and Columbia Primitive Baptist Church Cemetery at Nankin are catalog details, not wording on the stone. The Georgia death index gives November 20, 1983, Brooks death and residence, age 81, filed November 21. The original civil certificate has not been inspected.

A Social Security parent-role entry names Tennys M. Ingram and D. W. Knight as parents of Robert Wade Knight. It is not Tennys’s own application or a record naming her parents. The age/name/locality sequence, original marriage and household evidence strongly support the adult identity, but the remaining parent-naming original gap stays open.

The AI-indexed November 21,1983 Valdosta Daily Times obituary points to image908926194, which returned “page … not found” twice. That route was stopped. Its Georgia Bradford sibling claim remains UNVERIFIED and does not override the inspected 1972 wording Proudfoot. Tennys’s omission from Mattie’s 1972 survivor list is not proof that Tennys was then deceased.

docs.title: John Ingram: parent-naming index and original checks
docs.text:
The Social Security Applications and Claims Index entry gives September 10, 1887, Berrien, Georgia, birth, parents Isom B. Ingram and Annie A. Folsom, and a March 1941 name entry. This is an extracted administrative index, not the original application; the SS-5 has not been inspected. It substantially strengthens the adult-to-child identification without closing the original-document gap.

The original WWI draft card records John Inghram, 29, resident Barney, born September 10, 1887, Adel, farmer, single, with mother and sisters dependent on him. The registrar’s report is dated June 5, 1917. No mother or sister is named there, and registration does not prove military service.

The 1950 original, Ty Ty, Tift County, ED 137-5, sheet 11, lines 26–27, lists John, 62, farmer, with wife Nancy E., 55, both Georgia-born. The name Nancy E. is retained as written; this inspection alone does not expand it to Elizabeth or independently establish the marriage. “Own business” in the work column is not a land-title statement.

The photographed marker at memorial 118092789 reads John Ingram / Sept. 10, 1887 / Feb. 13, 1954. Oak Ridge Cemetery, Tifton, is the catalog attribution, not wording on the stone. The Georgia death index reports February 13, 1954 death and residence in Tift, age 67. That age differs from the marker/application birth date, which would make him 66; the original civil certificate is still needed.

Bounded marriage and obituary searches did not produce an assigned original in the reviewed slices. A suggested 1945 Kokomo marriage notice naming a child Comer Y. Ingram and suggested Indiana records remain unassigned, not additions to this Georgia family.

docs.title: Ninnie Ingram Holloway: original certificate and a niece bridge
docs.text:
The original South Carolina death certificate, 74-003474, records February 21, 1974, Beaufort Memorial Hospital, death; January 8, 1886, Georgia, birth; age 88; widowed; and residence at Bay View Nursing Home in Beaufort. It records February 23 burial in Beaufort Memorial Gardens. The informant is Mrs. W. R. Cochran, with a Savannah address; no relationship is written in that field.

The parent fields actually read “Isom Barney Holloway” and “Folsom, Annie America Holloway.” The earlier suggestion that the father’s surname was merely an indexing problem is withdrawn. These are anomalous original entries, not new evidence that Barney’s surname was Holloway. The broader identity chain and independent parent-naming records for other children remain necessary.

The June 3, 1965 Beaufort Gazette, page 2, obituary headed “Mrs. John G. Jones” identifies Audrey Bernice Holloway Jones as a Barney-born daughter of Ninnie Ingram Holloway and the late Matthew Holloway. It names Miss Mattie Ingram of Beaufort as her aunt. Audrey died May 26; the notice reports the funeral already held and burial in Beaufort Memorial Gardens. It also names daughter Mrs. W. R. (Sue) Cochran of Anchorage. That name is a useful lead for the later informant, but a shared married name alone does not establish that the 1974 Savannah informant was the same person.

Additional bounded searches did not resolve Georgia’s Proudfoot/Bradford discrepancy or locate Ninnie’s own 1974 obituary. Only the recorded result slices were reviewed; these are not claims that the records do not exist.

docs.title: Lula Mae Ingram Webb: marriage and later life
docs.text:
The original Webster County white marriage register, Book A, page 96, middle entry, names William Claude Webb and Lula Ingram. The license is December 11, 1932, but the ceremony return says December 18; recording followed January 6, 1933. The searchable index’s December 11 date is the license date, not the recorded ceremony.

The January 1, 1933 Macon Telegraph, page 13, confirms a December 18 wedding in Cordele, at the home of Mr. and Mrs. P. M. Strickland. It explicitly calls Lula Mae the daughter of the late Mr. and Mrs. Barney Ingram of Barney. The January 1 publication date is not the wedding date. The photograph headed “Attractive Bride” beside this article belongs to a different notice and is not a portrait of Lula.

The announcement reports a University of Georgia education and home-demonstration work, describing “Baker county, with headquarters at Preston.” That county/place wording has not been independently resolved. It describes William Claude as stationed in San Diego with Navy aviation; this newspaper statement is not an inspected service record.

The 1950 original, Columbus ED 162-46, sheet 76, lines 16–19, lists William C., 46—not the index’s 16—his wife, 44, daughter Nancy A., 12, and nephew Jack Knight, 18. The wife is a welfare worker. Her reported age differs from the later November 1904 birth date and is retained rather than recalculated.

Her December 19, 1998 Ledger-Enquirer obituary, page 31, reports December 17 death at Sumter Regional Hospital in Americus, age 94, and November 19, 1904 birth in Brooks County. It names parents Isom Barney Ingram and Annie America Folsom Ingram, surviving husband William Claude Webb, and daughter Nancy Webb Petras. It reports teaching and home-demonstration work in Stewart and Webster counties. The notice announces a service at the Chapel of the Pines Mausoleum in Parkhill Cemetery, Columbus; prospective arrangements are not proof of completed burial. The original civil death certificate has not been inspected.

docs.title: Annie B. Ingram Howard: a separate Howard household
docs.text:
The original Brooks white marriage register, Book F, left second entry, records Homer Howard and Miss Annie B. Ingram, license and ceremony December 23, 1926, recorded April 8, 1927. It supplies no parents.

The 1950 original, Brooks ED 14-1, sheet 2, lines 8–12, lists Homer, 44, Annie B., 43, Sara E., 12, Don, 10, and Ora, 86, mother of the head. Ora is not identified as Annie’s mother. The marriage, age/locality sequence and Mattie’s direct sibling notice strongly support this adult trail, but do not supply an exact birth date or establish posthumous birth.

A separate 1950 Brooks entry for Annie B., about 47, with T. S. Howard is not merged here. A suggested death-index entry for Annie B. Howard, 71, in Whitfield County with Murray residence in 1975 is also unassigned. Bounded cemetery searches did not establish a secure burial for Annie or Homer; no cemetery absence is claimed.

docs.title: Connections to Other Barney Families
docs.text:
The 1870 and 1880 Berrien County records place Barney with John L. Ingram and Martha A. Ingram. The 1880 sibling group includes George W. Ingram, Martha J. Ingram, William J. Ingram, William W. Ingram, Nancy P. Ingram, and John G. Ingram. George W. is especially important because Barney's 1906 obituary names G. W. Ingram of Adel as his brother.

The strongest confirmed nearby connection is HH#169, John Giles Ingram, another son of John L. and Martha A. Ingram. HH#161 George W. Ingram may be part of the broader Ingram network, but the precise connection should not be assumed without renewed proof in that entry.

docs.title: Original record reconciliation
docs.text:
The 1884 Berrien marriage entry, no. 448, names Barney Ingram and America Folsom, with a November 7 license and November 9, 1884 ceremony. It names no parents. This differs from the marriage year estimated from fifteen years married in the 1900 census.

The 1900 original, ED 9, sheet 9 A, lines 6–16, reports America, 33, born December 1866, with nine children born and nine living. The 1910 original, ED 21, sheet 13 A, lines 12–23, reports America, 41, widowed, with twelve born and twelve living. These are source statements, not independently proved birth histories.

The July 13, 1906 newspaper, page 4, was re-inspected. “Mr. Barney Ingram Dead” reports age 42, death near Barney “last Friday morning” after twenty-five days of typhoid fever, wife and eleven children, brother G. W. Ingram of Adel, and burial at the camp ground near Morven. The item is credited to the Adel News, so the relative phrase is not treated as an independently dated original report. The support petition below supplies an explicit July 6 date. The brother in this notice is not automatically George W. of household 161, whose separate estate reports a 1903 death.

The 1923 original death certificate, file 34150, calls her Mrs. Annie A. Ingram, widowed, spouse I. B. Ingram, and records December 8, 1923 death in Barney, Brooks County. It gives December 31, 1865, Berrien County, as birth, age 57 years 11 months, father William Folsom and mother Martha. Her birth date differs from the 1900 entry and her 1910 age. Informant C. B. Ingram of Carrollton has no relationship label on this certificate; it does not by itself prove that he is her son Charles. Burial is recorded December 9 at Mt. Zion Cemetery. The original says widowed, unlike the index’s married classification.

docs.title: Related probate records
docs.text:
The original twelve-month-support register, Book B, pages 72–73, names Mrs. America Ingram as widow of I. B. Ingram, reports his death on July 6, 1906, and states twelve minor children, without naming them. The administrator, recorded as F. B. Walker, acknowledges notice January 7, 1907. The initials, date, place, business activity, and public role make Fleming Bates Walker the strong-probable identification. The appraisers sign January 9, and the court admits their report as its judgment at the February 4, 1907 term.

The support is valued at $4,868, including 245 acres, more or less, in lot 371, land district 12, Brooks County, described as the Ingram home place, with livestock, crops, equipment, cash and household/kitchen furniture. The boundary text mentions a branch, but its name has not been securely transcribed here. This is a support award, not the administrator’s deed, a purchase price, or a complete title chain.

America’s name, her widow status, the 1906 death, and Walker's administration provide a stronger bridge to this household than I. B. initials alone. The award does not name the children or settle the twelve-versus-eleven count. The separate estate sale concerns 190 acres in lot 414, not the lot 371 home place. Neither record identifies lot 523 or proves that these parcels were the same.

docs.title: Research Notes
docs.text:
• Original counts now inspected: 1900 nine born/nine living; 1910 twelve/twelve. Reconcile these with the 1906 eleven-survivor notice and 1907 twelve-minor petition without assuming a complete named child list.
  • Georgia’s 1972 Proudfoot wording has been rechecked. A probable Bradford trail now has original daughter-marriage and census support, but needs a parent-naming adult record and explanation of the printed surname/place discrepancy.
  • Nina’s marriage and original civil death remain open. Lula’s original marriage and parent-naming notices are now inspected; her civil death and completed burial still need confirmation. Annie’s marriage and 1950 household are inspected, but her precise birth, death, burial and parent-naming adult evidence remain open.
  • John’s parent-naming Social Security application index strengthens the adult trail; the underlying application and original civil death certificate remain uninspected.
  • Tennis/Tennie M. Ingram has a strong 1930 sister placement with William L. Ingram, but her later adult trail remains incomplete.
  • John L. Ingram's pre-1850 parentage remains undocumented in the current source trail.
  • Mattie’s 1972 certificate has been re-inspected; the informant’s handwritten surname remains uncertain. Preserve its age76 versus obituary77 conflict.

docs.title: Military Service
docs.text: Pal Ingram, the eight-year-old son in 1900, is identified at high confidence as Oel Barnes, Dell, or Del B. Ingram. His adult trail includes World War I draft and service records, a Georgia service card, VA Master Index, Georgia death index, and a military headstone application. Those records make his military-service trail part of the household's later history.

docs.title: Open Research Questions
docs.text: • Resolve the open items flagged in Research Notes above with direct records before expanding this household narrative.

docs.title: Research Status
docs.text:
• Status: Source-Researched, not Source-Exhausted.
  • Strengths: The head couple, marriage, 1870-1900 identity chain, 1906 obituary, Annie America's 1923 death record, 1900/1910 child framework, and several adult-child trails are now well supported. Minnie/Ninnie, Oel Barnes/Dell, Walter Washington, and Mattie Louise are closed at high confidence. John now has a parent-naming Social Security application index, with original draft and later census checks. Charles Benton now has an original parent-naming death certificate; William Lee retains the earlier later-life support.
  • Remaining cautions: Georgia’s Proudfoot/Bradford discrepancy, Nina Barrs and Annie Howard still need the remaining vital-record links; Lula’s marriage and parent-naming death notice are now inspected, with civil death/burial confirmation open; Tennys’s parent-naming original/civil death certificate, John’s original application/death certificate, child-count reconciliation, and John L. Ingram's earlier parentage remain open.

docs.title: Household #169: Ingram, John Giles
docs.text:
Back to the 1900 Census & Household Index

In the 1900 Barney census, Melis Ingram headed a 2-person household. The table below preserves the exact names, relationships, ages, birthplaces, and occupations recorded for the household.

docs.title: Household Snapshot
docs.text:
Melis Ingram headed a 2-person household in the 1900 Barney census with 1 spouse or marital partner.

Melis Ingram's listed occupation was Laborer Farm.

All listed household members were reported as born in Georgia.

docs.title: Newspaper and Public-Record Trail
docs.text: This section flags public-record leads separate from the census table. The detailed discussion stays in the family narrative, research status, and source citations below.

docs.title: 1900 Census Household
docs.text: Name Relation Age Birthplace Occupation Melis Ingram Head 21 Georgia Laborer Farm Della Ingram Wife 20 Georgia —

docs.title: Children and Later Trails
docs.text:
No children are listed in this household in the 1900 census table.

The 1900 name "Melis" is best treated as a phonetic or enumerator rendering of Giles/Miles. The surrounding record trail identifies the head as John Giles Ingram Sr. The household was newly married in 1900, so the later children are documented through subsequent records rather than through the Barney enumeration itself.

docs.title: Household identity and correction
docs.text:
John Giles Ingram Sr. was born in January 1879 according to the 1900 census. His World War I draft registration gives the fuller date 15 January 1879 and lists DeSoto County, Florida as birthplace. The federal censuses consistently place his birth in Georgia, so the Florida birthplace should be noted as a record conflict rather than resolved fact.

The identity chain is strong across the 1880, 1900, 1910, 1930, 1935, 1940, and 1950 records. In 1880 he appears as John G. Ingram, age 1, in the Berrien County household of John L. Ingram and Martha A. Ingram. In 1900 he appears in Barney as Melis Ingram with wife Della. In 1910 he is John G. Ingram in Robinson, Colquitt County, Georgia. Later records use J.G., John D., and John G. Ingram in Florida. The World War I draft registration supplies the full name John Giles Ingram.

John died in Hardee County, Florida, in 1950 and is buried at Oak Ridge Cemetery, Arcadia, DeSoto County, Florida. His Find a Grave memorial is #51109505.

docs.title: Della Florence Kennedy Ingram
docs.text:
Della Florence Kennedy was born 17 November 1878 and died 26 June 1949 in Hardee County, Florida. She is buried with John at Oak Ridge Cemetery, Arcadia, DeSoto County, Florida. Her Find a Grave memorial is #51260353.

Her maiden name is supported by the Social Security Applications and Claims Index entry for daughter Mildred Ingram Brewer, which identifies Mildred's parents as John G. Ingram and Della F. Kennedy. Della's parents were Samuel G. Kennedy, who died in 1879, and Mary A. D. Martin, who died in 1880. Two guardianship records document the Kennedy children after their parents' deaths: an 1880 Stewart County record and an 1886 Thomas County record. Those records place Della, also called Florence, among the Kennedy children.

John and Della married about 1899, based on the 1900 census statement that they had been married one year. No separate marriage record has been cited in this entry.

docs.title: Children and later trails
docs.text:
The later family is well documented through census records and cemetery memorials. All ten children are identified in the current source trail.

Her Social Security Applications and Claims record confirms Della's Kennedy maiden name. John Giles Ingram Jr. Born 1921, died 2010; Find a Grave #65735233. docs.title: Connections to Other Barney Families
docs.text:
John Giles Ingram was a son of John L. Ingram and Martha A. Ingram of Berrien County. The 1880 sibling group includes Icoum B. Ingram, George W. Ingram, Martha J. Ingram, William J. Ingram, William W. Ingram, Nancy P. Ingram, and John G. Ingram.

HH#168, Isom Barney Ingram, is the clearest nearby household connection. The 1880 census places Barney and John Giles in the same parental household, and Barney's 1906 obituary names G. W. Ingram of Adel as Barney's brother. This supports the John L. and Martha A. Ingram family cluster used in both HH#168 and HH#169.

docs.text:

docs.title: Family Narrative
docs.text:
• John A. Hiers/Hires was enumerated as John Hines in Barney in 1900 with wife Francis and five children. The 1900 record gives his birth as October 1855 and says he and Francis had been married 11 years.
  • The same family appears in Barney in 1910 as John Hires and Francis Hires, with children Mollie, Vessie/Bessie, Lettie, Lebbie, Robert, Stella, Nina, and Ocalla. The 1910 census is the strongest bridge between the 1900 Hines spelling and the later Hires/Hiers spellings.
  • In 1920, John A. Hires and Francis Renore Hires were still in Barney. Children at home were Ocala, Bessie, Bob, Libbie, Leddie, and Ruby.
  • John died on 15 November 1921 in Barney, Brooks County, Georgia. The FamilySearch Georgia deaths record names him John A. Hires, age 66, married, with father Phillip Hires, mother Francis Croft, and spouse Frances Hires. The mother's-name field still conflicts with the Hiers/Alderman parentage trail and appears to be an informant or clerk error using the wife's maiden name.
  • Francis/Frances R. Hiers appears as a widowed head of household in 1930, 1940, and 1950. The 1940 census places daughter Okella Hiers, age 48, in her household. The Georgia Death Index gives Francis R. Hires, female, age 87, died 22 January 1956 in Colquitt County, Georgia, certificate 10700. A FamilySearch Find a Grave index entry gives Francis Lenore Croft Hires, born 25 October 1868, died 22 January 1956, buried at Berlin Cemetery in Colquitt County.
  • John appears as a child in Phillip Hires's household in 1860 and in Phillip Hiers's household in 1870. The 1880 census places John Hiers, age 25, as nephew in William Hiers's household. These records support the Phillip Hiers family connection, though they do not by themselves prove every later compiled parentage claim.
  • Francis Lenore/Renore Croft is supported as the wife from the 1900-1940 household trail. Her likely Croft childhood family is supported by the 1870 and 1880 Brooks County census entries for Jacob H. Croft and Jerona/Jerony Croft.
  • Okella/Ocalla/Ocala Hires is supported from the 1900, 1910, 1920, 1930, and 1940 census trail. FamilySearch also has a 1941 Colquitt County marriage record for Okella Hiers to W. J. Bryan that names parents John Hiers and Frances Hiers.
  • Stella Hires is supported from the 1900 and 1910 census trail. FamilySearch has a 22 August 1915 Brooks County marriage record for Stella Hires and Charlie Johnson, and a Georgia death record for John Turner Johnson naming Charley Johnson and Stella Hires as parents. A FamilySearch Find a Grave index entry reports Stella Hiers Johnson, born 1896 and died 14 November 2000, buried in Cook County.
  • Mollie Hines/Hires is supported from the 1900 and 1910 parental households. The best online adult trail is Mollie J. Hires Johnson: a Brooks County marriage record gives Mollie Hires/Hiers marrying N. A. Johnson on 4 March 1912; the later FamilySearch tree attachment places the same person with William Alexander Johnson; the 1920 and 1930 Colquitt County census records place Mollie/Mollie J. Johnson with William A./Will Johnson and children; and a child NUMIDENT record names Arthur Johnson's parents as William A. Johnson and Mollie Hires. The parent-child proof comes through the child NUMIDENT and the FamilySearch tree attachment path. This supports the adult identity, but Mollie's own death and burial remain unclosed.
  • Bessie Hines/Hires is supported from the 1900 and 1920 parental households. A FamilySearch NUMIDENT record for Laddie Harris gives his birth as 5 September 1923 at Barney/Brooks, Georgia, death as 19 December 2000, and parents as J. B. Harris and Bessie Hires. A companion NUMIDENT result names Bessie Hires as spouse of J. B. Harris and mother of Laddie Harris. A FamilySearch tree profile for Bessie Hires, attached to the John A. Hiers and Frances Lenore Croft family, gives Joseph Benjamin Harris as spouse, Laddie Harris as child, an SSDI death for Bessie Hiers in September 1980 in Queens, New York, and a GenealogyBank obituary-index source under Bessie Hires Harris. This Harris/death trail is secondary-supported and not cleanly closed because the tree has duplicate/conflicting Bessie profiles and the 1900 household age does not align with the 1903 birth date attached to the Harris profile.

docs.title: Connections to Other Barney Families
docs.text:
• John A. Hiers appears to be the brother of Jacob Hunter Hiers of HH#144. The shared Phillip Hiers household trail supports the connection; compiled memorial/tree material should not be treated as the only proof.
  • Through the Hiers/Alderman parentage claim, this household belongs in the Hiers, Alderman, Strickland, and Croft cluster, but direct records should be preferred over Geneanet, Find a Grave relationship links, or unsourced tree relationships.
  • Possible same-surname households HH#130 and HH#195 remain only same-surname leads unless direct records connect them.

docs.title: Research Notes
docs.text:
• John A. Hiers's direct online death record gives 15 November 1921, while the FamilySearch Find a Grave index gives 15 September 1921 and burial at Berlin Cemetery. Use the direct Georgia deaths record for the death date unless an image-level cemetery or certificate review proves otherwise. The mother's-name conflict remains unresolved.
  • Francis Lenore Croft Hiers's 1956 death is supported by the Georgia Death Index. Burial is supported by the FamilySearch Find a Grave index. An obituary, probate file, or original death certificate image would still improve the entry but is no longer required to establish the date.
  • Mollie Hines/Hires is supported as the Mollie J. Hires who married William Alexander/N. A. Johnson, but her own death and burial remain open. The 1905 J. B. Moore and 1909 D. C. Baker marriage candidates remain rejected or unproved because they conflict with Mollie's 1910 parental-household appearance and lack parent-linking support.
  • Bessie Hines/Hires has a supported adult Harris trail through Laddie Harris's NUMIDENT, but the FamilySearch tree evidence is secondary and internally conflicted. Do not use the September 1980 Queens, New York death as a closed fact unless a direct death, obituary, cemetery, or probate record confirms that the Bessie Hiers in SSDI is the Barney/Brooks County daughter.
  • The 1900 son John ?? Hines remains unresolved. FamilySearch tree profile G9JQ-VY9 attaches only the 1900 census and a 1910 Robert Hires census source, which appears to conflate John with brother Robert rather than prove John's survival. Online searches still found no separate parent-linked death, marriage, draft, census, or burial record for John.
  • The 1930 Ancestry index has errors: Francis R. Hiers is indexed as male, and Okella/O Cally's age appears inconsistent with the broader census trail. Use the image and household context rather than the index alone.
  • A direct marriage record for John A. Hiers and Francis Croft has not been located in this pass; the circa 1889 marriage date is inferred from the 1900 census.
