docs.title: Household #171: Turner, Mary Ann Royal
docs.text:
Back to the 1900 Census & Household Index

In the 1900 Barney census, Mary Turner headed a 3-person household. The table below preserves the exact names, relationships, ages, birthplaces, and occupations recorded for the household.

docs.title: Household Snapshot
docs.text:
Mary Turner headed a 3-person household in the 1900 Barney census with 1 child and 1 extended-family member.

Mary Turner's listed occupation was Farmer.

All listed household members were reported as born in Georgia.

docs.title: Newspaper and Public-Record Trail
docs.text: This section flags public-record leads separate from the census table. The detailed discussion stays in the family narrative, research status, and source citations below.

docs.title: 1900 Census Household
docs.text: Name Relation Age Birthplace Occupation Mary Turner Head 63 Georgia Farmer Julia Alde Daughter 28 Georgia — William Alde Grandson 6 Georgia —

docs.title: Children and Later Trails
docs.text: This section is reserved for later-life child evidence. No later spouse, death, burial, obituary, probate, separate household, or descendant-line identification has been added here yet from direct records.

docs.title: Family Narrative
docs.text:
Mary Ann Royal Turner (listed in 1900 as May S. Turner) - Born: December 1832 in Georgia; compiled/cemetery material gives 8 December 1832 in Houston County, Georgia - Died: 19 July 1905 - Buried: Woodlawn City Cemetery, Adel, Cook County, Georgia - Marital status in 1900: Widowed - Occupation: Farmer - Children: 11 children born, 9 living, per the 1900 census - Identification note: The 1900 household head is recorded as May S. Turner. The current evidence trail treats her as Mary Ann Royal Turner, widow of Job Turner. - Parentage caution: Isaac I. Royal and Nancy Murray remain secondary-supported parent candidates only. No direct parent-link record has been reviewed for Mary Ann Royal in this entry.

Husband

Job Turner (also Joab Turner and J. S. Turner in some records) - Born: about 1823, probably North Carolina, per later household context and secondary sources - Died: 18 December 1881, per cemetery and compiled material - Buried: Woodlawn City Cemetery, Adel, Cook County, Georgia - Marriage context: A Confederate widows application cited on Mary Ann Royal Turner's Find a Grave memorial says Mary married Job Turner in Marion County, Georgia, in 1850. A Brooks County marriage record also exists for Mary A. Royal and J. S. Turner on 8 February 1879; the context of that later record remains unresolved. - Parentage caution: Amos Isaac Turner and Nancy Smith remain secondary-supported parent candidates only. No direct parent-link record has been reviewed for Job Turner in this entry.

Children and Family Reconstruction

The household's child count remains difficult. The 1900 census says Mary had 11 children, 9 living. The 1860, 1870, and 1880 census trail; cemetery records; FamilySearch profiles; Find a Grave memorials; and Ancestry tree hints produce overlapping but not identical child lists.

Current evidence supports William J. Turner, Sarah E. or Sarah Abby Turner Middlebrooks, Isaiah S. Turner, Isaac McDaniel Turner, Albert Augustus Turner, Thomas J. Turner, John A. Turner, Charlie W. Turner, Mary Julia "Mollie" Turner Alderman, Nancy A. or Nancy Orelia Turner Alderman, Robert Amos Turner, and Arthur C. Turner as part of the working reconstruction, with different confidence levels. Martha Lee Turner Middlebrooks should not be counted as a child of Job and Mary on current evidence because her Georgia death-record detail names John Turner and Jane Vance as parents.

Sarah E. or Sarah Abby Turner is now treated as Sarah Abby Turner Middlebrooks. FamilySearch profile KC36-B57 attaches the 1870 Turner household census, the 1874 Georgia county marriage to W. M. Middlebrooks, the 1880 census as Sarah A. Middlebrooks, and cemetery-index records under Sarah Abby Turner Middlebrooks. The adult trail is supported by census and marriage evidence; the exact death date rests on cemetery-index evidence rather than a death certificate.

Robert Amos Turner is no longer only a tree-based candidate. FamilySearch profile KJP1-KG4 attaches Robert or Robert A. Turner to the 1870 and 1880 Turner household censuses, then follows him through 1897 Georgia marriage records, 1900-1920 census records, and a 1921 Florida marriage record. The census attachments are the main parent-link evidence. His exact birth and death details still need image-level review.

Thomas J. Turner and Arthur C. Turner remain unresolved children. Thomas appears in the 1860 household as a one-year-old. A possible adult candidate, Thomas J. Turner born September 1859 in Georgia and living in Alachua County, Florida, in 1900, lacks parent-link evidence tying him to Job and Mary. Arthur C. appears in the 1880 household, age four, but no secure adult or death trail was found.

Isaiah Smith Turner supplies one important parent-link record. FamilySearch Florida death record FPD3-J25 names Job Turner and Mary Ann Royal as Isaiah's parents. This supports Mary's maiden name and the Job-Mary child framework, but it does not name Mary Ann Royal's own parents.

Alderman Household Members

Mary Julia "Mollie" Turner Alderman is the best current identity for the Julia Alde in Mary's 1900 household. Ancestry and FamilySearch index the 1900 entry under Alde, Aldwin, Alderman, and Turner variants. The 1910 Colquitt County census places Mollie J. Alderman, age 39 and widowed, as head of household with Wm I. Alderman, age 16, listed as her son; the census reports one child born and one living. This is the clearest direct source found for William's mother. Mollie's 1948 Valdosta death notice names one son, W. I. Alderman of Valdosta, and one sister, Miss Nancy Alderman of Moultrie. This strengthens the Mollie-William-Nancy cluster but still does not name Mollie's parents.

William Alde in the 1900 household is best identified as William Ivey/Ivy/Ira Alderman, born about October 1893 and died in 1956. His adult trail is supported by the 1910 census with Mollie J. Alderman, the 1915 Colquitt County marriage to Lula Banks, World War I service records, Veterans Administration Master Index, 1950 census, Find a Grave or headstone material, NUMIDENT-linked child records, and the full 1956 obituary image in The Valdosta Daily Times. Those records support William's adult identity and later family, but they do not name his father. The 1956 obituary names wife Lula Banks Alderman, daughters Shirley Bacon and Lynette Overby, sons Earl, T. I., Aaron, and Howard Alderman, 11 grandchildren, church membership, military service, funeral, and burial details, but no parents.

The leading father candidate for William is J. S. Alderman. Ancestry's Georgia county marriage record shows J. S. Alderman married M. J. Turner in Brooks County on 8 January 1893. The timing fits William's October 1893 birth, and the names fit the Mary Julia "Mollie" Turner Alderman interpretation. Ancestry tree hints identify J. S. as James Seward "Send" Alderman, son of Jonathan Howell Alderman and Amy Ann McKinney. No reviewed record directly names William Ivey/Ivy/Ira Alderman as James Seward Alderman's son, so this remains candidate evidence rather than proof.

Nancy A. or Nancy Orelia Turner Alderman has an adult trail supported by Find a Grave, Florida death-index material, the 1950 census, the 1900 Mary Turner household context, and Ancestry tree claims naming Job Turner and Mary Ann Royal. The tree claim remains secondary. No new parent-naming record was found in the June 2026 review.

Census and Record Trail

Mary Ann Royal Turner is followed through a broad census and cemetery trail. The 1900 household head is recorded as May S. Turner, a census/index form now treated as Mary Turner in the wider record chain. In 1850, Mary A. Turner, age 16, was recorded in Macon County, Georgia, in a Turner household headed by Levi Turner. The same record says she was married within the year. The exact connection between that household and Job Turner remains unproved. In 1860, she appears in New River, Florida, in the household of Joab Turner, an apparent variant of Job Turner. The Ancestry index reads her name as Levi A. Turner, but the later record pattern supports treating this as a misreading of Mary or Mary A. R. Turner. In 1870, Mary Turner was in Colquitt County, Georgia, with Job Turner and children. In 1880, Mary A. R. Turner was in District 1311, Berrien County, Georgia, with Job Turner and a large child group. By 1900, she was widowed in Barney, Brooks County.

Mary is identified in compiled and cemetery material as Mary Ann Royal Turner, born 8 December 1832 in Houston County, Georgia, died 19 July 1905, and buried at Woodlawn City Cemetery in Adel, Cook County, Georgia. The Houston County birthplace and 1850 marriage statement come from a Confederate widows application cited on her Find a Grave memorial. That application says she was born in Houston County, married Job Turner in Marion County, Georgia, in 1850, and that Job served in Company D, Georgia 20th Cavalry, later transferred to the Georgia 22nd Battalion. The application should be treated as a strong lead until the image or copy is reviewed directly.

Job Turner is supported as Mary's husband by the 1860, 1870, and 1880 household trail, the Confederate widows application citation, cemetery material, and the 1879 Brooks County marriage record for Mary A. Royal and J. S. Turner. The 1879 marriage may be a late formalization or re-recording of an older marriage, but that explanation should not be treated as proved until the record image and county context are reviewed. Job is also indexed or described as Joab Turner and J. S. Turner in some sources. His parentage remains unresolved by direct evidence.

Mary Ann Royal's parentage remains secondary-supported rather than proved. FamilySearch, Ancestry trees, and GeorgiaRoyal.net identify Isaac I. Royal and Nancy Murray as her parents. GeorgiaRoyal.net places Mary Ann Royal, born 8 December 1832 and married to Job Turner, among the children of Isaac I. Royal and Nancy Murray. This should remain labeled as compiled evidence until a census household, estate record, marriage record, Bible record, or other parent-link source is found.

Job Turner's parentage also remains secondary-supported rather than proved. FamilySearch and the FamilyTreeDNA Turner DNA Project identify him as a son of Amos Isaac Turner and Nancy Smith, with a Lenoir County, North Carolina birth. The Turner DNA Project line #119540 is useful context, but it is not a documentary parent-link record.

docs.title: Connections to Other Barney Families
docs.text:
• HH#175 Charlie W. Turner is a son in the Job Turner and Mary Ann Royal Turner family reconstruction. His separate household entry documents his adult trail.
  • HH#177 Isaac McDaniel Turner is also a son in this family reconstruction. His household entry documents his adult trail and his Alderman marriage connection.
  • HH#144 and HH#170 connect indirectly through the Hiers-Alderman network. Mary Turner's daughters Mollie and Nancy Orelia married into the Alderman family, while the Hiers households carry Alderman ties through Mary Catherine Alderman.
  • HH#153, HH#155, HH#176, HH#178, and HH#180 belong to the broader Alderman cluster relevant to the Turner-Alderman marriages. Exact kinship paths should be cited from direct records where available and from compiled Alderman sources only as secondary support.
  • HH#168 and HH#169 lived in District 1311, Berrien County, the district where the Turner family was enumerated in 1880. This is geographic context only, not a proved kinship connection.

docs.title: Research Notes
docs.text:
• The 1900 Julia Alde entry is probably Mary Julia "Mollie" Turner Alderman. The 1910 Mollie J. Alderman census, the 1948 Mollie death notice, the 1948 funeral notice, Find a Grave, Ancestry indexing, Ancestry tree/photo hints, and FamilySearch profile KCR2-SGP all support that interpretation. A primary record naming Mollie's parents is still needed.
  • William Alde is probably William Ivey/Ivy/Ira Alderman. The 1910 census directly names Mollie J. Alderman as his mother. The leading father candidate is J. S. Alderman, who married M. J. Turner on 8 January 1893 in Brooks County, but no reviewed record directly names William's father.
  • Mary J. Turner and Nancy A. or Nancy Orelia Turner need reconciliation. Nancy Orelia has a supported adult trail; Mary J. remains unresolved. A marriage, death, probate, Bible, church, or child record naming parents would clarify whether Mary J., Mary Julia/Mollie, and Nancy were separate daughters or partly duplicate identities.
  • Martha Lee Turner Middlebrooks should stay excluded from the Job-Mary child list unless stronger original evidence explains the conflict. Her own Georgia death-record detail names John Turner and Jane Vance as parents.
  • Sarah Abby Turner Middlebrooks and Robert Amos Turner have improved adult trails, but image-level review of key attached sources would strengthen both. Sarah's exact death date rests on cemetery-index evidence. Robert's exact birth and death details remain dependent on compiled or attached-source trails.
  • Thomas J. Turner and Arthur C. Turner each appear in the child census trail but lack a secure adult or death trail.
  • Mary Ann Royal's parents and Job Turner's parents remain secondary-supported only. The current entry should not present Isaac I. Royal and Nancy Murray, or Amos Isaac Turner and Nancy Smith, as proved parents without direct or near-direct evidence.
  • The 1879 Brooks County marriage record for Mary A. Royal and J. S. Turner needs image and courthouse-context review before explaining it as a formalization or re-recording of the 1850 marriage.

docs.title: Military Service
docs.text: William Alde, the grandson in this 1900 household, is best identified as William Ivey, Ivy, or Ira Alderman. His adult trail includes World War I service records, Veterans Administration Master Index material, a military headstone application, and a 1956 obituary that mentions military service. Those records support a household-member service note, though they do not resolve his father's identity.

docs.title: Family Narrative
docs.text:
James D. Johnson (also James Johnson) - Born January 1851, Georgia - Died After 1900; no accepted death record has been found. The former 1922 Taylor County, Florida lead has been eliminated as a different Florida-born James D. Johnson. - Marital Status: Single (never married, no children) - Occupation: Farmer (1900 census) - Parents: James C. Johnson (born ~1819, South Carolina) and Sidney L. Mims (born December 7, 1812, Georgia; died August 26, 1899)

James D. Johnson was the eldest child of his father's second marriage. His father, James C. Johnson, married three times:

  1. Elizabeth Miley (born ~1826, South Carolina) — first wife. Children: Paul Hamilton (~1844), Mary C. (~1846), Sarah R. (~1848).
  2. Sidney L. Mims (born December 7, 1812, Georgia; died August 26, 1899) — second wife. James D. was likely her first child, born January 1851 at the transition between marriages.
  3. "Sidney Elizabeth Hiers" — listed in FamilySearch as a third wife, but this is almost certainly a duplicate conflation of Sidney L. Mims. No independent record evidence supports this as a separate person.

Grandparents: Rev. Paul Johnson (FamilySearch G3QS-G4B) and Mary Polly Hiers (FamilySearch L8RN-STS). The Hiers connection links this household to HH#170 (John A. Hiers) and HH#144 (Jacob Hunter Hiers).

  • Paul Hamilton Johnson, born ~1844; mother Elizabeth Miley; Confirmed 1850 and 1860 censuses
  • Mary C. Johnson, born ~1846; mother Elizabeth Miley; Later "Mary Shockey" per FamilySearch (L1BV-FFQ); living with James D. in 1900, age 54
  • Sarah R. Johnson, born ~1848; mother Elizabeth Miley; Confirmed 1850 census
  • James D. Johnson, born Jan 1851; mother Sidney L. Mims; Head of HH#172
  • George A. Johnson, born ~1855; mother Sidney L. Mims; Confirmed 1880 census
  • Nancy E. Johnson, born ~1857; mother Sidney L. Mims; Confirmed 1880 census
  • Rev. John Calvin Johnson, born ~1860; mother Sidney L. Mims; FamilySearch GQLC-14N; three wives, fourteen children, Gwinnett County

1850 Census — Lowndes County, Georgia. James C. Johnson (31, male, South Carolina), Elizabeth (24, female, South Carolina), Paul (6), Mary (4), Sarah (2). James D. not yet born. FamilySearch ARK: MZYT-RB3.

1860 Census — Brooks County, Georgia. James D. appears as a child in James C. Johnson's household. Ancestry record 10751328 (link expired at time of research).

1870 Census — Brooks County, Georgia. James D. in James C. Johnson household. Ancestry record 587998.

1880 Census — Brooks County, Georgia. James D. (age 29) listed with siblings George A., Sarah R., Mary R., and Nancy E. in father's household.

1890 Georgia Property Tax Digest. James D. Johnson, Morven District 660, White. Ancestry record 716431.

1900 Census — Barney, Brooks County, Georgia (this household). James D. Johnson, age 49, single, born January 1851, Georgia, farmer. Living with sister Mary Johnson (age 54). FamilySearch ARK: M3FP-FPC. Note: Ancestry indexes marital status as "Widowed" but FamilySearch confirms "Single" on the original image. James D. never married and had no children.

1910 Census — Not Located. No match found in Brooks County (zero results) or in Georgia statewide (144 results, none clearly matching a single man born circa 1851). Florida search also returned no definitive match. He may have been missed by the census enumerator, enumerated under a different name, or residing in a location not yet searched.

1920 Census — Not Located. Florida statewide search returned only six results, none in Taylor County and none matching James D. Johnson's profile. No match found in Georgia either.

The Florida/Taylor County 1922 lead has now been downgraded from ambiguous candidate evidence to an eliminated cluster. FamilySearch search results for James D. Johnson in Taylor County show a Find a Grave memorial, 1910 census, 1920 census, and Florida death-index entry all pointing to a different man: James D. Johnson, born in Florida about 1849-1851, married to M. V./Mary/Miram Johnson, and buried at Perry, Taylor County, Florida. The detailed death certificate (FamilySearch ARK: FP9C-F2Z) also belongs to this Florida-born man, not to the Georgia-born single James D. Johnson in HH#172.

Ancestry's Florida probate index for James D. Johnson, probate date 20 November 1922, Taylor County, Florida (collection 8993, record 150662, image 005888907_00045), is most likely part of the same Florida-born James D. Johnson cluster unless the image proves otherwise. The index alone does not name parents, birthplace, spouse, heirs, or a Brooks County connection, and it should not be used as evidence for the HH#172 James D. Johnson.

No direct death certificate, burial record, probate file, obituary, or post-1900 census continuation has been found for the Georgia-born James D. Johnson after the 1900 Barney census.

docs.title: Connections to Other Barney Families
docs.text:
James D. Johnson's grandmother, Mary Polly Hiers (FamilySearch L8RN-STS), connects this household directly to two other Barney households: - HH#170 — John A. Hiers (Mary Polly's son, James D.'s uncle) - HH#144 — Jacob Hunter Hiers (Mary Polly's grandson, James D.'s cousin)

The Johnson-Hiers family network spans at least three households in the Barney precinct, all tracing back to Rev. Paul Johnson and Mary Polly Hiers. Rev. Paul Johnson appears on the 1850 Lowndes County census as a separate household near his son James C. Johnson.

docs.title: Research Notes
docs.text:
1. 1910 and 1920 census absence. James D. does not appear in any searchable census record after 1900. The 1922 Taylor County death-index lead is now eliminated as proof for this man, so there is no accepted post-1900 date by which he is known to be alive. He may have died before 1910, been enumerated under a name variant, lived in a household where his surname was not recorded, moved away, or been missed by enumerators.

  2. Sister Mary's later life. Mary C. Johnson (FamilySearch L1BV-FFQ), age 54 in 1900 and living with James D., has no traceable record after 1900. The FamilySearch tree lists her as "Mary Shockey," but no matching Shockey record has been found in post-1900 Georgia or Florida censuses.

  3. Death/probate ambiguity now eliminated as proof. The Florida Death Index "J D Johnson, 1922, Taylor County" and the Ancestry Taylor County probate index should not be treated as supporting HH#172 unless a probate image later names Georgia/Brooks County relatives. FamilySearch results tie the Taylor County death/burial/census cluster to a different Florida-born married James D. Johnson with wife M. V./Mary/Miram Johnson.

  4. "Sidney Elizabeth Hiers" third wife. FamilySearch lists a third wife for James C. Johnson named "Sidney Elizabeth Hiers." Given the 14-year age gap between Elizabeth Miley (born ~1826, South Carolina) and Sidney L. Mims (born 1812, Georgia), and the absence of any independent record for a third wife, this is almost certainly a duplicate entry conflating Sidney Mims with the Hiers surname. No separate marriage record or census entry supports a third marriage.

docs.title: Family Narrative
docs.text:
George A. Johnson (age 46, Farmer) - Full Name: George A. Johnson (middle name not confirmed; "A." from 1860 census and 1880 suggestion) - Born September 1853, Georgia (per 1900 census) - Died After 1910 (exact date not found in available records) - Occupation: Farmer (owned farm, no mortgage listed in 1900) - Father was James C. Johnson (b. South Carolina) - Mother was Sidney L. Mims (b. Georgia, December 7, 1812 — died August 26, 1899) - Siblings: Paul Hamilton, Mary C. (Shockey), Sarah R., James D. (HH#172), Nancy E., John Calvin, and others - Grandparents: Rev. Paul Johnson + Mary Polly Hiers (connects to HH#170 and HH#144) - Key Relationship: George A. Johnson is the brother of James D. Johnson (HH#172), confirmed via 1860 census showing both in their father James C. Johnson's household

Roda (Rosa/Rhody) Ann Weeks. - Married November 14, 1886, Colquitt County, Georgia - Born ~1866, Colquitt County, Georgia - Father was Charles Weeks - Mother was Rhoda Weeks (maiden name unknown) - 1870 Census: Age 4, in father Charles Weeks' household, Colquitt County GA - 1880 Census: Age 14, in father Charles Weeks' household, Colquitt County GA (indexed as "Rhoda E. Weeks") - Name Variants: Roda (marriage cert), Rosa (1900 census), Rhody (1900 census), Rhoda (1910+ census, death record), "Rhodie E." (Oregon record — see below) - Note on "Lizzie Weeks": A Georgia death record for "Geo Johnson" (collection 2562) lists spouse as "Lizzie Weeks." Rhoda's middle initial "E." may stand for Elizabeth, with "Lizzie" as a nickname. Whether Lizzie is Rhoda's given name or a second wife after Rhoda's 1932 death remains unresolved. - Died May 19, 1932, Brooks County, Georgia (Certificate #13278)

  1. William Johnson — born ~1887, Georgia (age 13 in 1900; likely "Willie" age 23 in 1910)
  2. Nancy Johnson Hunt — born ~1889, Georgia (age 11 in 1900); died 7 May 1937 in Moultrie, Colquitt County, Georgia. Georgia death record names father Geo Johnson and mother Lizzie Weeks.
  3. James Pinkey Johnson — born ~1891, Georgia (age 9 in 1900; "James I" age 17 in 1910); died 21 January 1937 in Moultrie, Colquitt County, Georgia. Georgia death record names father Geo Johnson and mother Lizzie Weeks.
  4. Charley (Charlie) Johnson — born ~1897, Georgia (age 3 in 1900; age 13 in 1910)
  5. Daniel S. or Daniel Shepherd Johnson — born ~1899, Georgia (age 1 in 1900; age 11 in 1910); died 17 January 1969 in Montgomery, Montgomery County, Alabama. Alabama death/burial index names father George A. Johnson and mother Lizzie Weeks. Wife listed as Mary Ella Johnson.

  6. George Samuel Johnson — born ~1906, Georgia (age 4 in 1910 as "Samuel"). A likely adult trail exists for George Samuel Johnson, born 4 March 1906 in Colquitt County, later found in WWII draft, 1950 Portland, Oregon census, Washington marriage, Oregon death, and FindAGrave records, but no parent-naming record has been found to prove he is the 1910 child.

  7. Year: 1860; Location: Brooks, GA; Head Name (indexed): Geo A Johnson; Age: 7; Occupation: —; Spouse: —; Children in HH: In father James C. Johnson's household

  8. Year: 1870; Location: Brooks, GA; Head Name (indexed): George Johnson; Age: 17; Occupation: Farm laborer; Spouse: —; Children in HH: In father's household; cannot read/write
  9. Year: 1880; Location: Morven, Brooks, GA; Head Name (indexed): George A. Johhnson (sic); Age: 26; Occupation: —; Spouse: —; Children in HH: Single; in father's household as Son
  10. Year: 1900; Location: Barney, Brooks, GA; Head Name (indexed): George Johnson; Age: 46; Occupation: Farmer; Spouse: Rosa (age 36); Children in HH: William 13, Nancy 11, James 9, Charley 3, Daniel 1

  11. Year: 1910; Location: Robinson, Colquitt, GA; Head Name (indexed): George Admson (sic); Age: 56; Occupation: Farmer; Spouse: Rhoda (age 44); Children in HH: Willie 23, James I 17, Charlie 13, Daniel 11, Samuel 4

  12. Sibling Connection to HH#172: The 1860 census confirms George A. Johnson (age 7) in the household of James C. Johnson (age 42) and Sidney L. Mims (age 47), along with James D. Johnson (age 9). Both George and James D. are sons of James C. Johnson, making HH#172 and HH#173 sibling households. Both connect to Rev. Paul Johnson and Mary Polly Hiers (HH#170/HH#144) as grandparents.

  13. Wife's Family: Rhoda Ann Weeks was the daughter of Charles and Rhoda Weeks of Colquitt County. She appears in the 1870 census at age 4 and the 1880 census at age 14 in her father's household. The 1886 marriage in Colquitt County confirms the connection.

  14. County Migration: The family moved from Brooks County (1860-1900) to Colquitt County (1910), a shift of approximately 20 miles. The 1910 census in Robinson, Colquitt County is the last confirmed record.

  15. Name Indexing Variations: The surname appears as "Johnson," "Johhnson" (1880), and "Admson" (1910) across different records — these indexing errors are common for Johnson-family records in this precinct.

  16. Post-1910 Gap: The family has not been found as a complete household in the 1920 or 1930 censuses, nor has a death record been located for George A. Johnson. Rhoda's death record (May 19, 1932, Brooks County GA, Certificate #13278) confirms she survived George, but the timing of his death is unknown. The adult trails for Nancy Johnson Hunt, James Pinkey Johnson, and Daniel S./Shepherd Johnson are now supported by parent-naming death records or death/burial indexes. William, Charley, and George Samuel remain unresolved.

  17. Oregon Record Eliminated: An Oregon death record for "George A Johnson" with spouse "Rhodie E Weeks" and child "George Samuel Johnson" was investigated but eliminated. George would have been ~115 years old if he died in Oregon in 1968, making this a different person with coincidentally similar names.

docs.title: Family Narrative
docs.text:
Charles Pinkney Weeks (also listed as Pinksuy Weeks, Pink Weeks) - Born April 23, 1835, Georgia (birth year varies by source: 1834 per Civil War records, 1835 per FindAGrave, 1837 per earlier FindAGrave, 1838 per 1900 census) - Died August 7, 1901, Moultrie, Colquitt County, Georgia (confirmed by FindAGrave and Civil War records) - Buried Murphy Cemetery, Colquitt County, Georgia - Occupation: Sawmill laborer (1900 census) - Nickname: "Pink" — confirmed by Georgia death record listing "Pink Weeks" as spouse of Rodie - Father was James Weeks (born ~1810, South Carolina, per 1850 census) - Mother was Elizabeth Weeks (born ~1815, South Carolina, per 1850 census)

Rhoda Chason Harrell Weeks (also Rodie, Rhody) - Born August 31, 1840, Thomas County, Georgia - Died October 28, 1920, Moultrie, Colquitt County, Georgia - Buried Murphy Cemetery, Colquitt County, Georgia - Maiden name: Harrell - Middle name: Chason (not a second surname; maiden name is Harrell) - Father was Lewis Harrell (born ~1802, North Carolina) - Mother was Litty (also Letha) Harrell (born ~1804, North Carolina) - Cannot read or write (noted in 1910 census) - Marriage: ~1861 (per FindAGrave), Colquitt or Thomas County, Georgia - Married approximately 40 years by 1900 census (8 children born, 6 living) - Survived Charles by 19 years; appears in 1910 census as widowed mother-in-law in the Moses Pitts household

  • Mary Ann ("Janie"), born ~1862; 1870 Age 8; 1880 Age 17; Married Moses Pitts; appears in 1910 census with mother Rhoda
  • Charles Luke, born ~1865; 1870 Age 5; 1880 Age 15; Listed as "Chas L" on Georgia death record of father
  • Rhoda Ann, born ~1866; 1870 Age 4; 1880 Age 13; Married George A. Johnson, Nov 14, 1886, Colquitt County (HH#173)
  • Sarah, born ~1867; 1870 Age 3; 1880 Age 11; No further records located
  • James W., born ~1869; 1870 Age 4/12; 1880 Age 2; Appears as head of HH#193 (age 28, married to Mary, brother William in household)
  • Tempa, born ~1873; 1870 —; 1880 Age 7; Only appears in 1880 census
  • Thomas J., born ~1876; 1870 —; 1880 Age 4; Only appears in 1880 census

  • William, born ~1880; 1870 —; 1880 —; Appears in 1900 census (age 20); possibly same as William in HH#193

  • Note on child count: The 1900 census records 8 born, 6 living. Seven children appear across the 1870 and 1880 censuses, plus William (age 20) in 1900, making 8 total. Two children (Tempa and Thomas J.) appear only in 1880; two (Sarah and James) appear in 1870 and 1880. The two deceased children by 1900 are likely among those who appear in only one census enumeration.

  • Year: 1850; Name: Charles Weeks; Age: 12; Location: Lowndes County, GA; Household: Son, in James Weeks household (father, age 40, SC; mother Elizabeth, age 35, SC); Source: Ancestry 8054:18806080

  • Year: 1850; Name: Rhoda Harrell; Age: 10; Location: District 81, Thomas County, GA; Household: Daughter, in Lewis Harrell household (father, age 48, NC; mother Litty, age 46, NC); Source: Ancestry 8054:18806140

  • Year: 1860; Name: Rhoda Harrell; Age: 20; Location: Colquitt County, GA; Household: In father Lewis Harrell's household; mother listed as "Letha"; Source: Ancestry 7667:10751334

Charles Pinkney Weeks served in the Confederate Army during the Civil War.

  • Unit: Company H, 50th Georgia Infantry, Private
  • Enlisted: March 22, 1862
  • Service Notes: Injured or hospitalized during service; survived the war
  • Soldier Index: Record 1138:1588748 (Confederate Soldiers index)
  • Soldier Records: Record 1555:779070 (full name confirmed as Charles Pinkney Weeks, born about 1834)

Charles took the Reconstruction-era loyalty oath on July 6, 1867, in Butts County, Georgia, District 26 (Record 1857:1050468). This location is geographically inconsistent with all other records, which place Charles in Colquitt or Brooks County before and after the war. He likely spent time in Butts County during or shortly after the war, possibly while serving or recovering from his injury, before returning to South Georgia.

  1. FindAGrave Memorial #101885209 (Charles Pinkney Weeks): Born April 23, 1837; died August 7, 1901; Murphy Cemetery, Colquitt County, Georgia.
  2. FindAGrave Memorial #145288617 (Charles Pinkney Weeks): Born April 23, 1835; died August 7, 1901; Murphy Cemetery, Colquitt County, Georgia. (Ancestry-hosted index record — second memorial with different birth year.)
  3. Georgia Death Record #60768027 ("Pink Weeks"): Spouse listed as Rodie; child listed as Chas L. Confirms nickname "Pink." (Ancestry Collection 60525)
  4. FindAGrave Memorial #101884420 (Rhoda Weeks): Born August 31, 1840; died October 28, 1920; married 1861; Murphy Cemetery, Colquitt County, Georgia.
  5. FindAGrave US Index (Rhoda Ann Weeks): Maiden name Harrell; born August 31, 1840, Thomas County, Georgia; died October 28, 1920, Moultrie, Colquitt County, Georgia; buried Murphy Cemetery. (Ancestry Collection 60525)

  6. Georgia Death Record #127759 ("Rhodie Weeks"): Died October 28, 1920, age 81, Moultrie, Colquitt County, Georgia.

  7. Birth year inconsistency: Charles's birth year varies across sources — 1834 (Civil War records), 1835 (one FindAGrave), 1837 (another FindAGrave), 1838 (1900 census). The 1850 census lists him as age 12 (born ~1838), but the 1860 census shows age 23 (born ~1837) and the 1870 census shows age 31 (born ~1839). The most consistent cluster is 1837-1838.

  8. "Chason" is a middle name: Earlier confusion about whether "Chason" was Rhoda's maiden name has been resolved. Her maiden name is Harrell. "Chason" appears to be her middle name.

  9. 1880 middle initial discrepancy: The 1880 census lists "Charles T. Weeks," but no other record includes a middle initial "T." This may be an enumerator error or a name variant that was dropped in later usage.

  10. Mary Ann Weeks = "Janie" Pitts: The 1910 census shows Rodie Weeks (age 69, widow) living as mother-in-law in the household of Moses Pitts (age 46) with wife Janie Pitts (age 40). Janie Pitts (age 40, born ~1870) matches the age and position of Mary Ann Weeks (age 17 in 1880). The nickname "Janie" is a common shortened form of Mary Ann.

  11. James W. Weeks = HH#193: The 1900 census entry for HH#174 lists William Weeks (son, age 20) and Pinkey Weeks (granddaughter, age 11). Meanwhile, HH#193 lists James Weeks (age 28) as head with brother William (age 19). James W. Weeks (age 28 in HH#193) matches the expected age of Charles's son James (age 4/12 in 1870, age 2 in 1880). William in HH#193 (age 19) may be the same William listed in HH#174 (age 20) — the one-year difference is within census rounding.

  12. Butts County oath: The Reconstruction oath places Charles in Butts County in 1867, but every other record puts him in the Colquitt/Brooks/Lowndes area. This suggests a temporary wartime or post-war stay, possibly connected to his military service or recovery.

docs.title: Connections to Other Barney Families
docs.text:
1. HH#173 (George A. Johnson): Daughter Rhoda Ann Weeks married George A. Johnson on November 14, 1886, in Colquitt County. This is the primary cross-volume link — HH#173 and HH#174 are connected by marriage.

  2. HH#193 (James Weeks): Son James W. Weeks appears as head of HH#193 (age 28, married to Mary, with brother William age 19). Same age and location as Charles's son James. HH#193 is a child household of HH#174.

  3. HH#55 (James Harrell): James Harrell (age 37, b. ~1863, sawmill laborer) in Barney bears the same surname as Rhoda's maiden name. Lewis Harrell (Rhoda's father, b. ~1802 NC) was in Thomas/Colquitt County. James (b. ~1863) is roughly 60 years younger than Lewis, which makes a grandson relationship plausible. The HH#55 entry was marked research-exhausted before the Weeks/Harrell connection was known. If HH#55 is revisited, the Lewis Harrell line should be the first avenue of investigation.

  4. Pitts family: Daughter Mary Ann "Janie" Weeks married Moses Pitts. The 1910 census shows Rhoda (widow, age 69) living with them in Barney. No Pitts household appears in our 1900 Barney enumeration.

  5. Harrell family (Thomas/Colquitt County): Lewis Harrell (b. ~1802 NC) and wife Litty/Letha (b. ~1804 NC) appear in the 1850 Thomas County census and 1860 Colquitt County census. Ancestry suggested records show a "Chasn Harrell" in non-population schedules and a "Mrs Rhoda Harrell" in Georgia Property Tax Digests (1793-1892), suggesting Lewis died and his widow Rhoda (the elder, mother of our Rhoda) appears independently in tax records.

Discrepancies & Resolutions.

  • Issue: Birth year; Source A: 1900 census: ~1838; Source B: Civil War: ~1834; FindAGrave: 1835 or 1837; Resolution: 1837-1838 is the most consistent cluster; no single source is definitive
  • Issue: Middle initial; Source A: 1880: Charles T. Weeks; Source B: All other records: Charles Pinkney Weeks; Resolution: Likely enumerator error; no "T" appears elsewhere
  • Issue: Butts County oath; Source A: 1867 Reconstruction oath: Butts County; Source B: All other records: Colquitt/Brooks/Lowndes; Resolution: Temporary wartime or post-war residence
  • Issue: Rhoda's middle name; Source A: FindAGrave: Rhoda Ann; Source B: Census/other: "Chason" appears; Resolution: "Chason" may be a middle name alongside Ann, or an enumerator misread
  • Issue: Nickname; Source A: Full name: Charles Pinkney; Source B: Death record: "Pink Weeks"; Resolution: "Pink" is a clear shortening of Pinkney

  3. Direct proof that William Weeks in HH#174 is the same William living with James W. Weeks in HH#193.
  4. Adult or death trails for Sarah, Tempa, and Thomas J. Weeks.
  5. Direct marriage source for Charles Pinkney Weeks and Rhoda Harrell, if one exists; current marriage timing rests mainly on census and Find a Grave/compiled context.

Gordon, and father Chas Turner. - Appears as Mary T. Gordon in the 1950 Moultrie household with husband Talmadge F. Gordon Sr. and son Thomas F. Gordon Jr. - Georgia Death Index: Nettie T. Gordon, female, white, age 64, died March 23, 1964, Colquitt County, Certificate #007941.

  1. Charlie W. Turner was the son of Job Turner (North Carolina native) and Mary A. R. Turner (Georgia native), establishing a Berrien County Turner family line with roots in North Carolina.

  2. Charlie and Martha Strawder grew up as next-door neighbors in Berrien County (1880 census, dwellings 385-386) before their 1894 marriage.

  3. Mattie died in Cumberland, Harlan County, Kentucky, on August 8, 1929. After her death, Charlie lived with his daughter Nettie and son-in-law Talmadge F. Gordon in Moultrie for at least twelve years (1930-1940).

  4. The 1900 indexer recorded the surname as "Garnes." All later censuses use Turner, confirming the indexer made an error.

  5. Birth year drift across censuses: 1869 (1900) to roughly 1865 (1910) to 1871 (1920) to 1870 (1930-1940). The 1900 census, which gives a specific month (January 1869), is the most reliable.

  6. The 1910 census lists "Margaret" as a son. Given the name, this is almost certainly an enumerator error for daughter.

  7. Middle initial conflict: the 1920 and 1930 censuses give "W" while the 1940 index shows "A" with a correction note to "Chas W Turner." The W initial is better supported.

  8. The 1910 census lists Charlie's father's birthplace as North Carolina (correct, confirmed by 1880 census). The 1930 census lists Georgia instead, which is an error.

  • HH#171 Mary Turner: Mary Ann Royal Turner (HH#171) is Isaac's mother and the matriarch of the Turner family. The 1880 census lists Isaac Mc D. Turner, age 23, single, in her household. HH#171, HH#175, and HH#177 are three households from the same family: Mary (the mother), Charlie (son #8), and Isaac (son #4). Two of Mary's daughters married Alderman men, and Isaac married Nancy Ellen Alderman (HH#176's daughter), creating Turner-Alderman links from both directions.

  • Item: 1900 surname; Conflict: "Garnes" vs. Turner; Resolution: Indexer error; all later censuses confirm Turner

docs.title: Connections to Other Barney Families
docs.text:
Isaac Turner sits at the junction of three Barney households:

HH#171 Mary Turner (Source-Researched): Mary Ann Royal Turner, Isaac's mother, is the widowed head of HH#171. Her 1880 census includes Isaac Mc D. Turner, age 23, single, in her household. Two of Mary's daughters (Mollie and Nancy Orelia) married Alderman men, creating a Turner-to-Alderman link independent of Isaac's marriage.

HH#175 Charlie W. Turner (Well-Researched): Charlie is Isaac's younger brother, also a son of Job Turner and Mary A.R. Turner. The 1880 census lists both in the parental household.

HH#176 Jonathan Howell Alderman (Source-Researched): Isaac's first wife Nancy Ellen Alderman was Jonathan's daughter (book ID 15-2-14-8). This makes Isaac a son-in-law of HH#176.

HH#178 George W. Alderman (Source-Researched): George is Nancy Ellen Alderman Turner's older brother (book ID 15-2-14-1), making him Isaac's brother-in-law. Eleven primary sources document George and wife Isabel Coulter from 1870 through death. Isabel's mother identified as Sena Ann Saffold, resolving census name variants.

  • Isaac's sisters married Aldermans: The obituary lists two sisters, Mrs. Mannie Alderman (Moultrie) and Mrs. Hollis Alderman (Valdosta). These are likely the daughters of HH#171 who married into the Alderman family, reinforcing the Turner-Alderman connection from both directions.

docs.title: Research Notes
docs.text:
1. Nancy's death date: FindAGrave and Geneanet give December 22, 1905; the book "Aldermans in America" gives December 23. One-day discrepancy; primary record (death certificate image) not yet viewed.
  2. Mother's name variants: 1860 "Levi A" (enumerator misread), 1870 "Mary," 1880 "Mary A.R.," FindAGrave "Marry Ann." All refer to the same woman, Mary Ann Royal Turner. See HH#171 for full analysis.
  3. Isaac's middle name: Census records use "Mc" or "M.D."; FindAGrave and the obituary use "McDaniel"; Geneanet uses "Med." The birthplace "McDaniel" in Berrien County suggests the middle name came from the community, not a person's surname.
  4. Geneanet infant-death errors: Both John Henry Turner and Hosea Turner are listed with infant-death date ranges (1885-1886 and 1897-1898) on Geneanet. The obituary proves both survived to adulthood. Geneanet entries are community-submitted and should be verified against primary sources.

  5. Daughter identification: The obituary names four daughters, but matching them to census records requires inference. Mrs. L.C. Shadrick likely equals Grace (1910 census). Mrs. C.D. Symorette and Mrs. R.F. Hannon are likely Willie Mae and Mary Letha, but which is which remains unclear.

  6. Jessie E. F. Nelson marriage now proved: FamilySearch and Ancestry both show Jessie E. F. Nelson marrying I. McD Turner in Colquitt County on June 3, 1917. Her 1900 Worth County and 1910 Monk, Colquitt County census entries provide the pre-marriage trail; the 1910 household names parents Charley M. Nelson and Martha Nelson.

  7. Adult trails for children: John Henry is now directly supported through SS Applications, Wakulla County census records, obituary index, and Find a Grave. Grace, Mamie Ive, Willie Mae, Mary Letha, Marion McDaniel, Juanita, and Cecil Eugenia still need direct adult records where the current entry relies on obituary matching, Find a Grave, NUMIDENT hints, or Geneanet.

  5. 1890: Wesley Flurnoy appears on the Georgia Freedman Tax List, Hat, Irwin County, District 690 (Fletcher). This places him outside Brooks County during the 1890 gap between censuses.

  7. 1910-1950: Not found in any federal census under plausible name variants (Wesley Flournoy, Wesley Flurnoy, Wesley FL, Wes Flournoy, J. Wesley Flournoy) in Georgia or surrounding states. No match in Brooks County or statewide searches. Wife Dora and daughters Nonie and Dollie B. also not located after 1900.

  8. June 2026 Ancestry follow-up: Targeted searches for Dora Flournoy with spouse Wesley and for Nonie Flournoy with parents Wesley/Dora did not produce a safe continuation. The strongest Dora hits belong to Alabama, Missouri, or California women with conflicting birthplace, parents, or household context. Nonie/Nannie hits were also geographically and demographically mismatched. No new record was attached.

  9. June 2026 FamilySearch follow-up: FamilySearch searches for Wesley Flournoy born 1863-1866 in Georgia with spouse Dora return the known 1900 Brooks County household as the only matching household. A later John Wesley Flournoy death/obituary cluster in Atlanta/Cobb/Fulton is eliminated because it names parents George Flournoy and Josephine Gallen, not John and Hannah Flournoy of Brooks County. No FamilySearch continuation was found for Dora, Nonie, or Dollie B.

Disambiguation: Two Wesley Flournoys in Georgia.

A different Wesley Flournoy lived in Jefferson County, Georgia, and is not the same person as our Brooks County subject. The Jefferson County Wesley can be distinguished by multiple factors:

  • Factor: 1900 wife; Brooks County Wesley (HH#179): Dora (age 20); Jefferson County Wesley: Amy/Annie (age 26)
  • Factor: 1900 children; Brooks County Wesley (HH#179): Nonie, Dollie B.; Jefferson County Wesley: Jinnie, Claudius, Rosa

  • Factor: Literacy; Brooks County Wesley (HH#179): Cannot read or write; Jefferson County Wesley: Can read and write
  • Factor: Home ownership; Brooks County Wesley (HH#179): Rents; Jefferson County Wesley: Owns farm
  • Factor: Mother-in-law; Brooks County Wesley (HH#179): None listed; Jefferson County Wesley: Sarah A. Morris

The Jefferson County Wesley appears in every census from 1900 through 1940 (Bartow and Phillips districts), with wife name variants Amy/Annie/Amil/Amine (same person), and died July 24, 1946, Jefferson County, age 78, certificate #16640.

docs.title: Connections to Other Barney Families
docs.text:
Wesley Flournoy belongs to one of the larger Black family networks in the Barney community. His parents John and Hannah Flournoy had at least ten children, and several of Wesley's siblings appear as heads of other Barney households:

  • Elizabeth Flournoy (b. ~1851) — married Thomas Lightsey (HH#12) on July 20, 1874, Brooks County. Died before 1900. Their children married into HH#10 (William Betts, via daughter Ella Lightsey) and HH#13 (George Wright, via daughter Lucy Lightsey).

  • Polly Flournoy (b. ~1852) — head of HH#185, widow with nine children (Mary, Arthur, Lula, Thomas, Cora, Earnest, Moses, Ella, John, Nettie). Living in Barney in 1900.

  • Elsie Flournoy (b. ~1875, not yet born in 1870) — married James Bailey (HH#51) on December 15, 1895, Brooks County. Mother Hannah Flournoy (age 50, widowed) was living in the Bailey household in 1900, which confirms the family link directly. The Baileys migrated to Leon County, Florida by 1910.

  • Thomas Flournoy (b. ~1860) — listed in 1870 at age 10. Not yet linked to a specific Barney household but appears in the Flournoy sibling list from HH#12's documentation.

  • Charles Flournoy (b. ~1868) — listed in 1870 at age 2. Appears in the Flournoy sibling list from HH#12's documentation.

Through these siblings, HH#179 connects to a cluster of nine other households: HH#9 (Ceily Davis, born Celey Lightsey), HH#10 (Betts), HH#12 (Lightsey), HH#13 (Wright), HH#51 (Bailey), HH#104 (Phillip Lightsey), HH#126 (Jasper Lightsey), HH#165 (Henry Lightsey), and HH#185 (Pollie Flournoy). The Lightsey-Flournoy-Davis-Betts cluster is one of the densest Black family networks documented in Barney.

Father John Flournoy died between 1880 (age 51, living in Morven) and 1900 (Hannah listed as widowed in HH#51). His Reconstruction-era voter oath record (Wesley Flornoy, Baker County, July 17, 1867) may belong to John rather than our Wesley, who would have been roughly three years old at the time. That record requires verification against the original image.

After the 1900 census, Wesley, his wife Dora, and their two young daughters vanish from all available records. No death certificate appears in the Georgia Death Index for Brooks or adjacent counties. No census match appears under any plausible spelling variant through 1950. This pattern echoes what happened to his sister Elizabeth (died before 1900) and the general mortality the Flournoy family experienced in the 1890s and early 1900s. The family may have moved out of state, died in an unrecorded event, or been enumerated under a name that does not match standard Flournoy variants.

docs.title: Research Notes
docs.text:
1. 1910 and later census trail for Wesley, Dora, Nonie, and Dollie B. under Flournoy/Flo(u)rnoy/Flurnoy and possible remarried or step-household surnames.
  2. Death, burial, church, probate, tax, or newspaper source for Wesley after the 1900 census.
  3. Dora's maiden name, marriage record, death/burial, or remarriage record.
  4. Adult or death trails for Nonie and Dollie B. Flournoy.
  5. Original-image review of the 1890 Freedman tax-list entry and the 1867 oath entry to decide whether either belongs to Wesley or to another Flournoy, likely father John.
  6. Secondary/local sources for Black Brooks County families, church cemeteries, and migration into Florida, if primary records remain absent.

docs.title: Family Narrative
docs.text:
Rubin Baker was born about May 1860 in Georgia and died 20 June 1938 in Brooks County, Georgia. His Georgia death record gives age 61, but that age conflicts with the 1900 census and the rest of the census trail; it should be treated as an informant or index error. His name appears as Rubin, Reuben, and Ruben Baker in different records.

The known online trail places him in several distinct records: a possible 1867 Reconstruction oath in Muscogee County, an 1870 Muscogee County household with wife Rose, an 1880 Hamilton County, Florida household with wife Jane, a Brooks County tax-digest entry, the 1895 Brooks County marriage to Lizzie Flournoy, the 1900-1930 Brooks County census trail, and his 1938 Georgia death record. The Annie Wright marriage and the Nankin-district Ruben Baker remain a caution because more than one Ruben/Rubin Baker lived in Brooks County.

Lizzie Flournoy Baker was born about 1875 and died 14 March 1950 in Brooks County. The 1880 census places a five-year-old Lizzie Flournoy as niece in the Primus and Mary Rhem household in Quitman, Brooks County. Her later Social Security Applications and Claims entry appears under Elizabeth Flintall and names spouse Ruben Baker and child Elizabeth Isom, indicating that she remarried or used a later surname after Rubin's death.

The 1910 and 1920 census trail expands the child list to John W., Buster/Bertie, Charlie, Leila/Lila, Hardy, Ira/Ivory, Marie, Nina, Hattie L., and Elizabeth. A renewed FamilySearch pass closed part of the child-trail problem: Hardy Baker has a Brooks County marriage to Ruth English on 23 September 1920 and World War I draft-registration hits; Marie Baker has a Brooks County marriage to Preston Stevens on 13 June 1920, matching the later Stevens-grandchild pattern around Lizzie's household. Hattie L. Baker remains with Lizzie through the 1930 and 1940 Barney census records. Nina remains with Lizzie in 1930 and 1940, with grandsons identified as Stivens/Stevens and Preston Stevens. Adult trails for Bertie/Buster, Annie, Leila/Lila, Ira/Ivory, and some later children remain incomplete.

docs.title: Connections to Other Barney Families
docs.text: Lizzie's Flournoy surname connects this household to the Brooks County Flournoy network documented in HH#179 and HH#185, but her exact parent within that network is not proved. Her 1880 placement as niece of Primus and Mary Rhem also creates a Rhem-Flournoy question that has not been closed.

docs.title: Research Notes
docs.text:
1. Lizzie's parentage and the Rhem-Flournoy relationship need a direct record; current evidence proves the surname and 1880 placement but not her parents.
  2. John Baker's biological father remains unknown; he is explicitly Rubin's stepson in 1900.
  3. Adult or death trails are still needed for Bertie/Buster, Annie, Leila/Lila, Ira/Ivory, Nina, Hattie, and Elizabeth Baker/Isom. Hardy Baker and Marie Baker now have Brooks County marriage records, but death/burial trails remain preferred.
  4. The Nankin-district Ruben Baker with wife Julia/possible Annie Wright must remain separated unless a direct source ties that man to this household.
  5. If only secondary tree material appears for a child trail, use it as a lead only and state that no primary record has been located.

docs.title: Online exhaustion update
docs.text: The June 2026 source pass exhausted the available online Ancestry/FamilySearch-indexed trail without safely closing Lizzie's parentage, John Baker's biological father, or the adult/death trails for Bertie/Buster, Annie, Leila/Lila, Ira/Ivory, Nina, Hattie, and Elizabeth Baker/Isom. The authenticated FamilySearch re-pass added Hardy Baker's 1920 Brooks County marriage to Ruth English and WWI draft trail, and Marie Baker's 1920 Brooks County marriage to Preston Stevens. Elizabeth Baker/Isom is supported through Social Security Applications material under Lizzie's later Elizabeth Flintall identity, but the other child trails remain unclosed. Secondary tree material was not used as proof.

docs.title: Family Narrative
docs.text:
The 1900 census explicitly places this as a White household, not a Black Barney household. Henrietta Elizabeth Rountree Joyce was born about 1846 and died in 1912. She was the daughter of Weston W. Rountree and Edith Elizabeth Folsom. Edith appears in the 1900 household as Henrietta's mother and connects the household to the Folsom-Rountree family.

Henrietta married William Washington Joyce, a Confederate veteran of the 57th Georgia Infantry and son of James Jackson Joyce and Elizabeth Wells. Their son George S. Joyce is HH#186. The prior entry's Rountree/Folsom lineage is supported by FindAGrave memorials, death-record evidence for related family members, and compiled family sources, but the entry should separate primary records from secondary lineage summaries.

The known children of Weston W. Rountree and Edith Elizabeth Folsom include Henrietta Elizabeth Rountree Joyce, James Wesley Rowntree, George F. Rowntree, Noel Lester Rountree, William F. Rountree of HH#187, Hardy Vickers Rowntree, and Harriett B. Rountree Hitch. That sibling framework is useful, but some details rely on FindAGrave and compiled material rather than direct vital records.

docs.title: Military Service
docs.text: William Washington Joyce, Henrietta's late husband, is identified in the current family narrative as a Confederate veteran of the 57th Georgia Infantry. Because he was not enumerated in the 1900 household, this should be presented as immediate family context rather than a 1900 household-member line item unless a later pass adds direct service-file citations.

docs.title: Connections to Other Barney Families
docs.text: HH#182 connects directly to HH#186 because George S. Joyce is Henrietta's son. It also connects to HH#187 because William F. Rountree is Henrietta's brother. Through Edith Folsom, the household belongs to the Folsom-Rountree-Joyce network that overlaps with Brooks, Lowndes, Berrien, and Colquitt counties.

docs.title: Family Narrative
docs.text:
William Wirt Burney was born 7 April 1869 in the Boston, Thomas County, Georgia area and died 19 March 1942 in Thomas County. His parentage is supported by the 1870 and 1880 census trail in the William James Burney and Rachel Foreman household and by his death record, which names his mother as Rachel Freeman or Foreman. The Foreman form is supported by the 1856 Glynn County marriage of William James Burney and Rachael Foreman.

The 1900 Barney entry appears to be a temporary Brooks County residence. William is alone in the household, listed as married for five years, and working as a day laborer. By 1910 he was back in Boston, Thomas County, widowed and working as a city policeman. He married Mary Gertrude Gaskins in Thomas County on 30 May 1912, and later census records place him in Boston through 1940.

The first wife remains only partly identified. FindAGrave lists Georgia E. Burney as a spouse, and the 1900 census indicates a marriage about 1895, but no direct marriage or death record for Georgia E. has been located in the current entry. Known children are Frank Burney, supported by FindAGrave, and Margaret "Peggy" Burney Willis, supported by census and Social Security Applications material from the second marriage.

docs.title: Connections to Other Barney Families
docs.text: This household is not a long-term Barney family cluster. Its strongest network is the Thomas County Burney-Gaskins family. The Barney appearance may reflect temporary farm labor, a short residence tied to the first marriage, or work away from the Boston household.

docs.title: Family Narrative
docs.text:
Robert Roberts was born in Georgia, probably around 1850-1852, and died 15 July 1925 in Coweta County, Georgia. The 1900 census gives the most specific birth detail, June 1850, while later censuses drift to younger ages. His wife was Frances Lee, supported by the 19 January 1874 Lee County marriage record and by Georgia death-record material naming spouse Francis Lee.

The census trail begins with a likely 1870 Greene County Robert Roberts, age 18, living as a farm laborer in the Robert McWhorter household. The 1880 census places Robert and Frances in Coweta County with early children Samuel, George, and an unnamed infant daughter. An 1890 Brooks County tax digest entry for Bob Roberts bridges the move from Coweta to Brooks. The 1900, 1910, and 1920 censuses place the family in Barney.

The Georgia death index records Bob Robert/Roberts dying in Coweta County in 1925, suggesting a return to the earlier Coweta County area. No burial or FindAGrave memorial has been located in the current online source set. A renewed FamilySearch pass also clarified the Will Roberts problem: a Georgia death record for Will Roberts, born in Coweta County and died in 1932, names parents Bob Roberts and Francis Lee, and a 1900 Coweta County census entry places William Roberts in a Robert/Frances household. This supports Will as part of the Coweta-linked Robert Roberts family cluster, but it does not close the adult trails for the children actually enumerated in HH#184 in 1900.

docs.title: Connections to Other Barney Families
docs.text: Robert Roberts may belong to the wider Roberts network that includes HH#189 Prince Roberts Jr. and the Prince Roberts Sr. family, but no direct kinship proof has been found. The older Peter Henry/Hulda Roberts connection in HH#164 has been downgraded because the refreshed marriage evidence names Hulda Williams.

docs.title: Research Notes
docs.text:
1. Robert's parents remain unidentified; both were reported as Georgia-born but never named in located records.
  2. Adult or death trails are still needed for Samuel, George, the unnamed 1880 daughter, Thomas, John, Frances, Amanda, Ruby Lee, Joseph, Benjamin, and the grandchildren Eugenia/Lugenia, Robert B., and Willie W.
  3. Elizabeth Cooper, niece in 1920, needs a Cooper-family connection record.
  4. Will Roberts is now supported as a Coweta-born child of Bob Roberts and Francis Lee through a Georgia death record and a matching 1900 Coweta census record, but he is not one of the children enumerated in the 1900 Barney household.
  5. Burial location remains unknown.
  6. Any Roberts connection to Prince Roberts Sr. should remain a lead only unless a direct source appears.

docs.text: The June 2026 pass exhausted available online primary/indexed sources for Robert's parents, burial, most child adult trails, Cooper connection, and possible Prince Roberts kinship. The authenticated FamilySearch re-pass closed only the Will Roberts note: Will's Georgia death record names Bob Roberts and Francis Lee, and a 1900 Coweta County census record places William with Robert and Frances. No safe source was found to name Robert's parents or to connect him directly to Prince Roberts Sr. The children and grandchildren listed above remain unclosed unless future courthouse, cemetery, church, probate, or local records surface.

docs.title: Family Narrative
docs.text:
Pollie/Polly Flournoy was born in Georgia in the mid-1850s and died 6 August 1923 in Brooks County, Georgia. Her 1900 birth month and year are August 1852, while the 1870 census age of 14 supports a birth year around 1856. The 1910 age of 43 is inconsistent with the 1870 and 1900 records.

Pollie was the daughter of John and Hannah Flournoy. The 1870 Brooks County census places her in John Flournoy's household with siblings including Wesley Flournoy of HH#179. Her death record names Hannah Flournoy as her mother.

The 1900 and 1910 census records report 17 children born and 14 living. Her husband was absent from the 1900, 1910, and 1920 households. Social Security Applications and Claims records for Mattie Ella Johnson and Marlver Stuard connect Pollie to spouse Marlver Stuard, but no marriage record has been located.

By 1920 Pollie was a washerwoman in Barney, living with daughter Ella Franklin and three Robertson grandchildren: Harvy, May Bell, and Ethel Lee. Those grandchildren show that one of Pollie's daughters had a Robertson/Roberson connection, but the parent and husband have not been identified.

docs.title: Connections to Other Barney Families
docs.text: Pollie is part of the same Flournoy sibling network as Wesley Flournoy (HH#179), Elsie Flournoy, Elizabeth Flournoy, and other Brooks County Flournoy descendants. The family ties into the Lightsey-Flournoy-Davis-Betts cluster already documented elsewhere in the encyclopedia.

docs.title: Research Notes
docs.text:
1. Marlver Stuard's marriage, death, and whereabouts need direct records; current support comes from Social Security Applications material.
  2. Adult or death trails are still needed for Mary, Arthur, Lula, Thomas, Cora, Earnest, Moses, John, and Nettie.
  3. The parent of Harvy, May Bell, and Ethel Lee Robertson is unresolved; search Robertson, Roberson, Robinson, and variant Brooks/Lowndes/Colquitt records.
  4. Pollie's father is supported by the 1870 family placement but not named in the available death-index entry; image-level death-certificate review is still needed.
  5. If secondary trees supply the Robertson or Stuard connection, label them as secondary until a marriage, death, census, SS, or court record confirms the link.

docs.title: Online exhaustion update
docs.text: The June 2026 pass did not locate a direct Pollie Flournoy-Marlver Stuard marriage, a death trail for Marlver, or a source naming the Robertson grandchildren's parent. Mattie Ella Johnson is supported by Social Security Applications material naming Marlver Stuard and Pollie Flournoy. The remaining children and Robertson connection are exhausted in online indexed sources and should be pursued through local marriage books, church/cemetery records, probate, and courthouse material.

docs.title: Children and Later Trails
docs.text: This section is reserved for later-life child evidence. No later spouse, death, burial, obituary, probate, separate household, or descendant-line identification has been added here yet from direct records.

docs.title: Family Narrative
docs.text:
The photographed George S. Joyce marker reads “AUG. 19, 1873” and “OCT. 2, 1912.” Find a Grave memorial 53836224 places it in Camp Ground Cemetery Mount Zion Church, Morven, Brooks County. The photograph was inspected on September 20, 2026. October 2 fits the illness/probate chronology below; it is a marker-supported death date, not a newly found contemporary death certificate or obituary. The stone's erection date and informant are unknown.

George S. Joyce was born about August 1873 in Georgia. The Barney News column dated September 27 and published September 28, 1912 reports: “We are glad to learn that Mr. George Joyce is improving from a severe illness.” Brooks County temporary letters dated October 7, 1912 already name G. S. Joyce as deceased and appoint G. W. Alderman to care for the estate; permanent letters followed on November 6. These records narrow the previously reported probate upper bound to October 7. They do not give an exact death date, and the newspaper's reporting date is distinct from its publication date. Illness notice, p. 7; temporary letters, p. 32.

George was the son of William Washington Joyce and Henrietta Elizabeth Rountree Joyce of HH#182. The 1880 census places him in their Morven, Brooks County household. He married Lucy Alice Alderman on 30 January 1893 in Brooks County. The 1900 census calls his wife "Susin," but the marriage record, 1910 census, and later widow records show the wife was Lucy Alice Alderman Joyce.

Lucy Alice Alderman Joyce was born 14 October 1874 and died in November 1939 in Brooks County. She was the daughter of Jonathan H. "Doc" Alderman and Amy A. McKinney, book ID 15-2-14, entry 7, in Aldermans in America. After George's death she remained widowed and appears as head of household in 1920 and 1930.

Seven children are documented across census records: William H., Venie/Vinnie A., James C., Letty/Lettie, Dorothy/Dotsie, G. B., and Clyde Joyce. The authenticated FamilySearch re-pass closed or narrowed most of these adult trails. William H. is supported as William Howard Joyce by the 1930, 1940, and 1950 Florida census trail, Florida 1945 state census, and Veterans Administration Master Index entry giving birth 9 October 1896 and death 10 October 1957. James C. is supported as James Clifford Joyce by 1930 Brooks County census continuity, Veterans Administration Master Index, World War I service-card material, and Find a Grave, with birth 7 April 1901 and death 3 June 1957. Vinnie A. has a Social Security Applications/NUMIDENT-style record as mother of W. T. Burton and spouse of Artie L. Burton. Dorothy/Dotsie has a Brooks County marriage to Finnons/Finnons F. Webb in December 1930. G. B. is supported as George B. Joyce by 1940/1950 Brooks County census entries, World War II draft registration, Georgia Death Index, and Find a Grave, with death 23 April 1966. Clyde has 1940/1950 Brooks County census entries, World War II draft/enlistment/discharge records, Georgia Death Index, and Find a Grave, with birth 25 November 1910 and death 22 August 1967. Letty/Lettie has SSDI/NUMIDENT, Georgia Death Index, and Find a Grave-style support under the Joyce surname, but the earlier Maxey newspaper item still lacks a matching marriage certificate in the online pass.

docs.title: Connections to Other Barney Families
docs.text: George links HH#186 to HH#182 through his mother Henrietta Rountree Joyce, and to HH#187 through his uncle William F. Rountree. Lucy Alderman links the household to the large Alderman network including HH#176, HH#178, HH#180, and HH#191.

docs.title: Research Notes
docs.text:
1. Seek contemporary death or burial evidence to corroborate the photographed marker's October 2, 1912 date. The September 27 illness report and October 7 temporary appointment fit that date but do not independently state the day of death.
  2. Venie/Vinnie needs a fuller adult/death trail beyond the W. T. Burton NUMIDENT link if available.
  3. Letty/Lettie Joyce has later death/burial support under the Joyce surname; the Maxey newspaper marriage notice should remain a separate lead unless a marriage certificate or matching later Maxey record is located.
  4. Lucy's death-date discrepancy between Aldermans in America and Georgia Death Index should be resolved by image-level death-certificate review.
  5. Aldermans in America is useful but secondary; use original records first where available.

docs.title: Online exhaustion update
docs.text: The June 2026 pass confirmed the core George-Lucy trail and probate/death-index framework. The authenticated FamilySearch re-pass added direct or near-direct adult trails for William Howard Joyce, James Clifford Joyce, Dorothy Joyce Webb, George B. Joyce, and Clyde Joyce, and a partial Vinnie A. Joyce Burton trail through a NUMIDENT child record. Letty's later death/burial trail appears under the Joyce surname; the Maxey marriage notice remains unclosed unless a certificate or later vital record is found. The September 2026 original-record review recovered temporary administration on October 7, 1912, earlier than the November 6 permanent appointment used in this prior summary. The later marker-photo check supplies October 2, 1912 as a marker-supported death date; a contemporary death notice or burial register remains sought. The earlier online-exhaustion claim is withdrawn.

docs.title: Military Service
docs.text: The military-service evidence in this household appears in the children's adult trails. William Howard Joyce is supported by Veterans Administration Master Index material. James Clifford Joyce is supported by Veterans Administration Master Index material plus World War I service-card material. Clyde Joyce is supported by World War II draft, Army enlistment, and discharge records. G. B. Joyce has World War II draft-registration support, but draft registration alone should not be treated as proof of service unless a service record is added.

docs.text: Previously researched household; probate chronology updated from originals on September 20, 2026. The earlier George-Lucy identity, marriage, census, family-network and child-trail research is retained. This bounded source review does not claim that every online source has been exhausted. Remaining gaps include contemporary corroboration of George's marker date and burial place, Vinnie's fuller death trail, and the unresolved Letty/Lettie-Maxey marriage-certificate question.

docs.title: Newspaper and Public-Record Trail
docs.text:
Original Brooks probate records inspected September 20, 2026 name H. V. Rountree temporary administrator of Wm. Rountree on January 16, 1928, and permanent administrator on March 5, 1928. The corresponding bond is also dated March 5. These records identify the administrator and estate; they do not state a family relationship.

A sale return by H. V. Rountree reports a courthouse sale on the first Tuesday in October 1928, with the cover filed October 8. It includes a town lot in Barney sold to J. I. Moody for $70. The sheet gives no street, lot number, dimensions or building description. Five other tracts—not expressly the Barney lot—refer to G. I. Tillman's survey plat in Brooks deeds Book 42, page 101. The administrator's deed and plat remain to be inspected before assigning a location or earlier title.

Probate citation correction: the formerly cited Ancestry records 8635:120698 and 8635:129982 are two filmings of the same Lowndes County testamentary appointment, page 177, dated October 3, 1927, for a deceased William F. Rountree, with Mrs. Minnie Rountree as executrix. They are not Brooks 1928 probate evidence and are excluded from support for this household. The independent census, death and family findings below are retained; this correction does not establish a relationship between the two estates.

docs.title: 1900 Census Household
docs.text: Name Relation Age Birthplace Occupation William Ramtree Head 46 Georgia Farmer Rilla Ramtree Boarder 10 Georgia Farmer Manda Roberts Boarder 55 Georgia Cook Joe Hendrey Boarder 24 Georgia Day Laborer Farm

docs.title: Children and Later Trails
docs.text: No child-tracking items are open for this page because the 1900 table lists no children in the household.

docs.title: Family Narrative
docs.text:
William F. Rountree was born about 1854 and died in 1928. Death-record evidence identifies his parents as Weston/Wesley Rountree and Edith Folsom, matching the Folsom-Rountree-Joyce network. He was the brother of Henrietta Elizabeth Rountree Joyce of HH#182 and uncle of George S. Joyce of HH#186.

The 1900 household is racially mixed: William is the White head, while Rilla Rountree, Manda Roberts, and Joe Hendrey are Black boarders. The earlier race line that treated William as Black was incorrect and has been removed. The boarders likely reflect post-emancipation labor, tenancy, or former-enslavement proximity, but no direct record proves a specific kinship or former enslaver relationship.

Rilla Rountree is the strongest boarder trail. The 1900 census lists her as a 92-year-old Black widow, mother of 10 children with 7 living. A 23 August 1904 Valdosta Times item reprinted from the Adel News describes Rilla Rountree as an "old-time slavery woman" past 100, living on J. H. Kennon's place, with son Si Rountree age 77. The ages are approximate but the name and family pattern support the same Rilla/Rolla Rountree cluster.

Manda Roberts and Joe Hendrey remain unresolved. Manda may belong to the Roberts family network connected to HH#184 or HH#189, and Joe's surname may connect to Hendry/Henry variants near HH#164, but both are leads only.

docs.title: Connections to Other Barney Families
docs.text: William connects to HH#182 as Henrietta's brother and to HH#186 as George Joyce's uncle. Rilla's surname may reflect historic ties to the Rountree family, but the current evidence does not identify her enslaver, parents, spouse, or exact children beyond the newspaper reference to son Si/Simeon.

docs.title: Research Notes
docs.text:
1. William's death record has now been located directly and should be cited for his death date and parentage.
  2. Rilla's 1884 Brooks County marriage record has been located, but her full child list, especially Si/Simeon Rountree, still needs reconstruction.
  3. Manda Roberts needs an adult trail before connecting her to Prince Roberts, Robert Roberts, or any other Roberts household; no safe continuation was found.
  4. Joe Hendrey/Hendry has a likely same-district continuation in 1920 and 1930 Brooks County, but no marriage/death record was found to connect him to Peter Henry/Hendry.
  5. Any former-enslavement relationship is historical context only unless supported by probate, labor, Freedmen's Bureau, estate, deed, or other direct records.

docs.title: Online exhaustion update
docs.text: The earlier claim that William's probate trail was closed online is withdrawn. Newly inspected Brooks appointments and the 1928 sale return provide further estate evidence; the administrator's deed, cited plat and estate-to-household details still need direct comparison. Rilla has a new Brooks County marriage hit, and Joe Hendrey/Hendry has 1920 and 1930 Brooks County continuations, but neither trail proves kinship to William Rountree or to the Henry/Hendry network. Manda Roberts remains a 1900-only boarder for this entry after targeted Ancestry searches; the similarly named 1880 Chattanooga result is not safe to attach. Former-enslavement or family-labor relationships remain unproved and should be pursued through estate, deed, probate, Freedmen's Bureau, church, and cemetery sources.

docs.text: Active probate and title followup. The independently researched identity, death and cemetery findings are retained, while the two misassigned Lowndes probate citations are excluded. Brooks appointments and a sale return are now documented, but the Barney lot's bounds and the estate's relationship details remain open. Rilla and Joe have additional online leads; Manda and the boarder relationship questions remain unresolved.

docs.title: Family Narrative
docs.text:
Silas George Graham was born about 1871 in North Carolina and died in July 1957. The earliest secure record is the 1880 Whiteville, Columbus County, North Carolina census, where Silas is age 9 in the household of maternal grandfather Ned Baldwin, with parents Isaac Graham and Helen Baldwin present. By 1900 Silas had migrated to Brooks County, Georgia, where he was farming with wife Hannah and four children.

Hannah Baker Graham was born about 1876, with birthplace varying between Florida and Georgia in census records. Social Security Applications and obituary-index material identify her as Hannah Baker, spouse of Silas. No marriage certificate has been located.

The family moved from Brooks County to Valdosta, Lowndes County by 1920. Silas appears there in the 1920, 1930, 1940, and 1950 censuses. By 1950 Hannah was absent and Silas had wife Lorena. The child list spans Eddie/Johnny, Nellie, John, Angie/Arness, Alexander/Amos, Annie Mae, Emanuel, Mary, Willie F., Leola, Blanche, and Jesse/Jessie. Leola's 1934 death record names Silas Graham and Hannah Baker; Blanche's married surname Wilson is supported by Social Security Applications material.

The possible 1870 Isaac Graham in Marion County, South Carolina is geographically plausible because Marion County borders Columbus County, North Carolina, but it is not proved to be Silas's father.

docs.title: Connections to Other Barney Families
docs.text: Silas's migration creates a North Carolina-to-Brooks-to-Lowndes County trail. The Baker surname of Hannah may connect to other Baker families in Brooks County, but no direct link to Rubin Baker or other Barney Bakers has been proved.

docs.title: Research Notes
docs.text:
1. Silas and Hannah's marriage record is still needed.
  2. Hannah's death date and burial need direct records; she is present in 1940 and absent by 1950.
  3. Adult/death trails are needed for Eddie/Johnny, Nellie, John, Angie/Arness, Alexander/Amos, Annie Mae, Emanuel, Mary, Willie F., Jesse, and Blanche Wilson.
  4. The 1870 Isaac Graham candidate in Marion County, South Carolina should remain tentative until tied to Helen Baldwin or Silas by a direct record.
  5. Lorena's maiden name and marriage to Silas need direct proof.

docs.title: Online exhaustion update
docs.text: The June 2026 pass exhausted available online indexed sources for the Silas-Hannah marriage, Hannah's death/burial, Lorena's maiden name/marriage, and the remaining child adult trails. Leola and Blanche have parent-naming support, and the long census trail is strong, but the listed gaps remain open because no safe online primary record was found.

docs.title: Family Narrative
docs.text:
The head of HH#189 is best identified as Prince Roberts Jr., born about February 1874 in Georgia, son of Prince Roberts Sr. and Lucy Roberts. He appears as Prince Roberts Jr. in the 1880 Brooks County census, as Frank Roberts in the 1900 Barney census, as Prince Roberts in the 1910 and 1920 Barney censuses, as a badly indexed Prince/Pike Roberts in 1930 Hickory Head, and as Prince Roberts in the 1950 Valdosta census. No death record has been located.

The 6 August 1899 Brooks County marriage record names Prince Roberts and Janie Flournoy. This primary record is the strongest proof that the 1900 "Frank" is Prince. The 1900 household has wife Jane and infant son Isaac, consistent with the August 1899 marriage. A June 14, 2026 Ancestry search result also surfaced an Ancestry tree entry for "Prince Frank Roberts" with spouse Hannah Jane "Janie" Flournoy and parents Prince Roberts and Lucy Roberts; that tree is secondary and should not be treated as proof by itself.

Janie Flournoy Roberts was born about 1878-1883 in Georgia and died in December 1957 in Dade County, Florida. Her pre-marriage trail includes a likely 1900 Valdosta census entry as Jane Flornouy, laundress and boarder, and a 1908 Valdosta city directory entry for Janie Flournoy. Her parents remain unresolved; she does not fit cleanly as a child of John and Hannah Flournoy because her reported mother's birthplace is Georgia, while Hannah's is Virginia.

Children documented across the census trail include Isaac/Governor, Mary M., James F., Willie E./Will Everett, Simeon/Simon, and Bessie Mae Roberts. The authenticated FamilySearch re-pass closed the infant Isaac/Governor trail: he appears as Isaac Govoner Roberts in a Georgia death record, died 21 January 1929 in Barney, Brooks County, with parents Janie Flournoy and Prince Roberts and spouse Lola Clark. Adult/death trails for Mary M., James F., Willie E./Will Everett, Simeon/Simon, and Bessie Mae Roberts remain incomplete in the entry.

docs.title: Connections to Other Barney Families
docs.text: Prince Roberts Jr. connects to the Prince Roberts Sr. family, which also includes Ike Roberts (HH#61) and Louise Roberts Stroud. His possible relationship to Robert Roberts (HH#184) remains unproved. Janie's Flournoy surname may connect to the HH#179/HH#185 Flournoy network, but her exact parents have not been identified.
